query_text: A wheel-spoke assembly, comprising: a rod member, possessing a central portion and a pair of end portions, wherein the end portions are joined to opposing extremities of the central portion, each end portion presents an outer circumferential face, and the outer circumferential faces each carry a grip-increasing feature; and a pair of sleeve pieces, each formed about at least part of the grip-increasing features through an overmolding operation, wherein the sleeve pieces each present an exterior circumferential face oriented away from the rod member, and the exterior circumferential faces each carry a coupling feature.

A guard assembly for a road vehicle's roadwheel, the roadwheel including a hub flange, a plurality of radial members, and a resilient ring, the guard assembly comprising: a mounting member affixed to the hub flange and/or the radial members; and a shielding member carried by the mounting member, wherein at least a portion of the shielding member covers an exterior face of the resilient ring.

A collapsible spare tire apparatus comprising: a half-disc body and a half-disc extension hinged together at one pair of adjacent extremities by a pivot pin, which establish a stowed configuration wherein the extension lies folded against the body and a deployed configuration wherein the extension projects outward so that the body and extension jointly constitute a complete wheel rim; a curved outer surface of both the body and the extension being wrapped with a metal band to enhance load-bearing capacity, and an elastomeric strip secured around an exterior of said metal band to provide grip and dampen vibration during operation; the body including a central aperture bounded by an internally threaded receiving sleeve configured to mount the body to a vehicle; a rotary cam sleeve of predetermined profile seated over said receiving sleeve and serving as the base of a lobe, said cam sleeve being joined to the body by a retaining collar permitting unlimited rotation of the cam sleeve while allowing the lobe to lie horizontally in the stowed configuration between an inner edge of the extension and a shoulder projecting from the body adjacent the pivot pin, referenced to a vertical axis passing through the hub of the body; a first anchor point located on an opposite side of the shoulder receiving one end of a tension coil, the opposite end of said coil being attached to a second anchor point at a free end of the extension to hold the extension horizontal when at rest; a guide pin fixed to the body on a side opposite the pivot pin, referenced to the same vertical axis, cooperating with a vertical channel formed at the free end of the extension beneath the second anchor point to guide and constrain travel of the extension during transition from the stowed to the deployed configuration; and wherein rotation of the cam sleeve in a counterclockwise direction drives the lobe outwardly against the extension to move it from the stowed to the deployed configuration, the body and extension then forming the complete rim, a locking catch at a distal end of the lobe preventing displacement of said lobe, and the apparatus being characterized in that a reduced-diameter receiving sleeve is coupled to a mating externally threaded hub provided on the vehicle wheel and secured by a central hex bolt operated through a tightening grip, and wherein the metal band and the elastomeric strip are fastened to one another by anchor-head fasteners and nuts.

A thermal barrier assembly comprising: a first protective sheet and a second protective sheet, each sheet possessing a pair of perimeter borders, wherein the perimeter borders of the first sheet and the perimeter borders of the second sheet are generally coincident and are joined together to define assembly boundaries; and wherein the first protective sheet is constituted by two or more sections, each section presenting an interior margin, the interior margins of the sections being configured to shift in relation to one another.

A steering knuckle assembly for an automobile, the assembly comprising: a hub flange to which a road wheel may be secured; a torque coupling unit having a coupling casing and a coupling actuator member linked to the coupling casing, wherein the coupling casing is positioned concentric with the hub flange and is non-rotatably joined to the hub flange; and a knuckle on which the hub flange and the coupling casing are carried non-rotatably by way of a bearing, wherein the bearing has an outer race affixed to the knuckle, an inner race split along an axial direction, and a plurality of rollers disposed radially between the inner race and the outer race, wherein the split inner race includes a first inner race segment and a second inner race segment, wherein the first inner race segment is formed as one piece with the hub flange, and the second inner race segment is formed as one piece with the coupling casing, and wherein the coupling casing is adapted to be axially secured to the hub flange such that an axial spacing between the first and second inner race segments is adjustable.

A tire for a vehicle, comprising: a crown region extending circumferentially and shaped as a ring; a pair of flank regions positioned on opposite sides of the crown region; a pair of bead regions located radially inward of the flank regions; a ply structure extending between the bead regions; and a set of belt plies arranged radially outward of the ply structure within the crown region; the crown region being formed as a two-layer assembly having a subtread layer positioned radially outward of the belt plies and an outermost tread layer positioned radially outward of the subtread layer and forming a ground-engaging surface of the crown region; the outermost tread layer including a compound comprising from 60 to 90 parts by weight of precipitated silica per 100 parts by weight of a rubber blend containing 15 to 30 weight percent of natural rubber, 40 to 70 weight percent of a chain-end-functionalized styrene-butadiene rubber exhibiting a vinyl content of 35 to 45 percent, and 15 to 30 weight percent of a functionalized butadiene rubber in which an active chain end of a conjugated diene polymer is capped with at least one group selected from a hydrocarbyloxysilane compound and a polyorganosiloxane, the three rubbers together totaling 100 weight percent; a hardness Hu of a subtread rubber at 20 degrees Celsius and a hardness Hc of the outermost tread rubber at 20 degrees Celsius satisfying Hu being greater than Hc; the hardness Hc lying between 63 and 67 inclusive; and a difference between Hu and Hc being at least 10.

An inflatable tyre comprising: a tread section; a belt ply assembly in which reinforcement filaments are single-strand filaments disposed transversely across the tyre width at a density of no fewer than 50 filaments per 5 cm, measured along a cross-section of the belt ply assembly taken in the radial direction of the tyre; and a cross-sectional width Wt (mm) and an overall diameter Dt (mm) of the tyre, mounted on a standard wheel rim and inflated to 250 kPa, that together satisfy the following relation: 1500≤(Dt² × π/4)/Wt.

A tire comprising: a tread region; and a reinforcing ply structure disposed beneath the tread region and employing single-strand filaments as reinforcing elements, wherein a count g of the single-strand filaments per 5 cm measured along the axial direction in a radial section of the reinforcing ply structure, together with a cross-sectional axial dimension Wt (mm) of the tire mounted on a standard wheel rim and inflated to 250 kPa, fulfills the following relations: g/(0.31 Wt+14.35)>1; and g/(0.31 Wt+56.45)<1.

A tyre for a motor vehicle, comprising: at least two belt layers whose cords intersect at a inclination, the cords in each layer being oriented in a common direction, lying alongside one another with separation, and enclosed by elastomeric compound; wherein a first layer among the at least two belt layers incorporates cords configured as steel filaments each possessing a thickness D between 0.33 mm and 0.37 mm and a breaking strength between 3080 N/mm2 and 4190 N/mm2; the steel filaments of the first layer each exhibiting a twist count of essentially zero turns over a span equal to 200 times the filament thickness; and the steel filaments of the first layer being disposed at a density of 90 to 130 ends per decimetre.

A pneumatic tyre for a motor vehicle, comprising: a plurality of belt layers whose cords cross one another at an inclination; wherein the cords in each belt layer extend in mutually spaced, substantially aligned fashion and are encapsulated in elastomeric compound; wherein every belt layer of the tyre incorporates cords formed from steel filaments each exhibiting a diameter of 0.33 mm to 0.37 mm and a tensile strength of 3080 N/mm2 to 4190 N/mm2; and wherein each steel filament possesses a twist count of zero turns over a measured length equal to 200 times the filament diameter.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a crown reinforcement arranged in a tread region, the crown reinforcement including at least one reinforcing ply; the at least one reinforcing ply incorporating a monofilament steel element exhibiting a minor dimension SD and a major dimension LD, wherein a quotient SD/LD is less than 1.00; and an elastomeric coating enveloping the monofilament element, the monofilament element being positioned such that the minor dimension SD extends along a thickness axis of the reinforcing ply; and the elastomeric coating possessing a complex modulus E* between 7 MPa and 20 MPa when measured at 70° C., an initial strain of 10%, a dynamic strain amplitude of plus or minus 1.0%, and a frequency of 10 Hz.

An automotive wheel arrangement, comprising: a hollow cylindrical rim structure; a first shroud member; and a second shroud member, wherein the rim structure includes at least a disc portion disposed along an axial extent of the rim structure, wherein the first shroud member is positioned on a first face of the disc portion and the second shroud member is positioned on an opposing second face of the disc portion along the axial extent of the rim structure, wherein the rim structure is made of a first substance, wherein the first shroud member and the second shroud member are made of a second substance, wherein the first substance is distinct from the second substance, and wherein the first shroud member and the second shroud member have dissimilar configurations relative to one another.

A vehicle wheel arrangement, comprising: a first wheel unit, including a first hollow cylindrical hub body; a first flange panel; and a second flange panel, wherein the first hollow hub body includes at least a first disc member positioned along an axis of the first hollow hub body, wherein the first flange panel is disposed on a first face of the first disc member and the second flange panel is disposed on a second face of the first disc member along the axis of the first hollow hub body, wherein the first hollow hub body is made of a first substance, wherein the first flange panel and the second flange panel are made of a second substance, wherein the first substance is distinct from the second substance, and wherein the first flange panel and the second flange panel are shaped dissimilarly from one another; and a second wheel unit, including a second hollow cylindrical hub body; a third flange panel; and a fourth flange panel, wherein the second hollow hub body includes at least a second disc member positioned along an axis of the second hollow hub body, wherein the third flange panel is disposed on a third face of the second disc member and the fourth flange panel is disposed on a fourth face of the second disc member along the axis of the second hollow hub body, wherein the second hollow hub body is made of the first substance, wherein the third flange panel and the fourth flange panel are made of the second substance, and wherein the third flange panel and the fourth flange panel are shaped dissimilarly from one another, and wherein the first wheel unit is mountable on a port side of the vehicle and the second wheel unit is mountable on a starboard side of the vehicle relative to a direction of travel of the vehicle.

A process for producing a vehicular wheel structure, the process comprising: supplying a hollow tubular barrel possessing at least one disc portion situated along a longitudinal axis of the barrel, wherein the barrel is composed of a first substance; furnishing a first shield member made of a second substance and a second shield member made of the second substance; and positioning the first shield member on a first face of the disc portion while positioning the second shield member on a second face of the disc portion along the longitudinal axis of the barrel, wherein the first substance is different from the second substance, and wherein the first shield member and the second shield member are shaped dissimilarly from one another.

A rotatable hub assembly for a vehicle road wheel, comprising: a hub housing having a first axial end and a second axial end; a flange region of the hub housing situated between the first and second axial ends and configured to receive a road wheel; a bore defined through the hub housing; an inner face of the hub housing surrounding the bore; an outer face of the hub housing facing away from the inner face; a conduit having an inner aperture formed in the inner face of the hub housing, the inner aperture positioned axially beyond the first axial end of the hub housing; and an outer aperture of the conduit formed in the outer face of the hub housing, the outer aperture positioned between the flange region and the second axial end of the hub housing.

A process for producing a hub for a vehicle wheel, the process comprising: molding a hub blank possessing an axial bore and a wall encircling the bore, wherein molding involves creating a partial channel within the wall of the blank; and machining an aperture through the wall so as to finish the channel.

A hub assembly for a vehicle road wheel, the hub assembly comprising: a hub housing; a rim-securing section of the hub housing configured to carry a road wheel; a conduit having an outer aperture in the hub housing and an inner aperture in the hub housing; and a shield of the hub housing arranged to prevent the road wheel from engaging the outer aperture.

A deceleration-type rolling device, comprising: a rolling assembly having a hub holder, a spindle extending through the hub holder, and a rotor turning around the spindle, the hub holder defining an aperture through which the spindle is inserted, the spindle having a flattened-profile segment at one terminal, the rotor including a hub body whose perimeter is joined to an outer tire, the hub body defining a shaft opening through its midpoint, the spindle being received within the shaft opening, the rotor being arranged to rotate freely about the spindle, a plurality of stoppers arranged on one face of the hub body proximate a border thereof in a radial pattern, the stoppers being arranged to revolve together with the rotor; and a braking assembly comprising a mounting block and a slider, the mounting block including a securing hole and a guide channel, the securing hole fitted around and affixed to the flattened-profile segment of the spindle, the mounting block positioned on one side of the rotor, the slider movably seated within the guide channel, the slider including a slider shank, the slider shank having a resilient section coupled to a leading end thereof, the resilient section having a catch portion coupled to a leading end thereof; wherein, when the rotor descends a slope, the guide channel inclines downward at an incline angle and the slider travels along the guide channel under gravitational pull, such that the catch portion extends beyond an exterior of the guide channel to obstruct a travel path of the stoppers, whereby the stoppers pass over and strike the catch portion successively, such that cooperation between the catch portion and a spring force of the resilient section produces a deceleration effect.

A velocity-moderating wheel apparatus, comprising: a hub assembly having a support housing, a spindle extending through the support housing, and a rotor configured to turn freely about the spindle, the support housing including an aperture through which the spindle extends, the rotor including a spoke carrier whose perimeter is coupled to a tire, the spoke carrier including a central opening through its middle, the spindle extending through the central opening, the rotor being arranged to rotate independently about the spindle, a plurality of resilient catches arranged on one face of the spoke carrier proximate a rim thereof in a radial pattern, the resilient catches being arranged to revolve together with the rotor; and a deceleration mechanism comprising a mounting block and a slide element, the mounting block positioned beside the rotor, the mounting block including a guide channel, the slide element movably received in the guide channel, the slide element including a stop surface at a leading end thereof; wherein, when the rotor descends a slope, the guide channel tilts downward at a slope angle and the slide element travels along the guide channel under gravitational force, such that the stop surface projects beyond an exterior of the guide channel to obstruct a path of the resilient catches, whereby the stop surface impedes the resilient catches through elastic flexing and rebound of the resilient catches, such that the resilient catches pass over and strike the stop surface sequentially before returning to shape, thereby reducing speed.

A temporary replacement apparatus for a trailer tire comprising: an elongated support having a proximal extremity and a distal extremity; a fastening assembly having a fixed jaw affixed to said elongated support adjacent said proximal extremity, said fastening assembly having a adjustable jaw displaceable toward and away from said fixed jaw, said fastening assembly being adapted to grip a suspension leaf of a trailer between said fixed jaw and said adjustable jaw such that said elongated support projects from the trailer adjacent to and in alignment with a trailer axle; and a roller pivotally mounted to said elongated support adjacent said distal extremity.

A temporary replacement apparatus for a trailer tire, the apparatus comprising: a beam having an entry extremity and a terminal extremity, the beam extending lengthwise between the entry extremity and the terminal extremity, the beam having an upper face and a lower face, each of the upper face and the lower face spanning from the entry extremity to the terminal extremity, the beam being fabricated from a hollow rectangular-section conduit; a securing assembly including a base plate, a pair of U-shaped fasteners, and a set of retaining collars, the base plate being disposed against the lower face of the beam adjacent the entry extremity, each U-shaped fastener including two externally screw-threaded legs passing through the upper face and the lower face of the beam, each U-shaped fastener together with the upper face of the beam bounding a respective opening of a pair of openings, the securing assembly being arranged to accept a suspension leaf of a trailer through the pair of openings so that the suspension leaf projects sideways from the beam, each retaining collar being screwed onto a respective threaded leg of a respective U-shaped fastener and bearing against the base plate, the securing assembly being adapted to grip the suspension leaf when the suspension leaf passes through the pair of openings such that the beam projects away from the trailer adjacent to and in parallel with an axle of the trailer; a spindle unit including a support section and a rolling section, the rolling section being pivotally joined to the support section, the support section being affixed to the lower face of the beam, the rolling section projecting away from the terminal extremity of the beam such that the rolling section is turnable about a rotation line parallel to a central lengthwise line of the beam; and a tire mounted on the rolling section of the spindle unit.

A rubber mixture suitable for tyre tread formulations, the mixture including: one hundred parts per hundred rubber of at least one diene-based elastomer; at least 0.1 phr of at least one reversibly bonding crosslinker having the general structure A-B-C, in which A denotes at least one moiety able to form a covalent link with the elastomer, B, which may be absent, denotes an inert organic linker of valence two or greater joined to both A and C, and C denotes at least one polydentate organic chelating group able to reversibly coordinate at least one metal cation; at least 0.1 phr of at least one salt of said metal cation; at least 0.1 phr of at least one reinforcing filler; and at least 0.1 phr of at least one curing agent.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, comprising: a pair of annular bead reinforcements; a casing ply structure spanning between the bead reinforcements; and a reinforcing belt arrangement positioned radially outward of the casing ply structure, an outside diameter OD (mm) of the covering falling within a span 200≤OD≤660, an overall cross-sectional width SW (mm) falling within a span 100≤SW≤400, the casing ply structure being constituted by two stacked plies each formed by enveloping organic fiber filaments with rubber skim compounds, the organic fiber filaments of the two plies being oriented at filament inclinations of 80 degrees or more and 100 degrees or less relative to a circumferential direction of the covering, and a breaking strength Tcs (N/50 mm) per 50 mm width of each of the two plies falling within a span 17≤Tcs/OD≤120 relative to the outside diameter OD (mm).

A pneumatic vehicle tyre, comprising: a pair of annular bead reinforcements; and a casing ply structure spanning between the bead reinforcements; wherein an outside diameter OD (mm) lies within 200≤OD≤660, an overall section breadth SW (mm) lies within 100≤SW≤400, the casing ply structure consists of two stacked casing plies each formed by embedding organic fibre cords in elastomeric coating compound, the organic fibre cords of the two casing plies exhibit cord inclination angles of opposite algebraic sign within a band of 45 degrees or more and 70 degrees or less relative to a tyre circumferential direction, and a tensile strength Tcs (N/50 mm) per 50 mm width of each of the two casing plies satisfies 17≤Tcs/OD≤120 relative to the outside diameter OD (mm).

A reinforcement sheet comprising: a set of parallel metal cords running lengthwise and spaced apart across its width at a spacing pitch p in mm, the cords being bedded within a rubber matrix formed from at least one elastomer, a reinforcing particulate, and a vulcanization package; each cord presenting, in a cross-section taken normal to its lengthwise direction, an outline fitting within a rectangle of width W and thickness T, and exhibiting a tensile rupture strength R_F in MPa determined per ISO 6892:1984; the sheet exhibiting a rupture load per unit width in N/mm of R_n; wherein the spacing pitch satisfies p ≥ 0.8·(R_F/R_n)·(a−1+π/4)·T², with a = W/T and 1/a lying between 0.35 and 0.75; and wherein the parallel cords are arranged transversely to the lengthwise direction.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tire, comprising: a casing formed of radially oriented cord layers extending in a toroidal path between two bead regions; wherein a section width SW of the tire is below 165 mm and a quotient of SW divided by an overall diameter OD of the tire is no greater than 0.26; the tire includes a tread region whose ground-contacting face bears one or more rib-like land regions; each land region is provided with a multiplicity of lateral incisions oriented along the axial direction of the tire; adjacent lateral incisions are spaced apart in the circumferential direction by a distance of 3 mm to 10 mm; and each lateral incision includes an enlarged-width section adjacent its floor, the width of the incision at the floor exceeding its width at the ground-contacting face.

A radial-ply passenger car pneumatic tyre, comprising: a casing formed of radially oriented reinforcing filaments extending in a toroidal path between a pair of bead regions; wherein a section width SW of said tyre is at least 165 mm and said section width SW (mm) and an overall diameter OD (mm) of said tyre fulfil the expression OD (mm)≥2.135×SW (mm)+282.3; said tyre includes a tread region whose ground-contacting face bears one or more rib regions, each rib region being provided with a plurality of lateral incisions extending across the tyre width; a circumferential spacing between adjacent lateral incisions of said plurality is from 3 mm to 10 mm; and each lateral incision exhibits an enlarged cavity at its floor side whose slit thickness exceeds that at the ground-contacting face side.

A radial-ply passenger car tyre, comprising: a casing formed of radially oriented reinforcing filaments extending in a toroidal path between a pair of bead regions; wherein a section width SW (mm) and an external diameter OD (mm) of the tyre fulfil the condition OD (mm)≥−0.0187×SW (mm) 2 +9.15×SW (mm)−380; the tyre includes a tread region whose ground-contacting face presents at least one rib-like block; the block is provided with a multiplicity of lateral slits running across the tyre width; the circumferential spacing between adjacent lateral slits is from 3 mm to 10 mm; and each lateral slit exhibits an enlarged section at its floor, the slit being wider at the floor than at the ground-contacting face.

A process for fabricating a pneumatic tire, the process comprising: positioning a first carcass layer having a first breadth; placing a second carcass layer over the first carcass layer, the second carcass layer having a second breadth smaller than the first breadth; placing a third carcass layer over the second carcass layer, the third carcass layer having a third breadth exceeding the first breadth; setting a first bead core at a first site over the third carcass layer; setting a second bead core at a second site over the third carcass layer; disposing a first sidewall reinforcing strip at a third site over the third carcass layer, the third site lying between the first site and the second site; disposing a second sidewall reinforcing strip at a fourth site over the third carcass layer, the fourth site lying between the third site and the second site; folding the first, second, and third carcass layers about the first bead core such that the first carcass layer has a first upturned flap of a first elevation, the second carcass layer has a second upturned flap of a second elevation less than the first elevation, and the third carcass layer has a third upturned flap of a third elevation greater than the first elevation, with the third upturned flap abutting the first sidewall reinforcing strip; and folding the first, second, and third carcass layers about the second bead core such that the first carcass layer has a fourth upturned flap of a fourth elevation, the second carcass layer has a fifth upturned flap of a fifth elevation less than the fourth elevation, and the third carcass layer has a sixth upturned flap of a sixth elevation greater than the fourth elevation, with the sixth upturned flap abutting the second sidewall reinforcing strip.

A process for fabricating a pneumatic tyre, the process comprising: supplying a pair of annular beads, one being a first annular bead and the other a second annular bead; supplying at least three carcass layers, namely a first carcass layer, a second carcass layer, and a third carcass layer; routing each of the at least three carcass layers between the first annular bead and the second annular bead, comprising: directing the first carcass layer downward, axially inward of the first annular bead, and folding the first carcass layer about the first annular bead so that the first carcass layer has a first upturned flap extending upward, axially outward of the first annular bead, the first upturned flap terminating at a first flap extremity; directing the second carcass layer downward, axially inward of the first annular bead and axially outward of the first carcass layer, and folding the second carcass layer about the first annular bead so that the second carcass layer has a second upturned flap extending upward, axially outward of the first annular bead and axially inward of the first upturned flap, the second upturned flap terminating at a second flap extremity positioned radially lower than the first flap extremity; and directing the third carcass layer downward, axially inward of the first annular bead and axially outward of the second carcass layer, and folding the third carcass layer about the first annular bead so that the third carcass layer has a third upturned flap extending upward, axially outward of the first annular bead and axially inward of the second upturned flap, the third upturned flap terminating at a third flap extremity positioned radially higher than the first flap extremity; disposing a circumferential reinforcing band radially outward of the at least three carcass layers, such that the reinforcing band extends axially across a portion of the at least three carcass layers; disposing a circumferential tread radially outward of the reinforcing band; positioning a first stiffening insert such that a first end thereof lies axially inward of a first end of the reinforcing band and radially inward of the reinforcing band, and such that a second end thereof lies axially outward of the first end of the reinforcing band and radially lower than the third flap extremity; positioning a second stiffening insert such that a first end thereof lies axially inward of a second end of the reinforcing band and radially inward of the reinforcing band, and such that a second end thereof lies axially outward of the second end of the reinforcing band; extending a first sidewall between the first annular bead and the circumferential tread; and extending a second sidewall between the second annular bead and the circumferential tread.

A process for manufacturing a pneumatic tyre, the process comprising: supplying a pair of annular bead cores; laying a plurality of carcass layers spanning between the pair of bead cores, the plurality of carcass layers including at least a first carcass layer and a second carcass layer; folding the first carcass layer about each of the pair of bead cores to form a first pair of flipped segments having a first elevation; folding the second carcass layer about each of the pair of bead cores to form a second pair of flipped segments having a second elevation exceeding the first elevation, each of the second pair of flipped segments lying axially inward of a corresponding one of the first flipped segments; positioning a circumferential reinforcing layer radially outward of the plurality of carcass layers; disposing a tread band radially outward of the circumferential reinforcing layer; arranging a first reinforcing insert having a first extremity radially inward of the circumferential reinforcing layer and a second extremity situated radially beneath an end of one of the first flipped segments; arranging a second reinforcing insert having a first extremity radially inward of the circumferential reinforcing layer and a second extremity situated radially beneath an end of one of the first flipped segments; and extending a pair of sidewalls between the pair of bead cores and the tread band.

An acoustic damper apparatus comprising: a pliable panel-like substrate; a plate-shaped mesh layer; and an absorptive filler enclosed within a sealed chamber defined between the pliable panel-like substrate and the plate-shaped mesh layer, the absorptive filler running lengthwise along an elongated axis of the acoustic damper apparatus.

A matched assembly of vehicle rims, comprising: a pair of rims mounted on one shared axle, each rim bearing a set of supplementary sculpted protrusions on its outward-facing surface, such that the paired rims exhibit higher load-bearing rigidity than the rims mounted on a different axle of the same vehicle.

A technique for reinforcing the front surface of a pair of vehicle wheels mounted on one axle while preserving an essentially matching design across the front surfaces of every axle, the technique comprising: employing computer-controlled machining or die-fabrication processes to form auxiliary spokes positioned next to and/or joined with the current spokes of the wheels on the opposite axle, which bears reduced loading; and

query_text: A rim disc arrangement comprising: a radial member which is a thin hollow panel and which bounds an interior cavity therein; a joining element projecting from an exterior face of the radial member; and a hub body having a housing cavity and at least one through channel communicating with the housing cavity, wherein the housing cavity and the at least one through channel jointly traverse the hub body, and wherein the at least one through channel is in fluid communication with the interior cavity.

A wheel-center cover apparatus comprising: a unitary shell body including (i) a cylindrical wall of ring-shaped section, a mounting extremity, and a terminal extremity located opposite the mounting extremity, (ii) a closing lid bordering and extending entirely over the terminal extremity, and (iii) a rim collar bordering and partially encircling the mounting extremity; the rim collar having an exterior collar face oriented toward the terminal extremity and, situated opposite the exterior collar face, an interior collar face delimiting a ring-shaped groove.

A vehicle road wheel configured to turn about a central axis, the wheel including: a receptacle zone for accommodating a rotor of a braking system, the receptacle zone encircling the central axis; a peripheral hoop having a recessed channel, the hoop encircling both the receptacle zone and the central axis, the recessed channel projecting from the hoop inward toward the central axis; and at least one arm joined to the peripheral hoop, the at least one arm located on an exterior side of the wheel and extending at least partly along a direction transverse to the central axis; wherein, measured along the central axis, the receptacle zone lies nearer the exterior side than the recessed channel does.

A rim assembly adapted for operation under reduced inflation pressure, the rim assembly comprising: a hub-engaging member having a joining face; a outer shell portion abutting the hub-engaging member along the joining face; and a retention protrusion with locking profile formed on at least the hub-engaging member, the locking profile including a rim edge having an inward-facing edge surface and a tire seat disposed between the retention protrusion and the rim edge.

A low-pressure-capable wheel assembly comprising: a hub portion having a joining face; a rim portion abutting the hub portion along said joining face; and a tire-retaining shoulder featuring locking profile contours on each of the hub portion and the rim portion.

A hub assembly for an automotive vehicle, comprising: a rotatable hub body, a stationary carrier casing, and an anti-friction bearing that supports the hub body for rotation relative to the carrier casing; wherein the bearing includes at least one circumferential array of balls or rollers running on a raceway formed in an inner race that is a discrete piece separate from the hub body and secured to the hub body; wherein the hub body defines a central bore provided with an internal spline arrangement through which the hub body may be coupled against relative rotation to a driveshaft stub carrying an external spline; wherein the internal spline arrangement comprises a first spline section, a second spline section, and a smooth unsplined section situated axially between and separating the two spline sections; and wherein the smooth unsplined section is positioned so as to lie radially across from an axial end face of the inner race located on the bearing-facing side.

A half-shaft transmission arrangement comprising: a hub bearing mounted within a knuckle; a retaining collar of annular form having an exterior rim fixed to an outer race of the hub bearing; a bellows cover having a wide flange at one terminus fitted to an interior surface of the retaining collar; and a sealing module positioned between a narrow neck at the opposite terminus of the bellows cover and a power transmission shaft, the sealing module inhibiting rotation of the bellows cover and blocking entry of contaminants.

A protective cover apparatus for shielding wheel fasteners and tool sockets, comprising: a pliable jacket formed to delimit an elongated sleeve possessing a cylindrical sidewall running from a closed terminus to an unobstructed terminus; wherein the elongated sleeve includes an inner cavity sized to accommodate a driving implement possessing a fastener recess, the fastener recess situated at the closed terminus of the elongated sleeve; wherein the elongated sleeve includes an outer face at the closed terminus adapted to mate against a wheel bolt; and wherein the cylindrical sidewall is resilient and adapted to deform into the fastener recess so as to be interposed between the wheel bolt and the driving implement held within the inner cavity.

A technique for employing a protective sleeve with a wheel fastener, the technique comprising: passing a driving tool bearing a fastener recess through an access aperture of a protective sleeve, the access aperture bounded by a lip of a sidewall extending between the access aperture and a closed terminus formed where the sidewall converges, the sidewall additionally bounding an inner cavity, such that the fastener recess is situated within the inner cavity at the closed terminus and arranged to abut an inner face of the sidewall at the closed terminus; mating a wheel fastener seated on a rim with an outer face of the closed terminus such that the inner face of the sidewall substantially matches an inner contour of the fastener recess, the wheel fastener positioned on a wheel; drawing the sidewall rearward along an outer surface of the driving tool so as to furnish a shield between the driving tool and a bolt bore of the wheel; and imparting a turning torque to the driving tool so as to tighten or slacken the wheel fastener on the wheel.

A tire-monitoring reminder arrangement for prompting replacement of a wheel covering, comprising: a wheel-mounted transducer, a configuration apparatus, and a remote computing host; wherein: the wheel-mounted transducer is affixed inside a wheel covering and includes a motion-sensing unit and a recording unit, the motion-sensing unit detecting and continuously supplying wheel angular-acceleration readings to the recording unit for logging and retention; the configuration apparatus includes a storage unit, a communication unit, and a processing unit, the configuration apparatus acquires the angular-acceleration readings and covering specification data via the communication unit, the covering specification data including a covering diameter; the configuration apparatus receives a permissible service-distance interval through the processing unit or the communication unit; the angular-acceleration readings, the covering diameter, and the permissible service-distance interval are held in the storage unit or conveyed by the communication unit to the remote computing host for retention; and the configuration apparatus or the remote computing host derives a revolution count of the wheel covering from the covering diameter and the angular-acceleration readings, then derives actual covering travel-distance data from the revolution count; the configuration apparatus or the remote computing host performs a calculation and comparison between the permissible service-distance interval and the actual covering travel-distance data to generate distance-comparison outcome information, and transmits the distance-comparison outcome information back to the configuration apparatus to indicate whether the wheel covering ought to be replaced.

A tire-monitoring cloud-based arrangement designed to prompt a tire swap, comprising: a tire-mounted transducer, a remote data hub, an on-vehicle controller, and a data-handling apparatus; wherein: the transducer is affixed inside a tire and includes a wheel-revolution sensing element that generates tire motion-acceleration readings, which are either passed to the on-vehicle controller, or sent onward to the remote data hub via the on-vehicle controller, or made available for retrieval by the data-handling apparatus when connected; the on-vehicle controller or the data-handling apparatus obtains tire specifications from an outside source, the specifications comprising a tire diameter and an acceptable service distance span; the diameter and the service distance span are kept in the on-vehicle controller or the data-handling apparatus, or are relayed to the remote data hub by the on-vehicle controller or the data-handling apparatus; and the on-vehicle controller, the data-handling apparatus, or the remote data hub derives a count of tire revolutions from the diameter and the motion-acceleration readings, then derives an actual distance traveled by the tire from that count; the on-vehicle controller, the data-handling apparatus, or the remote data hub carries out a calculation and comparison using the acceptable service distance span and the actual distance traveled to produce a distance-comparison output, and returns that output to the on-vehicle controller or the data-handling apparatus to signal whether the tire ought to be replaced.

A tire wear-alert cloud-based oversight arrangement, adapted to prompt tire swapping, comprising: a tyre-mounted detector; a configuration apparatus; a remote host computer; an onboard vehicle controller; an RFID transponder; and a data handling unit; wherein at least one of the configuration apparatus, the remote host computer, or the onboard vehicle controller includes an evaluation submodule; wherein: the tyre-mounted detector is fitted within a tyre; the configuration apparatus derives a mileage limit window by summing a vehicle distance shown on an instrument panel with an allowable tyre service distance range, and the mileage limit window is transmitted to the evaluation submodule of the remote host computer for retention; after the mileage limit window is acquired, the configuration apparatus repeatedly transmits a newly displayed vehicle distance on the instrument panel to the evaluation submodule of the remote host computer for retention, thereby producing distance progression records; the configuration apparatus interrogates the RFID transponder associated with the tyre-mounted detector to acquire corresponding tyre identification, and that identification is conveyed to the remote host computer for retention in association with the mileage limit window and the distance progression records; and the evaluation submodule of the remote host computer compares and computes the mileage limit window against the distance progression records based on the tyre identification to yield a mileage comparison outcome, and returns the mileage comparison outcome to the configuration apparatus, the onboard vehicle controller, or the data handling unit; and when the distance progression records surpass a lower bound of the mileage limit window, the remote host computer issues an alert message to the configuration apparatus, the onboard vehicle controller, or the data handling unit.

A tire-replacement reminder arrangement for a motor vehicle, comprising: a configuration instrument and a remote processing host; wherein: the configuration instrument acquires an odometer reading shown on an instrument panel together with an allowable wear distance for a tire, adds said odometer reading to said allowable wear distance to establish a distance limit window, and retains said distance limit window within the configuration instrument or transmits said distance limit window to the remote processing host for retention; once said distance limit window has been acquired, each time the remote processing host or the configuration instrument receives a fresh odometer reading, it stores and calculates resulting odometer progression information; the configuration instrument receives tire particulars from an outside source; said tire particulars are kept in the configuration instrument, or are forwarded by the configuration instrument to the remote processing host for keeping; said tire particulars are linked, within the remote processing host or the configuration instrument, to said distance limit window and to said odometer progression information; and the remote processing host or the configuration instrument compares and computes said distance limit window and said odometer progression information in light of said tire particulars to generate distance comparison outcome data, and returns said distance comparison outcome data to the configuration instrument to indicate whether the tire ought to be replaced.

A tire service-interval notification platform, designed to prompt tire changeover, comprising: an onboard vehicle controller, a remote data hub, and a data handling apparatus; wherein: the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus acquires an odometer reading shown on the instrument panel and a permissible tire wear distance band; the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus derives a distance limit window by summing the odometer reading with the permissible tire wear distance band, and the distance limit window is held in the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus, or is transmitted to the remote data hub for retention; once the distance limit window is established, each time the remote data hub, the onboard controller, or the data handling apparatus again obtains a fresh odometer reading from the instrument panel, it records and processes the fresh reading to produce distance progression data; the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus receives tire particulars from an outside source, the tire particulars being retained in the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus, or being sent to the remote data hub for retention by the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus; the tire particulars are linked with the distance limit window and the distance progression data within the remote data hub, the onboard controller, or the data handling apparatus; and the remote data hub, the onboard controller, or the data handling apparatus evaluates and calculates the distance limit window against the distance progression data using the tire particulars to generate distance comparison outcome information, and returns the distance comparison outcome information to the onboard controller or the data handling apparatus to indicate whether the tires ought to be swapped out.

A tire monitoring data handling arrangement, intended for tallying dispatched units and sorting dispatched goods of tire-mounted transducers, comprising: transducers each bearing a distinct identifier code, the identifier code being imprinted on an outer housing of the transducer and/or held as identifier code data in a retention circuit of the transducer; a configuration apparatus that acquires the identifier code data associated with each transducer and retains said data in a local buffer of the configuration apparatus or relays said data to a remote data center for retention; a computing block provided in at least one of the configuration apparatus and the remote data center, the computing block including a dispatch counting subunit and a goods sorting subunit; wherein the configuration apparatus or the remote data center forwards the received identifier codes to the dispatch counting subunit to total the number of identifier codes, thereby producing dispatch volume figures that are saved in the remote data center; and the configuration apparatus or the remote data center further forwards the received identifier codes to the goods sorting subunit, which groups the received identifier codes according to a preset grouping criterion to generate detailed dispatched-goods grouping records saved in the remote data center.

A tire monitoring cloud platform arrangement, designed to acquire identifier codes from multiple tire monitors collectively, comprising: tire monitors each having a transmitter circuit and a recording circuit, the recording circuit holding identifier code data assigned to the respective tire monitor; a configuration apparatus including a processor chip, a volatile storage, a calculation circuit, a long-wave transmitter-receiver, a short-wave transmitter-receiver, and an identifier screening circuit linked to the processor chip; and a shielded enclosure constituted by a hermetically closed housing able to block electromagnetic radiation, a long-wave activator being installed within the shielded enclosure; wherein the configuration apparatus and the tire monitors bearing identifier codes to be read are situated inside the shielded enclosure and sealed therein, the long-wave activator is energized to dispatch a long-wave activation signal to the tire monitors, the transmitter circuits of the tire monitors receive the long-wave activation signal and are prompted to return the identifier code data, and the short-wave transmitter-receiver of the configuration apparatus captures the identifier code data and relays it back to the processor chip; the processor chip uses the identifier screening circuit to discard identifier code data received more than once without duplicate logging, thereby gathering identifier code data of every tire monitor within the shielded enclosure collectively, and the processor chip compiles the identifier code data into an identifier roster, which it saves in the volatile storage and/or forwards to the cloud platform.

A sales-tracking process executed within a tire-monitoring cloud platform for vending tire monitoring transducers, the platform including monitoring transducers, a programming terminal, a remote host, and a data handling apparatus; the process comprising: presenting, by the remote host, a web interface through which purchasers submit purchase requests and thereby produce purchase records; compiling, by sellers using the programming terminal or the data handling apparatus, a roster of identifiers read from a number of monitoring transducers matching the purchase record; tallying, by the programming terminal, the transducers in the roster and initiating a bundling operation for the transducers upon the tally reaching a predetermined bundle size; and transmitting the roster to the remote host by the programming terminal, whereupon the remote host links the purchase record to the roster to generate and retain sales reporting data, which is made accessible for retrieval by the programming terminal or the data handling apparatus.

A process for controlling a surveillance apparatus that tracks at least one automotive attribute of a motor car, the process comprising: placing the surveillance apparatus into a traveling state or a parked state depending on a speed of the motor car; transmitting linking beacons for establishing a radio link with an outside unit in the parked state; and, before switching to the parked state, placing the surveillance apparatus into a preliminary state in which a passive listening for radio linking beacons originating from the outside unit is conducted, and wherein the preliminary state is entered prior to the parked state.

An apparatus for sensing a condition of a road vehicle, the apparatus comprising: a sensing unit configured to select between an active running state and an idle state based on the speed of the road vehicle; the sensing unit being further configured to transmit pairing messages to an outside terminal, such as a service tool for the sensing unit, while in the idle state; and, before entering the idle state, the sensing unit being configured to enter a preliminary state in which it listens without transmitting for pairing messages originating from the outside terminal.

A motor vehicle, comprising: a sensing apparatus for at least one operating characteristic of the motor vehicle, wherein the sensing apparatus is adapted to function in a motion state or in a idle state depending on a speed of the motor vehicle, the sensing apparatus being adapted to emit broadcast signals in the idle state for establishing a radio link with an outside unit, and before transitioning into the idle state, the sensing apparatus being adapted to function in an interim state, a silent scan for radio link signals originating from the outside unit being conducted by the sensing apparatus during the interim state.

An apparatus comprising: a compressor, adapted to be fixedly attached to a rim; a first member supported for rotation with respect to the compressor; a second member; and a biasing assembly coupled to the first member; wherein the first member is selectively movable between: a compression state, in which the first member bears against the second member and imparts a compressive load to the compressor, the compressive load arising from rotation of the compressor relative to the first member; and an idle state, in which the first member is spaced apart from the second member by an arcuate urging force exerted on the first member by the biasing assembly.

An apparatus for driving an air compressor, comprising: a compressor, adapted to be fixedly attached to a rim; a first suspended weight and a second suspended weight, each pivotally supported with respect to the compressor and selectively placeable among: a compression state, in which a compressing load, arising from displacement of the second suspended weight relative to the compressor, is transmitted to the compressor; and a idle state; a locking assembly adapted to restrain the first suspended weight against movement relative to the second suspended weight during the compression state; and a biasing arrangement joined to the first suspended weight and adapted to regulate movement of the first suspended weight during the idle state.

A towing coupler comprising: a forward section adapted to attach to a pulling machine; a trailing section joined to the forward section, adapted to attach to a hauled machine, and having a pair of elongated side members; and a carriage comprising: a top member spanning across the pair of side members; a bottom member positioned between the pair of side members; a clamp securing segments of each of the pair of side members between the bottom member and the top member; and a pair of projections rising from the bottom member toward the top member and seated laterally between inboard faces of the pair of side members.

A towing coupling apparatus comprising: a forward section adapted to attach to a pulling vehicle; an aft section joined to the forward section and adapted to attach to a towed vehicle; and a carriage joined to the aft section, the carriage having: a top panel fastened to the aft section; at least two braces attached to an underside of the top panel and projecting sideways beyond each lateral edge of the rails; and a bottom panel joined to the top panel and to the aft section.

A towing coupling apparatus comprising: a forward section configured to attach to a pulling vehicle; an aft section joined to the forward section and configured to carry a hauled vehicle; a carriage joined to the aft section, the carriage including: an upper panel having a strengthened region with a top face; a lower panel situated beneath and opposing the upper panel; and a threaded fastener engaging a face of the upper panel positioned beneath the top face of the strengthened region, thereby securing the lower panel and the upper panel to the aft section.

An apparatus for guarding a trailer's pressurized brake line connector, comprising: a shield assembly that blocks physical reach to the line connector when situated in a shut state, and that exposes the connector when situated in an unshut state; a locking element that holds the shield assembly in the shut state; and a control unit that energizes the locking element to release the shield assembly so it may move from the shut state into the unshut state.

A process, comprising: confirming, via a processor mounted on a trailer unit, that a towing vehicle holds permission to couple with the trailer unit; and, upon confirming that the towing vehicle holds such permission, instructing, via the processor, a latch assembly to release a shield member enclosing a pneumatic brake line fitting of the trailer unit so that the shield member can swing into an exposed state revealing the pneumatic brake line fitting.

An infant cradle apparatus, comprising: a receptacle having a floor section, a forward panel section, a rearward panel section, a left lateral panel section, and a right lateral panel section, each of the forward panel section, the rearward panel section, the left lateral panel section, and the right lateral panel section rising from the floor section, the rearward panel section joining a rear margin of the left lateral panel section to a rear margin of the right lateral panel section, the receptacle forming a first cutout between a first margin of the forward panel section and the left lateral panel section such that a top rim of the receptacle includes a first rim segment situated beneath a highest point of the forward panel section, the receptacle forming a second cutout between a second margin of the forward panel section and the right lateral panel section such that the top rim includes a second rim segment situated beneath the highest point of the forward panel section, the second margin of the forward panel section situated opposite the first margin of the forward panel section; a pedestal; a upright structure secured to the pedestal; and a swing member pivotally secured to the upright structure, the swing member adapted to carry the receptacle.

An infant sleeping apparatus, comprising: a support foundation; an upright member coupled to the support foundation; a cantilevered boom pivotally mounted to the upright member; a cradle carrier linked to the boom; a receptacle including a forward panel, a rearward panel positioned across from the forward panel, a left panel, and a right panel positioned across from the left panel, the forward panel having an overall elevation lower than an overall elevation of the left panel and an overall elevation of the right panel so that a leading margin of the left panel, a leading margin of the right panel, and a top margin of the forward panel together delimit an opening leading into an inner cavity of the receptacle; and a liner dimensioned to be detachably seated within the inner cavity of the receptacle, the liner being arranged to partially block the opening; and
