query_text: A process for strengthening a wire wheel element, comprising: cutting a drawn rod to a predetermined extent after being rectified; initially pressing one extremity of the rod with a first press tool to produce a preliminary cap and a narrowed shank; gripping the preliminarily shaped rod in a holding mold so that the reinforced segment is shaped during the gripping; pressing the rod held by the same holding mold with a second press tool to yield a finished cap, a finished narrowed shank and the reinforced segment; and threading the extremity opposite the cap through a rolling operation to form a screw section.

A spoke assembly comprising: an elongated shank body; a cap portion and a constricted section arranged successively extending from a first terminal edge of the shank body; a reinforcement segment formed adjacent the constricted section; and a screw-threaded region provided at a second terminal edge of the shank body.

A retention arrangement adapted to fasten a vehicle wheel rim onto a vehicle hub, the arrangement comprising: a fastening sleeve having a threaded outer face configured to mate with a threaded bore of the hub and a threaded bore of its own; a collar projecting from a leading end of the fastening sleeve so as to bear against the wheel rim along an axis of the arrangement; a series of resiliently flexible gripping tabs formed at a trailing end of the fastening sleeve, the tabs being circumferentially distributed about the fastening sleeve at intervals, each tab being yieldable in a radial sense and presenting an inward-facing flank and an outward-facing flank for engaging a bearing face of the hub; and a locking bolt including a stem carrying an outer thread engageable with the threaded bore of the fastening sleeve, and a cap disposed at an end of the stem, the cap presenting an outer peripheral face for engaging the inward-facing flanks of the tabs; wherein at least one of the inward-facing flanks of the tabs and the outer peripheral face of the cap is tapered, such that the tabs are urged radially outward when the stem is threaded into the threaded bore of the fastening sleeve.

A locomotion arrangement for an autonomous machine, comprising: a chassis enclosure; at least two propulsion rollers disposed inside the chassis enclosure; a control module possessing persistent machine-readable instructions that, upon execution by the control module, actuate the at least two propulsion rollers; a plurality of spherical supports disposed inside the chassis enclosure, the spherical supports being situated in relation to the chassis enclosure and to the at least two propulsion rollers so as to reduce a gravitational centroid of the machine and furnish steadiness during movement; and a plurality of cradle structures secured within the chassis enclosure for accommodating the plurality of spherical supports.

A hub assembly for a vehicle, comprising: a first rolling bearing unit having an inboard ring secured to a rotor body; a mounting disc detachably attachable to the rotor body; and a second rolling bearing unit having an external ring affixed to the rotor body and an internal ring affixed to a driveshaft; wherein the rotor body defines internal toothing that encircles external toothing formed on the driveshaft.

A hub assembly for a vehicle, comprising: a bearing unit having an inboard race secured to a central housing; a rim mount adapted to be detachably secured to the central housing; and a secondary bearing having an external ring fixed to the central housing and an internal ring fixed to a drive spindle which carries external teeth; wherein the central housing defines internal teeth of greater diameter than the external teeth; and wherein the internal teeth and the external teeth are arranged to engage a locking retainer and a torque transmitting joint in alternative arrangements.

A fibrous mat assembly comprising: a multiplicity of filaments formed from a metallic material, each filament extending along a longitudinal axis and presenting, in a plane perpendicular to that axis, a transverse outline defining a convex polygon.

A vehicle pneumatic tyre comprising a crown reinforcement having at least one reinforcing layer strengthened by steel cables set within elastomeric compound, each of the steel cables incorporating an identical quantity of steel wires, wherein the steel cables: extend side by side and are spaced at substantially uniform intervals within the at least one reinforcing layer; carry elastomer skim coatings on both faces whose combined thickness lies between 0.10 mm and 2.00 mm; when seen in transverse section, constitute open-flattened steel cables formed of four to six steel wires periodically laid together, at least two of which are flat-deformed in transverse section and exhibit a major dimension and a minor dimension orthogonal thereto whose quotient lies between 1.10 and 3.00; and are separated from one another by equal gaps ranging from 0.10 mm to 1.00 mm.

A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a casing having a main ply section extending in toroidal fashion between a pair of annular beads and a turned-up ply section emanating from the main ply section and wrapping about the periphery of the beads from an axially inward side to an axially outward side; and a transponder unit installed at the axially outward side of the turned-up ply section; wherein, in a reference condition in which the tyre is mounted on a specified wheel rim, inflated to a predetermined pressure, and unloaded, the cord run direction of the turned-up ply section is tilted relative to the tyre radial direction as seen along the tyre axial direction.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, comprising: a reinforcing girdle formed from one or more plies; a circumferential channel cut into a ground-engaging face; and an RFID-type transponder unit installed at a location situated radially beyond a floor of the channel, radially beyond an interior face of the uppermost ply of the girdle, and laterally beyond a narrowest ply of the girdle, wherein a radially exterior side of the transponder unit lacks any overlying girdle material.

A reconditioned pneumatic tire comprising: a foundation carcass having a crown structure formed of at least one reinforcing ply, the carcass being produced by eliminating an external radial portion situated radially beyond an exterior face of a radially outermost ply of the crown structure; a telemetry module installed within the foundation carcass at a site lying radially beyond an interior face of a radially innermost ply of the crown structure and laterally beyond a narrowest ply of the crown structure; and a replacement tread bonded to a radially exterior side of the foundation carcass, wherein a radially exterior side of the telemetry module is uncovered by the crown structure.

A method of manufacturing a renewed tire having an embedded signal-transmitting module, the method comprising: stripping, from a casing containing a belt formed of one or more plies, an upper portion extending radially beyond an exterior face of an outermost ply of the belt to yield a base casing; positioning a transponder within the base casing at a location radially beyond an interior face of an innermost ply of the belt and laterally beyond a narrowest ply of the belt such that a radially outward side of the transponder is left uncovered by the belt; and bonding a replacement tread band onto the base casing from a radially outward side of the base casing.

A two-wheeled vehicle tyre pair comprising: a front tyre and a rear tyre, each tyre having a tread section defining a prescribed rolling direction; each tread section being formed with a series of grooves oriented obliquely relative to the circumferential direction of the tyre; each groove having a central segment extending across the crown zone, an outer segment extending across the shoulder zone, and an intermediate segment joining the central segment to the outer segment; the intermediate segment being narrower in width than both the central segment and the outer segment; the central, outer, and intermediate segments all being angled toward a common side relative to the circumferential direction; the intermediate segment being bounded by a pair of walls, the pair including a first wall positioned forward along the rolling direction and a second wall positioned rearward along the rolling direction; the first wall of the front tyre being bevelled; and the second wall of the rear tyre being bevelled.

A pair of two-wheeler tires, consisting of a leading tire and a trailing tire, each having a tread carrying a multiplicity of slanted channels disposed obliquely relative to the circumferential direction, wherein each slanted channel comprises an initial segment traversing a central zone of the tread, a terminal segment traversing a flank zone of the tread, and a constricted segment joining the initial segment to the terminal segment, the constricted segment exhibiting a narrower channel width than both the initial segment and the terminal segment, all three segments being angled toward a common direction with respect to the circumferential direction, and the trailing tire having an assigned direction of wheel travel such that, in view of that travel direction, each slanted channel of the trailing tire meets the road surface starting from the initial segment and proceeding toward the constricted segment.

A mounting assembly adapted to secure at least one composite rim to a hub, the composite rim defining at least one receiving opening through which an elongate threaded member passes, the mounting assembly comprising: (A) a clamping member that either comprises the elongate threaded member or is designed to be secured onto the elongate threaded member, the clamping member possessing a mating section; and (B) a seating insert that incorporates: a support collar having a foundation designed to abut a face of the composite rim surrounding the receiving opening; a passage through which the elongate threaded member is threaded in operation, the passage defining a securing axis; a projecting portion which extends longitudinally from the foundation of the support collar relative to the securing axis about the passage, the projecting portion being shaped to protrude into the receiving opening of the composite rim; and at least one interlocking face extending from an interior wall of the projecting portion, the at least one interlocking face having a configuration substantially matching the mating section of the clamping member and being arranged to engage the mating section of the clamping member when the clamping member is tightened against the hub through the elongate threaded member, wherein at least a part of the at least one interlocking face lies beneath the foundation of the support collar and between the foundation of the support collar and a terminal end of the projecting portion, and wherein the terminal end of the projecting portion extends into the receiving opening of the composite rim and is separated from the hub, or from a feature situated within, upon, formed with, or next to the hub, such that the terminal end of the projecting portion does not directly contact the hub and/or said feature.

A vehicle wheel covering apparatus comprising: a pressure relief fitting; a cover panel having an interior section; a bayonet-type locking arrangement configured to attach to a wheel-and-tire unit and engageable with the interior section of the cover panel, wherein the cover panel is detachably affixable to the wheel by way of the bayonet-type locking arrangement and the bayonet-type locking arrangement permits the cover panel to pivot through a fraction of one full revolution into a locked orientation.

A hubcap apparatus, comprising: a pressure-relief fitting; a cover panel; and a snap-and-twist retention arrangement cooperating with the cover panel, wherein the cover panel is detachably mounted to a rim by the snap-and-twist retention arrangement, the snap-and-twist retention arrangement being configured to accept the cover panel and permit the cover panel to pivot less than one full revolution into a locked orientation.

A tire-hub covering apparatus, comprising: a pressure-relief fitting; a cover panel defining a central aperture; a locking coupler configured to engage a mounting frame fixed to a wheel hub, wherein: a collar is configured to fasten to the locking coupler when the collar is turned into a fastened orientation and to disengage from the locking coupler when the collar is turned into a disengaged orientation, and wherein the locking coupler fits through the aperture of the cover panel such that the cover panel is held to the coupler by the collar when the collar is turned into the fastened orientation.

A bicycle drivetrain core, comprising: a central spindle establishing an axis of revolution; a first revolving member supported on the spindle for rotation about the axis; a second revolving member supported on the spindle for rotation about the axis; a first pawl carrier having at least one first engaging projection, the first pawl carrier being linked to the first revolving member so as to turn therewith; a second pawl carrier having at least one second engaging projection meshing with the at least one first engaging projection, the second pawl carrier being linked to the second revolving member so as to turn therewith; and a sliding bearing element arranged to turn with the first revolving member and to glide relative to the second revolving member along a peripheral direction about the axis, the sliding bearing element possessing a first bearing face in sliding engagement with an axially oriented face of the one of the first pawl carrier and the second pawl carrier linked to the second revolving member, and a second bearing face in sliding engagement with a radially oriented face of that same carrier, the first bearing face being composed of a material differing from that of the second bearing face.

A cycling transmission assembly for a bicycle, the assembly including: a spindle extending along a central longitudinal axis; a driving carrier supported on the spindle for rotation about the axis; a driven carrier supported on the spindle for rotation about the axis; a pawl element provided with at least one engaging projection that meshes with at least one receiving notch, the pawl element being linked to the driving carrier so as to turn therewith; a catch element carrying the at least one receiving notch, the catch element being linked to the driven carrier so as to turn therewith; and a sliding member arranged to turn together with the driving carrier and to travel relative to the driven carrier along a circular path about the axis, the sliding member presenting a first bearing face in frictional contact with an axially oriented side of the catch element and a second bearing face in frictional contact with a radially oriented side of that same catch element, the sliding member comprising a first component bearing the first bearing face and a second component bearing the second bearing face, the first component being rigidly secured to the second component.

An axle-mounted transmission assembly for a pedal-driven cycle, the assembly including: a spindle establishing a central longitudinal axis; a drive member supported on the spindle for rotation about the central longitudinal axis; a driven member supported on the spindle for rotation about the central longitudinal axis; a pawl-bearing element having at least one first engagement projection and being joined to the drive member so as to turn therewith; a receiving element having at least one second engagement projection engaged with the at least one first engagement projection and being joined to the driven member so as to turn therewith; and a sliding element arranged to turn the drive member and to travel circumferentially relative to the driven member about the central longitudinal axis, the sliding element presenting a first bearing face in slidable contact with an end-facing face of the one of the pawl-bearing element and the receiving element joined to the driven member, and a second bearing face in slidable contact with an outward-facing face of that same element, the first bearing face lying at a first distance from the central longitudinal axis and the second bearing face lying at a second distance from the central longitudinal axis, the second distance being no greater than the first distance.

An assembly for a bicycle drivetrain, the assembly comprising: a spindle defining a central rotational axis; a first driven member supported on the spindle for rotation about the central rotational axis; a second driven member supported on the spindle for rotation about the central rotational axis; a first pawl element bearing at least one first engaging projection and secured to the first driven member for co-rotation therewith; a second pawl element bearing at least one second engaging projection engageable with the at least one first engaging projection and secured to the second driven member for co-rotation therewith; and a sliding block arranged to co-rotate with the first driven member while moving circumferentially relative to the second driven member about the central rotational axis, the sliding block including a first locking flange engaged with a second locking flange of the first driven member, the first locking flange presenting at least one first peripherally oriented face, the second locking flange presenting at least one second peripherally oriented face contacting the at least one first peripherally oriented face in a circumferential sense about the central rotational axis, wherein at least one of the at least one first peripherally oriented face and the at least one second peripherally oriented face comprises a ramped face tilted with respect to an axial orientation about the central rotational axis.

A bicycle transmission hub assembly, the assembly including: a spindle extending along a central longitudinal axis; a first driven member supported on the spindle so as to revolve about the central longitudinal axis; a second driven member supported on the spindle so as to revolve about the central longitudinal axis; a first pawl carrier having at least one first engagement projection, the first pawl carrier being linked to the first driven member so as to turn in unison therewith; and a second pawl carrier having at least one second engagement projection meshing with the at least one first engagement projection, the second pawl carrier being linked to the second driven member so as to turn in unison therewith, the at least one first engagement projection and the at least one second engagement projection being transitionable from a separated state to a meshed state such that tips of the at least one first engagement projection and the at least one second engagement projection draw toward one another along the central longitudinal axis while the first pawl carrier and the second pawl carrier turn relative to one another about the central longitudinal axis.

A tire-use elastomeric blend comprising: a polymer constituent and a reinforcing particulate material including at least precipitated silica; wherein the polymer constituent includes a functionalized styrene-butadiene copolymer (A) exhibiting a glass transition point of −50° C. or below, prepared by reacting a compound of formula with a functionalizing reagent, and a non-functionalized styrene-butadiene copolymer (B) whose glass transition point exceeds that of copolymer (A) by at least 30° C.; wherein in formula, R1 to R8 are independently C1–C20 alkyl radicals, L1 and L2 are independently C1–C20 alkylene radicals, and n is an integer from 2 to 4.

A pneumatic road wheel covering, comprising: a casing framework having two lateral margins each coupled to a respective bead assembly; optionally, a reinforcing ply arrangement disposed radially outward of the casing framework; a contact layer disposed radially outward of the casing framework, the reinforcing ply arrangement, or both; wherein the contact layer includes a cured elastomeric material formed by curing an uncured elastomeric formulation which, prior to blending, comprises an elastomer composition including: (i) 100 phr of a polymer blend comprising: a. at least one styrene-butadiene copolymer (SBR) exhibiting a glass transition temperature between −45° C. and −15° C. in a proportion of 40 phr to 100 phr, and b. from 0 phr to 30 phr of at least one polyisoprene (IR) exhibiting a glass transition temperature between −80° C. and −50° C.; (ii) from 15 phr to 50 phr of a tackifier mixture comprising: a. at least one tackifying resin having a softening point below 50° C. in an amount of 5 phr to 45 phr, and b. at least one tackifying resin having a softening point above 110° C. in an amount of 5 phr to 45 phr; (iii) from 1 phr to 130 phr of at least one reinforcing filler; and (iv) from 0.1 phr to 12 phr of at least one curing agent.

A curable rubber formulation prior to blending, the formulation containing: (i) 100 parts per hundred rubber of a polymer system including: a. at least one styrene-butadiene copolymer exhibiting a glass transition point between -45 C and -15 C present at 40 to 100 parts per hundred rubber; and b. 0 to 30 parts per hundred rubber of at least one polyisoprene exhibiting a glass transition point between -80 C and -50 C; (ii) 15 to 50 parts per hundred rubber of a tackifying system including: a. at least one tackifier having a softening point below 50 C at 5 to 45 parts per hundred rubber; b. at least one tackifier having a softening point above 110 C at 5 to 45 parts per hundred rubber; and c. 0 to 40 parts per hundred rubber of at least one tackifier having a softening point between 50 C and 110 C; (iii) 1 to 130 parts per hundred rubber of at least one reinforcing particulate; and (iv) 0.1 to 12 parts per hundred rubber of at least one curing agent.

A pneumatic vehicle covering for a passenger car, the covering including, in a meridional cross-section: a pair of bead cores configured to seat on a wheel rim; a pair of flank layers each joined to one of the bead cores; a belt-bearing crown having a first edge coupled to a radially outward extremity of one flank layer and a second edge coupled to a radially outward extremity of the other flank layer; at least one ply structure running from the bead cores to the crown, comprising multiple cord elements and secured within the bead cores by being folded upward around an annular anchoring member to define a principal portion and an upturned portion within each bead; two lower zones forming parts of the covering disposed on opposite sides of a radial reference line passing through a central point of the covering, a first lower zone on one side of the radial reference line encompassing one bead core and at least a segment of the flank layer on that side, and a second lower zone on the other side encompassing the other bead core and at least a segment of the other flank layer, each lower zone having a meridional face bounded by an axial reference line located at a radial distance equal to seventy percent of a distance H, H being the radial span between a first axial reference line tangent to a radially innermost point of the annular anchoring member and a second axial reference line tangent to the tread at its radially outermost point, and bounded radially inward by a perimeter contour of the bead configured for contact with the rim, each lower zone occupying a volume produced by revolving the meridional face about the rotational axis of the covering; wherein the bead of each lower zone includes at least one filler layer retained at least partly between the principal portion of the ply structure, the upturned portion of the ply structure and the radially outer segment of the annular anchoring member, and wherein each elastomeric compound of the covering has an elastic shear modulus and a viscoelastic loss measured per ASTM D 5992-96 at 23 degrees Celsius under a shear strain of ten percent, each compound layer of each lower zone having a viscoelastic loss Tan(δ)max of less than or equal to 0.10 constituting between thirty and ninety percent of the total volume of that lower zone, and the elastic shear modulus of each flank layer lying within the range of 0.5 to 10 MPa.

A airless wheel tyre comprising: an inner annular member having a first radius; an outer annular member having a second radius exceeding the first radius, the outer annular member being generally concentric with the inner annular member; and a multiplicity of web members extending between and joining the inner annular member and the outer annular member; wherein the web members exhibit a tensile rigidity of at least 11 and at most 150 N/mm°, and a compressive rigidity of at least 11 and at most 100 N/mm°.

An airless wheel structure comprising: an inner annular member possessing a first circumference; an outer annular member possessing a second circumference larger than the first, the outer annular member being arranged concentrically about the inner annular member; and a set of web elements running between and linking the inner annular member and the outer annular member; wherein the set of web elements exhibits a ratio of tensile rigidity to compressive rigidity falling within the span of 0.3:1 to 8:1.

A process for fabricating an airless wheel tread structure, the process comprising: simulating a reference wheel structure possessing a reference breadth and a reference rated loading; choosing a baseline radial rigidity value and a baseline lateral rigidity value informed by the simulating, the baseline radial rigidity value falling within a range of 11 to 150 N/mm° inclusive and the baseline lateral rigidity value falling within a range of 11 to 100 N/mm° inclusive; deriving a target radial rigidity and a target lateral rigidity for a wheel design having a first design breadth and a first design load rating by modifying the baseline radial rigidity value and the baseline lateral rigidity value chosen during the choosing; and building a first airless wheel having the first design breadth and the first design load rating, and further exhibiting the target radial rigidity and the target lateral rigidity derived during the deriving.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread arranged to engage a ground surface; a pair of angled plies having intersecting filaments; wherein a combined void capacity of the channels provided in the tread on the side facing away from the vehicle, relative to a central circumferential plane, is smaller than a combined void capacity of the channels provided in the tread on the side facing the vehicle, relative to said plane; and a reinforcement layer retaining a plurality of strengthening filaments oriented across the tyre width and along the radial direction, disposed at a set spacing between the angled plies and the tread, the reinforcement layer extending from the side facing away from the vehicle to the side facing the vehicle; and

query_text: A pneumatic tyre comprising: a pair of annular beads each incorporating a bead core; a casing ply extending from one bead to the other so as to wrap around both bead cores; a plurality of reinforcing strata arranged radially outward of a crown region of the casing ply, the strata including at least one hoop-oriented stratum having reinforcing filaments aligned substantially in a circumferential direction of the tyre, and at least one inclined stratum having reinforcing filaments oriented obliquely to the circumferential direction, the inclined stratum being situated radially outward of the hoop-oriented stratum; and a transponder unit including an integrated circuit chip and at least one rectilinear antenna electrically coupled to the integrated circuit chip, the transponder unit being embedded at a radial location that lies radially inward of a position of maximum tyre width and radially outward of an outermost edge position of the bead core, wherein the rectilinear antenna of the transponder unit extends along the circumferential direction of the tyre.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread bearing a road-contacting exterior face, the tread including a primary region spanning a middle section of the tread and a secondary region abutting the primary region and positioned at each side edge of the tread; wherein the primary region consists of a first elastomeric blend and the secondary region consists of a second elastomeric blend, and wherein the dynamic shear storage modulus of the first elastomeric blend at 50% strain exceeds that of the second elastomeric blend at 50% strain by no less than 150 percent.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread possessing a road-contacting exterior face; a central region occupying the crown of the tread and fabricated from a first elastomeric mixture; and a flank region positioned beside the central region at each transverse extremity of the tread and fabricated from a second elastomeric mixture; wherein the modulus of elasticity E at 100% elongation of the first elastomeric mixture, measured at 27° C., exceeds that of the second elastomeric mixture, measured at the same temperature, by between 125% and 325%.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread presenting a road-contacting exterior face; a central zone spanning the crown region of the tread and composed of a first elastomeric mixture; and a flank zone abutting the central zone and positioned at each lateral margin of the tread, the flank zone being composed of a second elastomeric mixture; wherein the modulus E at 150% elongation of the first elastomeric mixture, measured at 27° C., exceeds that of the second elastomeric mixture by between 125% and 325%.

A wheel hoop comprising: a ring-shaped structure encircling a central axis, a notional circular path being delineated on an exterior face of the ring-shaped structure, the notional circular path encompassing the central axis; and at least one fiber-reinforced tape, helically wound about the notional circular path through at least a full revolution and bonded to the exterior face of the ring-shaped structure, terminal edges of each of the at least one fiber-reinforced tape, measured along a lengthwise dimension of the fiber-reinforced tape, being registered with the notional circular path.

A cassette carrier adapted to be mounted on a sprocket carrier of a bicycle, the sprocket carrier coupled to a bicycle wheel hub and having a first helical thread, the cassette carrier comprising: a tubular body having a first axial terminus and a second axial terminus facing away from the first axial terminus, an interior wall of the first axial terminus bearing a second helical thread engageable with the first helical thread; and a radial collar positioned at the second axial terminus and extending outwardly past an exterior wall of the tubular body.

A tire-use elastomer blend, comprising: 10 to 50 parts by weight of a resinous thermoplastic component per 100 parts by weight of a diene-based elastomer, wherein at least 60 wt% of said diene-based elastomer is a styrene-butadiene copolymer exhibiting a bound styrene amount of 5 to 30 wt% and a 1,2-butadiene unit content of 10 to 35 wt%; wherein a 1:1 by-mass blend of said diene-based elastomer and said resinous thermoplastic component has a calculated glass transition temperature (Tga), derived from a mean glass transition temperature (Tg1) of the diene-based elastomer and a glass transition temperature (Tg2) of the resinous thermoplastic component, that differs from its measured glass transition temperature (Tgm) by 5 to 50 °C; the glass transition temperature (Tg2) of the resinous thermoplastic component exceeding the mean glass transition temperature (Tg1) of the diene-based elastomer by 110 to 150 °C; and the resinous thermoplastic component constitutes 30 wt% or more of the total plasticizing constituents present in the blend.

A pneumatic tire comprising: a cross-sectional height SH falling within 50 mm to 150 mm when the tire is fitted to a prescribed wheel rim and charged to a prescribed inflation pressure in an unloaded condition; a clearance dimension A measured along a normal extending from an uppermost location of a rim flange in a radial sense to an exterior surface of the tire, wherein A relative to SH obeys 0.01≤A/SH≤0.16; and a first location P where a horizontal reference running across the tire in its width sense through the uppermost location of the rim flange meets the exterior surface of the tire, a second location Q defining a rim breadth and a rim diameter of the prescribed wheel rim, and an inclination angle α between a line joining P and Q and the horizontal reference in the width sense lying within 50°≤α≤80°.

A tyre incorporating a built-in bladder, comprising: an outer contact member meant to engage the ground; a reinforcing band assembly; and a casing structure; wherein: said outer contact member forms the exterior surface of said tyre that engages the pavement; said casing structure includes a lateral panel, a rim-engaging bead, and multiple laminations including a radial ply serving as an upper lamination, an airtight innermost lamination serving as a lower lamination, and a bladder interposed between said radial ply and the airtight lamination; said bladder is a sealed enclosed chamber charged with a pressurizing medium within said casing structure, wherein said casing structure is affixed to said reinforcing band assembly and said reinforcing band assembly is affixed to said outer contact member; and said lateral panel guards said casing structure and said bead wraps about the casing structure to couple said tyre to a wheel rim.

A pneumatic tyre having an outboard-facing first lateral region and an inboard-facing second lateral region, delimited relative to a mid-circumferential plane, the tyre comprising: a ply structure that spans from a first annular bead bundle situated in the first lateral region to a second annular bead bundle situated in the second lateral region, the ply structure including: a main ply section that runs circumferentially between the first and second annular bead bundles; a first turn-up ply section that departs from the main ply section, wraps about a periphery of the first annular bead bundle from a tyre axial inner side toward a tyre axial outer side, and rises in a tyre radial outward direction; and a second turn-up ply section that departs from the main ply section, wraps about a periphery of the second annular bead bundle from the tyre axial inner side toward the tyre axial outer side, and rises in the tyre radial outward direction, wherein a terminal edge of the first turn-up ply section on its radially outward side lies farther in the tyre radial outward direction than a terminal edge of the second turn-up ply section on its radially outward side, and a wireless transponder is incorporated within a sidewall region of the first lateral region, situated radially inward of the terminal edge of the first turn-up ply section and radially outward of the terminal edge of the second turn-up ply section.

A tyre designed to be fitted to a motor vehicle with a prescribed orientation, the tyre comprising a tread compound layer disposed over a running surface; the tread compound layer comprising: a set of longitudinal channels running in a peripheral direction of the tyre, a couple of edge lugs delimited by the channels and positioned on lateral exteriors relative to an axial direction of the tyre, and a central rib-type element situated between the couple of edge lugs, the central element being a rib formation extending uninterrupted around the peripheral direction, and the tread compound layer exhibiting a dynamic storage modulus at −25° C. of at least 60 MPa and at most 150 MPa.

A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a pair of annular beads each incorporating a bead core; a casing ply running between the beads; a reinforcing ply situated radially outward of the casing ply; and a ground-engaging crown section; an outside diameter OD (mm) falling within 200≤OD≤660, an overall section width SW (mm) falling within 100≤SW≤400, a groove void proportion Aa (%) of the crown section falling within 0.008≤Aa/OD≤0.150, and, when a zone extending 48×(OD/SW)^(1/5) (%) inward from a widest ground-contact edge on the inboard side, as mounted on a vehicle, is designated as an inboard zone of the crown section, a groove void proportion Ai (%) of the inboard zone and a groove void proportion Ao (%) of an outboard zone, being the remainder of the crown section, satisfy Ai<Ao.

A pneumatic tread arrangement, comprising: a pair of peripheral channels extending around a tire axis; a rib bounded by the peripheral channels; and a plurality of pairings of a first transverse notch and a second transverse notch that cross the peripheral channels within the rib and alternate around the tire axis, the first transverse notch having an entry end communicating with one of the peripheral channels and a terminal end ending within the rib, a breadth at the entry end exceeding a breadth at the terminal end, and the second transverse notch having an entry end communicating with the other of the peripheral channels and a terminal end ending within the rib, a breadth at the entry end being smaller than a breadth at the terminal end, the narrower entry end of the second transverse notch being sealed when in contact with a road surface.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a transponder installed inside a sidewall region of the tyre; an ornamental section provided on an exterior face of the sidewall region and possessing a foundation face; and at least one textured zone located within the ornamental section, wherein within each textured zone, a plurality of ridges rising from the foundation face of the ornamental section by a height of 0.1 mm or more and 1.0 mm or less are arranged at intervals of 0.1 mm or more and 3.0 mm or less, and the whole of the transponder lies inside the ornamental section when viewed in a plane projected along a width direction of the sidewall region.

A spoked wheel construction, comprising: a circular outer ring having a plurality of perforated zones, each perforated zone including a ring-side stop formation at a margin thereof; a central hub positioned at a middle of the circular outer ring, the central hub defining a plurality of flange openings; a plurality of threaded sleeves, each sleeve having an interior threaded bore, an exterior stop portion, and being seated within a respective perforated zone of the circular outer ring with its exterior stop portion engaged with the ring-side stop formation; and a plurality of wire members, each wire member including a central shank, an enlarged anchor end disposed at one extremity of the central shank, and a threaded terminus disposed at an opposing extremity of the central shank, the enlarged anchor ends being received within the flange openings of the central hub and the threaded termini being engaged with the threaded bores of the sleeves.

A lightweight steel road-wheel assembly for a heavy-duty truck, comprising: a tire-seating barrel; a center plate including a mounting flange configured to be removably secured to a hub or spindle; wherein at least one of the barrel and the plate is formed from a quenched and tempered steel alloy containing between 0.18 and 0.37 percent carbon by weight, and at least one of the plate and the barrel is predominantly composed of martensite and exhibits an ultimate tensile strength of no less than 900 MPa; the barrel having a greatest wall thickness not exceeding 4.50 mm and/or the plate having a greatest wall thickness not exceeding 12.00 mm; and a quotient obtained by multiplying the wheel diameter by the wheel width and dividing by the wheel mass exceeding 4000 mm2/kg.

A omnidirectional roller wheel apparatus, comprising: a central carrier, said carrier including a flat disc section and a tubular section projecting outward from said disc section, said tubular section defining a foundation of an outer perimeter of said apparatus; a set of free-turning rollers disposed upon and circumferentially about said foundation; each of said free-turning rollers including an axle and a spinning member, said spinning member being journaled onto said axle by way of needle-type rolling bearings.

A mobile apparatus comprising a drive module, wherein the drive module includes: a principal turning member arranged to revolve around a primary spin axis; and a floating turning member arranged to shift relative to the principal turning member along a path transverse to the primary spin axis, and wherein the floating turning member is arranged to, responsive to revolution of the principal turning member, spin at a principal angular speed, the principal angular speed being an angular speed of the principal turning member.

A technique for operating a locomotive apparatus, the apparatus comprising: a central revolving member turning around a primary spin axis; a shiftable revolving member displaceable relative to the central revolving member and spinning at a principal rotational rate equal to the rotational rate of the central revolving member; and a set of radial arms, each radial arm having a peripheral extremity displaceable relative to the primary spin axis as the central revolving member turns and the shiftable revolving member displaces relative to the central revolving member, the technique comprising: directing the apparatus to move forward at a ground velocity; supplying an acceleration instruction to a processing unit to raise the ground velocity of the apparatus; and in response to the acceleration instruction being supplied to the processing unit, raising an arm displacement rate of a radial arm that engages the ground from among the set of radial arms.

An apparatus for propelling a mobile platform, the apparatus comprising: a primary revolving member arranged to turn around a first axis of spin; a secondary revolving member arranged to shift relative to the primary revolving member along a path crossing the first axis of spin; and wherein the secondary revolving member is arranged to, when the primary revolving member turns, turn at a primary angular speed, the primary angular speed being an angular speed of the primary revolving member.

A wheeled conveyance comprising: a tire-supporting hub having an outer annular section, an inner web section, a first power conveying assembly, and an energy storage cell; a power regulation circuit; and a second power conveying assembly coupled to the first power conveying assembly while the hub is turning, wherein the energy storage cell contains a liquid electrolytic medium that includes a carbon-based solvent, wherein the first power conveying assembly is situated within the inner web section, wherein the first power conveying assembly is coupled to the energy storage cell, wherein the second power conveying assembly is in conductive contact with the first power conveying assembly during rotation of the hub, and wherein the power regulation circuit is arranged to govern charging and discharging of the energy storage cell through the first power conveying assembly and the second power conveying assembly.

A motor vehicle comprising: a road-contacting hub assembly having an outer annular flange, a central plate, a first power coupling device, and an energy storage cell; a power regulating circuit; and a second power coupling device conductively joined to the first power coupling device, wherein the energy storage cell contains a liquid electrolyte that includes a carbon-based solvent, wherein the first power coupling device is situated in the central plate, wherein the first power coupling device is joined to the energy storage cell, wherein the first power coupling device is arranged to exchange electrical energy without physical connectors, wherein the second power coupling device is arranged to exchange electrical energy without physical connectors, and wherein the power regulating circuit is arranged to govern charging and discharging of the energy storage cell through the first power coupling device and the second power coupling device.

A wheel formed in two molded halves, comprising: a hub-bearing disk element and an outer rim element; wherein the disk element and the rim element possess matching interface faces that meet at a well region of the wheel; and wherein the wall of the rim element at its interface face is thinner than the adjacent portion of the rim element beside that face.

A multi-part rim assembly comprising: a spoke portion and a barrel portion; wherein the rim assembly exhibits regions of differing circumference along its axial extent, and the spoke portion and the barrel portion are secured together along matching faces of each, wherein a radial dimension of the engaging face of the spoke portion diminishes toward a terminal edge of that engaging face.

A hub assembly for an automotive wheel, comprising: an outer race component defining two parallel rows of outer tracks along its interior surface; an inner race assembly including a rotating hub member having a radially projecting mounting collar at one axial extremity and a reduced-diameter axial shoulder on its exterior, together with at least one bearing ring pressed onto the shoulder, the inner race assembly presenting two rows of inner tracks opposing the outer tracks; two rows of rolling bodies held for rotation between the outer tracks and the inner tracks; and a seal arrangement closing an open end, on one axial side, of an annular chamber bounded by the outer race component and the inner race assembly, wherein the hub member comprises the inner track, a sealing surface situated at the root of the mounting collar and contacted in sliding fashion by the seal arrangement, a cutout situated radially outward of the sealing surface within the mounting collar, and a collar face situated radially outward of the cutout within the mounting collar, the seal arrangement comprises a rigid insert fitted to an axial end of the outer race component, and a sealing body bonded to the rigid insert, the sealing body includes a wiper edge extending from the rigid insert toward the mounting collar and bearing against the sealing surface, and a labyrinth edge extending from the rigid insert toward the mounting collar radially outward of the wiper edge and axially facing the cutout across a clearance, and the cutout includes a floor located between a radially outer boundary and a radially inner boundary of the cutout, the floor marking the greatest depth of the cutout, and an inclined surface extending radially from the radially outer boundary toward the floor and sloping toward the one axial side as it proceeds from the radially outer boundary toward the floor.

An apparatus, comprising: a decoupling assembly of a drivetrain arrangement, the decoupling assembly including a retaining member arranged to couple with an axle channel formed in a half-shaft and a gear channel formed in a differential side pinion.

A drivetrain arrangement for a motor vehicle, the arrangement comprising: a decoupling assembly having a retainer positioned within a shaft channel of a half-shaft, wherein the retainer couples with a gear channel of a differential output gear during a powered operating state.

A technique for operating a drivetrain decoupling arrangement of an automobile, the technique comprising: shifting a half-shaft toward a differential gear assembly upon a propulsion setting being chosen and coupling a retainer with a circumferential recess of the half-shaft together with a first region of a output gear; and shifting the half-shaft away from the differential gear assembly upon a towing setting being chosen and coupling the retainer with the circumferential recess of the half-shaft together with a second region of the output gear.

An apparatus for transmitting rotational force, comprising: a main shank; a far extremity; and a near extremity, the near extremity incorporating: a transverse section presenting a left face and a right face; a left upright member possessing an upper terminus and a lower terminus, the left upright member attached to the left face of the transverse section at a location intermediate the upper terminus and the lower terminus; a right upright member possessing an upper terminus and a lower terminus, the right upright member attached to the right face of the transverse section at a location intermediate the upper terminus and the lower terminus; wherein a first contour is shaped into the upper terminus of the left upright member and a second contour is shaped into the upper terminus of the right upright member.

A wheel arrangement, comprising: a rim possessing an outboard peripheral margin and an inboard facing face; a driving projection secured to the outboard peripheral margin; and a reaction member joined to the rim and to the driving projection, the reaction member including: a terminal section connected to the driving projection; and a further terminal section attached to the inboard facing face of the rim; wherein the terminal section includes: a transverse segment having a primary flank and a secondary flank; a first upright segment having an initial extremity and a subsequent extremity, the first upright segment affixed to the primary flank of the transverse segment at a location spaced between the initial extremity and the subsequent extremity; a second upright segment having a third extremity and a fourth extremity, the second upright segment affixed to the secondary flank of the transverse segment at a location spaced between the third extremity and the fourth extremity; wherein a first contour is shaped into the initial extremity of the first upright segment and a second contour is shaped into the third extremity of the second upright segment.

An axle braking system, comprising: a rotor assembly; a propulsion stud secured to the rotor assembly; and a force-transmitting member joined to a perimeter of the rotor assembly and to the propulsion stud, the force-transmitting member including: an attachment section situated adjacent the propulsion stud, the attachment section having an upper face and a lower face; a primary upright segment having an upper extremity and a lower extremity, the primary upright segment connected to the upper face of the attachment section between the upper extremity and the lower extremity; and a first contour machined into the upper extremity of the primary upright segment.

An aircraft pneumatic radial tyre comprising: a cross-sectional profile wherein, when mounted on a designated wheel rim, inflated to a specified pressure, and under no load, a rim breadth RW of the designated wheel rim relative to a maximum section width W satisfies RW/W≤0.7; and wherein, in that same cross-sectional profile under the same condition, a tread breadth TW relative to the maximum section width W satisfies 0.73<TW/W<0.8.

A bracing coupler for linking a spoke to a rim in a laminated wheel, the laminated wheel including a rim section forming a ring-shaped band centered on a rotational axis and defining a circumferential direction running about that axis and around the rim section, and a disc section including a round central boss and a set of struts extending along strut axes oriented radially relative to the circumferential direction, the struts running between the rim section and the boss so as to join them together, each strut presenting an outward-facing top surface, an opposed underside, and lateral flanks therebetween, the rim section containing a matching rim ply stack and each strut containing a matching strut ply stack, the bracing coupler comprising: at least one strut cradle having a bearing section wrapping around a terminal end of the strut ply stack about the strut axis and across the top surface of the strut ply stack, and at least two strut skirts extending over the flanks of the strut ply stack; and at least two rim lugs, each rim lug projecting from a strut skirt at a right angle to the strut axis, each rim lug adapted to be merged into the rim ply stack of the rim section of the laminated wheel; and wherein the coupler forms a unitary body whose fibre direction runs at a right angle to the strut axis.

A wheel-securing cap for an automotive hub, comprising: a central dome section; and a plurality of tabs arranged circumferentially along an outer edge of the dome section, each tab including a leading extremity, a trailing extremity, a lengthwise body running between the leading and trailing extremities, and an internal recess bounded by an inner wall and shaped to accept a wheel stud, wherein the leading extremities of the tabs lie in a common reference plane; wherein the dome section curves inwardly from a point along the lengthwise body of each tab toward the reference plane.

A drivetrain arrangement comprising: a hub bearing presenting a socket provided with inner grooves, a mounting face of the hub bearing presenting an aperture leading into the socket; and an axle shaft having a articulation casing and a spigot projecting from the articulation casing, the spigot being received within the socket of the hub bearing, the spigot having: a toothed section bearing a plurality of outer teeth engaged with the inner grooves; a collar situated between the toothed section and the articulation casing, the collar possessing a greatest outside dimension exceeding a root dimension of the inner grooves of the hub bearing; and an abutment face situated between the toothed section and the collar, the abutment face arranged to engage ends of the inner grooves of the hub bearing so as to prevent the articulation casing from advancing into contact with the mounting face; and
