query_text: A powertrain coupling arrangement comprising: a hub bearing forming a socket provided with inner toothing, an end face of the hub bearing exposing an aperture leading into the socket; and an axle assembly having a articulation casing and a spigot projecting from the articulation casing, the spigot situated inside the socket of the hub bearing, the spigot presenting: a toothed section bearing outer teeth engaged with the inner toothing; a collar positioned between the toothed section and the articulation casing, the collar possessing a largest outside dimension exceeding a root diameter of the inner toothing of the hub bearing; and an inclined abutment face positioned between the toothed section and the collar, the inclined abutment face contacting terminal ends of the inner toothing of the hub bearing to restrain the articulation casing from advancing into engagement with the end face; wherein the inclined abutment face is separated from the articulation casing by a first spacing, and the terminal ends of the inner toothing are separated from the end face by a second spacing, the first spacing being larger than the second spacing such that contact between the inclined abutment face and the terminal ends prevents the articulation casing from touching the end face.

A drivetrain coupling arrangement comprising: a hub bearing presenting a cavity furnished with inner keyways, a mounting surface of the hub bearing presenting an aperture leading into the cavity; and a driveshaft segment having a universal joint casing and a spigot projecting from the universal joint casing, the spigot lodged inside the cavity, the spigot comprising: a keyed section bearing a set of outer keys engaged with the inner keyways; a collar positioned between the keyed section and the universal joint casing, the collar exhibiting a largest outer dimension exceeding a root dimension of the inner keyways of the hub bearing; and an abutment face positioned between the keyed section and the collar, the abutment face bearing against terminal ends of the inner keyways of the hub bearing to prevent the universal joint casing from advancing into contact with the mounting surface; and an elastomeric gasket situated in a clearance formed between the mounting surface and the universal joint casing, the elastomeric gasket touching both the mounting surface and the universal joint casing.

A rotating hub assembly for an automobile, comprising: a casing defining an aperture configured to accept an axle journal of the automobile; a flange portion of the casing adapted to receive and retain a road wheel; a rolling element disposed within the aperture that permits the casing to turn relative to the journal; a monitoring module carried by the casing on a side of the rolling element away from the aperture and turning together with the casing, the monitoring module including a thermal transducer arranged to measure heat present outside the aperture; and transmitter electronics coupled to the thermal transducer that send, over a wireless link, heat readings usable to infer deterioration of the rolling element.

A castor unit comprising: a castor housing arrangement including a chassis member, a mounting base, and a stopper lever, the chassis member pivotally joined to the mounting base to permit a roller to rotate about a vertical axis relative to the mounting base, the stopper lever pivotally joined to the chassis member, the stopper lever to contact the roller when the stopper lever occupies a locking orientation; a rod having a proximal extremity and a distal extremity opposite the proximal extremity, the distal extremity to couple with the stopper lever; and a actuating arm having a first terminal portion and a second terminal portion opposite the first terminal portion, the actuating arm to swing relative to the castor housing arrangement between a primary orientation and a secondary orientation, displacement of the actuating arm to the primary orientation to cause the second terminal portion to drive the rod in a forward direction to move the stopper lever to the locking orientation to inhibit rotation of the roller, displacement of the actuating arm to the secondary orientation to cause the second terminal portion to drive the rod in a reverse direction to move the stopper lever to a freed orientation to permit rotation of the roller, the reverse direction opposite the forward direction.

A material-handling trolley comprising: a trolley chassis; and a set of swivel mounts, each swivel mount including: a roller; a swivel housing and a stopper lever, the roller attached to the swivel housing, the stopper lever pivotably attached to the swivel housing, the stopper lever shiftable between a locking orientation and a freeing orientation, the stopper lever pressing against the roller when in the locking orientation to inhibit turning of the roller relative to the swivel housing, the stopper lever releasing the roller when in the freeing orientation to permit turning of the roller relative to the swivel housing; a rod having a proximal extremity extending partly through the trolley chassis and a distal extremity opposite the proximal extremity extending partly through the swivel housing; and an actuating bar pivotably connected to the trolley chassis, the actuating bar including a grip and a lobe, the actuating bar moving the stopper lever between a locking orientation restricting turning of the roller relative to the trolley chassis and a freeing orientation permitting turning of the roller relative to the trolley chassis via the lobe and the rod when the actuating bar is pivoted relative to the trolley chassis.

A rolling support device comprising: a structure enabling a roller to turn about an axis; a retainer coupled to the structure that is movable to a blocking state preventing the roller from turning and to an unblocked state permitting the roller to turn; a transmission linking the retainer to the structure so that the retainer shifts between the blocking state and the unblocked state; and an actuator pivotally mounted to the structure, wherein displacement of the actuator between a first orientation and a second orientation induces the retainer to shift between the blocking state and the unblocked state through the transmission.

A tire-use elastomeric mixture, the mixture including: a rubber matrix component; particulate amorphous silica; an organosilane bonding promoter; a salt of a long-chain carboxylic acid with a metal; and an alkyl silane; wherein the rubber matrix component includes between 60 and 95 weight percent of a modified conjugated diene elastomer, which is prepared by coupling a polyorganosiloxane to a living terminus of a conjugated diene polymer chain, the polymer chain being built by joining a first living block to a second living block, the first living block consisting of 80 to 95 weight percent isoprene and 5 to 20 weight percent of a vinyl aromatic compound, possessing a living terminus, and having a number average... weight average molecular mass of 500 to 15000, and the second living block comprising 1,3-butadiene and a vinyl aromatic compound and possessing a living terminus; and the amorphous silica exhibits a CTAB surface area of at least 185 square meters per gram and is present in an amount of 55 to 90 parts by weight per 100 parts by weight of the rubber matrix component.

A pneumatic tread arrangement exhibiting non-mirror-symmetric geometry relative to a median plane perpendicular to the rotational axis, the arrangement comprising: a first outboard rib-like region, a first peripheral channel, an inner intermediate block region, a second peripheral channel, a central block region, a third peripheral channel, a second intermediate block region, a fourth peripheral channel, and a second outboard rib-like region sequentially arranged from a vehicle-facing inboard side; the central block region incorporating a plurality of central incisions oriented transversely across the tread, at least one of which exhibits a beveled section along at least one of its leading and trailing margins in the peripheral direction; the first intermediate block region incorporating a plurality of intermediate incisions oriented transversely across the tread, and at least one of which exhibits a beveled section along at least one of its leading and trailing margins in the peripheral direction.

A truck-type pneumatic tyre comprising: an outboard-positioned rib of a tread band that extends continuously about a rotational axis, is disposed axially away from a mid-circumferential plane, and is pierced by a multiplicity of incisions; each incision being bounded by two opposed faces, a central surface located midway between said faces, a transverse dimension of between 0.4 mm and 2.0 mm, and a radial penetration reaching at least 40% of a tread thickness; each incision including at least one segment that is displaced inwardly from the radially exterior edge of the incision and that extends along the incision's length in a wave-like pattern which, when viewed radially, forms arcs or single teeth; a reference surface passing through the location of greatest displacement of said segment intersects the central surface along a trace that conforms to the wave-like pattern; wherein each incision adopts the wave-like pattern solely within said segment, and wherein the amplitude of said trace diminishes, over every half-period of the wave, toward the tread-exterior terminus of the incision; and wherein said tyre is adapted for heavy goods vehicles.

A truck-type pneumatic tyre comprising: an outboard-positioned tread band element extending continuously around the circumference and situated axially beside the equatorial mid-plane of the tyre, the band element being penetrated by a set of narrow incisions, each incision bounded by opposed faces, a central plane lying equidistant between the faces, a breadth of 0.4 mm to 2.0 mm, and a greatest penetration along the radial direction amounting to no less than forty percent of the overall tread thickness; each incision possessing at least one sub-region displaced inwardly from the outer radial boundary of the incision and extending along the incision in a wave-like pattern that assumes an arc-shaped or single-tooth profile in the radial direction; a reference surface passing through the location of greatest displacement of the sub-region meeting the central plane along a boundary curve that mirrors the wave-like pattern; wherein the incision follows the wave-like pattern solely within the sub-region, and the amplitude of the boundary curve diminishes, across each half-period of the wave, toward the tread-exterior terminus of the incision; and wherein one or more of the incisions originate at an outer face of the band element and are each located within a web of the band element formed in a transverse groove, the web extending across most of the groove and presenting an upper face lying, relative to the outer face of the band element and measured at its lowest point along the radial direction, at a depth of 1.0 mm to 10.0 mm, particularly 2.0 mm to 5.0 mm.

A tyre comprising: a tread section; a pair of sidewall sections extending radially inward from the tread section; an indicia element projecting from a face of at least one of the sidewall sections and bearing a character, glyph, or pictorial design; an interface line between the indicia element and the face of the at least one of the sidewall sections; a multitude of minute projections whose elevation is less than an elevation of the indicia element; a first zone bounded on the indicia element side of the interface line and furnished with the minute projections; and a second zone bounded on the face side of the at least one of the sidewall sections of the interface line and devoid of the minute projections.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: an indicia section situated on an exterior face of a sidewall region; and a transponder unit, wherein the indicia section includes one or more indicia, each indicium presents a character, a sign, or an illustration and projects outward in a raised form, and at least a portion of the transponder unit is sunk within at least one of the one or more indicia.

An automotive hubcap assembly, comprising: a mounting member secured to a road wheel of a motor vehicle; a movable shield carried by and joined to the mounting member and operable between an open position and a closed position; a thermally responsive actuator applying a first biasing load on the movable shield, the first biasing load varying with ambient heat; and a rotation-responsive actuator applying a second biasing load on the movable shield, the second biasing load varying with rotational velocity of the road wheel, wherein the movable shield moves between the open position and the closed position in response to the first biasing load produced by the thermally responsive actuator and the second biasing load produced by the rotation-responsive actuator.

An automotive hubcap assembly, comprising: a mounting structure secured to a road wheel alongside a brake apparatus; a movable shield joined to the mounting structure and adapted to pivot between open and closed positions; a heat-reactive resilient component forming a first biasing mechanism that exerts a first load on the movable shield, the heat-reactive resilient component producing a non-proportional first resilient load across a defined temperature span; and a spring-type biasing element forming a second biasing mechanism that exerts a second load on the movable shield, the spring-type biasing element producing a second resilient load that varies proportionally with a change in its extension, wherein the movable shield is pivoted between the open and closed positions in response to the combined first and second loads.

A wheel assembly comprising: a hub member positioned at a center; a disc portion projecting radially from said hub member and including an interior section; said hub member including a tubular body having an inboard rim and an outboard rim, the inboard rim projecting inwardly past said disc portion; and a retaining band encircling the exterior face of said inwardly projecting section of said tubular body.

A process for building a wheel for a motor vehicle, the wheel including a mounting core, a disc member projecting outward from said core, said core including a tubular member having an outboard extremity and an inboard extremity, a collar fixed at said outboard extremity, said collar fastened to said disc member, said tubular member projecting inboard, the process comprising: releasing said collar from said disc member; placing a retaining ring about said inboard-projecting tubular member so that it abuts said disc member; and joining said retaining ring to said tubular member using fastening hardware.

A caster assembly, comprising: a housing configured to mount the assembly to a device; at least one roller mounted to the housing, the roller being rotatable around a roller axis; wherein the housing is arranged to pivot around a pivot axis that runs transverse to the roller axis, thereby altering the angular position of the roller relative to the pivot axis; and a restraint mechanism that is movable between a free condition and a fixed condition, wherein in the free condition the restraint mechanism permits pivoting of the housing around the pivot axis, and in the fixed condition the restraint mechanism prevents pivoting of the housing around the pivot axis, such that the angular position of the roller is fixed with respect to the pivot axis.

A storage apparatus for holding an implement, comprising: an enclosure adapted to retain an implement, the enclosure presenting a first face and an oppositely oriented second face, the second face forming a lower surface; and a mobility mechanism secured to the enclosure, the mobility mechanism including: a pin displaceable between a first location and a second location, a carrier member joined beneath the lower surface of the second face, projecting outwardly from the enclosure and bearing a plurality of openings, at least one of the openings serving as a pivot axis and at least one of the openings configured to accept the pin, a roller, and a pivot lever having a first extremity, a second extremity, and a plurality of openings, wherein the first extremity accepts the pin through at least one of its openings and is hingedly connected to the carrier member while the second extremity is rotatably mounted to the roller, the pivot lever being movable vertically between an elevated disposition and a lowered disposition relative to the lower surface, wherein the roller and pivot lever occupy the elevated disposition when the pin is at the first location and the roller and pivot lever occupy the lowered disposition when the pin is at the second location.

A rolling support apparatus comprising: a pin shiftable between a first location and a second location; a mounting plate having a bracket section that includes a plurality of openings, wherein at least one of the openings serves as a pivot axis and at least one of the openings is sized to accept the pin; a roller; and a pivot member having a leading end, a trailing end, and a plurality of holes, wherein the leading end engages the pin through at least one of the holes and is hingedly joined to the bracket section, while the trailing end is turnably joined to the roller, the pivot member being vertically displaceable between a raised state and a lowered state relative to the mounting plate, wherein the roller and pivot member occupy the raised state when the pin is at the first location and the roller and pivot member occupy the lowered state when the pin is at the second location.

A mobile storage cabinet apparatus comprising: an enclosure adapted to hold an implement, the enclosure presenting a first face and an opposing second face, the second face forming a lower surface; and a height-changing roller mechanism secured to the enclosure, the roller mechanism including a pin shiftable between an upper detent and a lower detent, a bracket projecting laterally from the lower surface of the second face, a rolling castor, and a pivoting lever having a proximal extremity and a distal extremity, wherein the proximal extremity is joined to the bracket and the distal extremity is rotatably joined to the castor by the pin, the castor being vertically displaceable between an elevated stance and a lowered stance relative to the lower surface of the second face, wherein the castor occupies the elevated stance when the pin is at the upper detent and the castor occupies the lowered stance when the pin is at the lower detent.

A technique for changing the elevation of a cabinet equipped with a height-adjustable caster arrangement, the technique comprising: slackening a fastener on the caster arrangement, the fastener initially situated in a first placement and displaceable between the first placement and a second placement, the caster arrangement occupying an elevated configuration while the fastener remains in the first placement; pivoting the fastener from the first placement into the second placement, the caster arrangement assuming a lowered configuration once the fastener sits in the second placement; and re-securing the fastener in the second placement by applying a clamping preload.

A pneumatic vehicle covering comprising: a sensing transponder assembly situated between an inner elastomeric stratum and an outer elastomeric stratum; wherein the inner stratum consists of 100 phr of at least one unsaturated hydrocarbon elastomer, at least one reinforcing particulate, and a vulcanizing system, and exhibits a T50 cure interval at 160° C. of roughly 1.5 to roughly 3.5 minutes; wherein the outer stratum consists of at least one unsaturated hydrocarbon elastomer, at least one reinforcing particulate, and a vulcanizing system, and exhibits a T50 cure interval at 160° C. (T50-2) exceeding T50-1 and of roughly 2.5 to roughly 5 minutes; wherein each of the inner and outer strata independently possesses a gauge of roughly 0.4 to roughly 3 mm; wherein the unsaturated hydrocarbon elastomer of the inner stratum comprises a predominant weight fraction of polybutadiene, polyisoprene, natural rubber, or blends thereof, together with no more than 10 phr combined of EPDM, butyl rubber, halobutyl rubber, or nitrile rubber; wherein the unsaturated hydrocarbon elastomer of the outer stratum comprises a predominant weight fraction of polyisoprene, natural rubber, styrene-butadiene rubber, or blends thereof, together with no more than 10 phr combined of EPDM, butyl rubber, halobutyl rubber, or nitrile rubber; wherein the reinforcing particulate of the inner stratum comprises roughly 30 to roughly 50 phr carbon black, and the reinforcing particulate of the outer stratum comprises roughly 30 to roughly 50 phr of a material selected from carbon black, silica, and mixtures thereof; and wherein the vulcanizing system of the inner stratum comprises elemental sulfur and at least one accelerator in a weight ratio of accelerator to sulfur of 0.7:1 to 1.5:1, and the vulcanizing system of the outer stratum comprises elemental sulfur and at least one accelerator in a weight ratio of accelerator to sulfur of no more than 0.6:1.

A pneumatic vehicle covering comprising: an electronic transponder unit having a wireless transceiver component interposed between an inner elastomeric stratum and an outer elastomeric stratum; wherein the inner elastomeric stratum consists of 100 phr of at least one unsaturated hydrocarbon polymer, at least one reinforcing particulate, and a vulcanization system, and exhibits a T50 scorch-to-cure interval T50-1 at 160° C. of roughly 1.5 to roughly 3.5 minutes; wherein the outer elastomeric stratum comprises at least one unsaturated hydrocarbon polymer, at least one reinforcing particulate, and a vulcanization system, and exhibits a T50 scorch-to-cure interval T50-2 at 160° C. exceeding T50-1 and ranging from roughly 2.5 to roughly 5 minutes; and wherein the inner and outer elastomeric strata each independently possess a thickness of roughly 0.4 to roughly 3 mm.

A process for vulcanizing a pneumatic tire fitted with a transponder unit, the process comprising: supplying a green tire casing and a transponder unit having a sealed interrogator element situated between an inner elastomeric stratum and an outer elastomeric stratum, wherein the inner stratum consists of 100 phr of at least one diene-based polymer, at least one reinforcing particulate, and a curing system, and exhibits a t50 scorch-to-cure time at 160° C. of roughly 1.5 to roughly 3.5 minutes; wherein the outer stratum comprises at least one diene-based polymer, at least one reinforcing particulate, and a curing system, and exhibits a t50 time at 160° C. (t50-2) exceeding t50-1 and falling between roughly 2.5 and roughly 5 minutes; wherein each stratum independently possesses a gauge of roughly 0.4 to roughly 3 mm; placing the sealed interrogator element against at least one part of the green tire casing; and subsequently curing the green tire casing together with the sealed interrogator element.

A tire ply structure, comprising: a stretched poly(ethylene terephthalate) filament bundle containing no less than 90 mole percent PET, the stretched filament bundle exhibiting a tenacity of at least 8.8 g/d and a 5% secant modulus of at least 2.8 g/d; a raw, undipped cord fabricated from the stretched filament bundle that, after thermal setting, displays a modulus enhancement potential of at least 110%; and a dip-treated, thermally set cord formed from the stretched filament bundle that, when held at 180° C. under a 0.05 g/dtex pre-tension for two minutes, yields a shrink force not exceeding 0.20 g/dtex.

A pneumatic cover designed for mounting on a power-assisted two-wheeler or wheelchair, the cover comprising: a belt structure situated radially inward of a running surface, said running surface being joined to a pair of bead cores through a pair of lateral walls; wherein the cover includes, along at least one of the lateral walls and projecting outward therefrom, a band formed of an elastomeric blend having an axial dimension (ep), measured normal to the lateral wall, at least 1 mm and no more than 4 mm, and a radial extent (Hr), measured normal to the rotational axis of the cover, at least 10 mm and no more than 30 mm; wherein the elastomeric blend of the band exhibits a Shore A durometer reading between 55 and 75 and a glass transition temperature between −15° C. and 0° C.; and wherein the elastomeric blend of the band defines a non-textured exterior face configured to engage a drive roller carrying a plurality of projecting engagement members.

A pneumatic vehicle tyre incorporating an electronic transponder unit enclosed within an elastomeric envelope, the envelope comprising: 100 parts by weight of at least one diene elastomer; at least one reinforcing particulate material; and a curing system, wherein the envelope exhibits a T50 vulcanization time at 160° C. of roughly 1.5 to roughly 3 minutes and a wall thickness of roughly 0.4 to roughly 3 mm, wherein the diene elastomer predominantly by weight comprises polybutadiene, polyisoprene, natural rubber, or blends thereof, and includes no more than 10 parts in aggregate of EPDM, butyl elastomer, halobutyl elastomer, or nitrile rubber; wherein the particulate material comprises roughly 30 to roughly 50 phr of carbon black; and wherein the curing system comprises elemental sulfur as crosslinking agent and at least one cure accelerator in a weight ratio of accelerator to sulfur of 0.7:1 to 1.5:1.

A pneumatic tyre incorporating an electronic transponder unit, the transponder being encased within an elastomeric sheath comprising: 100 parts by weight of at least one diene elastomer; at least one reinforcing particulate; and a vulcanization system, wherein the sheath exhibits a T50 scorch-to-cure interval at 160° C. of roughly 1.5 to roughly 3 minutes; and a wall gauge of roughly 0.4 to roughly 3 mm.

A process for vulcanizing a pneumatic tire incorporating an electronic transponder, the process comprising: furnishing a green tire body and a transponder assembly having a sealed interrogator element encased in an elastomeric sheath formed from 100 phr of at least one diene-based elastomer, a reinforcing particulate, and a curative system, the sheath exhibiting a T50 scorch-to-cure interval at 160° C. of roughly 1.5 to 3 minutes and a wall dimension of approximately 0.4 to 3 mm; situating the sealed interrogator element in contact with at least one structural portion of the green tire body; and thereafter vulcanizing the green tire body jointly with the sealed interrogator element.

An acoustic damping apparatus, comprising: a Helmholtz-type attenuator having a pliable, conduit-like attenuator housing with a proximal extremity, a distal extremity, and a passage placing the proximal extremity in fluid communication with the distal extremity, the attenuator housing coiled entirely about a rim-mounted hub of an automotive wheel at least once and arranged to dampen noise generated inside an interior void of a pneumatic tire of the automotive wheel.

A wheel assembly, comprising: a rim member; a pneumatic covering secured to the rim member and bounding an enclosed void; and an acoustic damper including a pliable, conduit-like damper body having a leading extremity, a trailing extremity, and a passage placing the leading extremity in fluid communication with the trailing extremity, the damper body coiled entirely around the rim member at least once, the acoustic damper embodied as a quarter-wave resonator whose tuned frequency depends on a span of the damper body and approximates a tonal frequency generated by the covering contacting a road surface, whereby the acoustic damper attenuates noise generated within the void.

A noise-dampening assembly, comprising: a set of acoustic chambers, each acoustic chamber including a pliable, conduit-like body possessing an intake extremity, an outlet extremity, and a passage placing the intake extremity in fluid communication with the outlet extremity, each of the conduit-like bodies coiled about a wheel hub of an automotive wheel at least once and operable to attenuate acoustic energy generated inside an enclosed void of a tire of the automotive wheel.

A technique for assessing an oscillatory property of a non-pneumatic wheel, comprising: obtaining, by a processor, contact-patch motion readings from a transducer affixed to a web member of a non-pneumatic wheel within a portion of the wheel, wherein the motion readings encompass signals gathered by the transducer across a time window during which a ground-engaging band running around a circumference of that portion makes contact with a road face; acquiring, by the processor, rotational speed information for the wheel across the time window; acquiring, by the processor, vertical force information borne by the wheel across the time window; and deriving, by the processor, an averaged oscillatory metric for the wheel from the motion readings, the rotational speed information, and the vertical force information.

A non-pneumatic wheel assembly, comprising: a vibration sensor affixed to a web member of the airless wheel within a segment of the wheel; and a processor operatively linked to the vibration sensor, the processor programmed to: obtain road-interface vibration signals from the vibration sensor, wherein the road-interface vibration signals include signal samples acquired by the vibration sensor across a time interval during which a ground-engaging band running around a perimeter of the segment engages a ground surface; obtain speed readings for the wheel across the time interval; obtain vertical loading readings for the wheel across the time interval; and derive an average vibratory metric for the wheel from the road-interface vibration signals, the speed readings, and the vertical loading readings.

An apparatus for pre-coiling a seat-belt retractor and fitting a stopper component, comprising a indexing turntable, the indexing turntable being furnished with a feeding location, a coiling location, a catch-notch locating location, a stopper mounting location, a rejected-part ejection location, and an acceptable-part ejection location; each location being equipped with a contour-matched holder, and a pawl base having an adjustable rotational sense being mounted beneath each contour-matched holder, a central axis of the pawl base carrying a ratchet spindle whose upper extremity passes through the contour-matched holder and couples with a spool shaft of the seat-belt retractor seated on the contour-matched holder; a coiling assembly being disposed beneath the coiling location, the coiling assembly being mounted on an equipment deck and situated under the pawl base at the coiling location, the coiling assembly comprising a first elevating unit and a first drive unit furnished with positional and torque feedback, the first elevating unit raising and lowering the first drive unit, an output extremity of the first drive unit carrying a bushing which, when the first elevating unit is raised, engages a lower end of the ratchet spindle for transmission so that the first drive unit rotates the ratchet spindle, and which, when the first elevating unit is lowered, disengages from the ratchet spindle; the coiling assembly further being disposed beneath the catch-notch locating location, a position sensing unit being mounted above the contour-matched holder at the catch-notch locating location, the position sensing unit comprising an upright bracket, a second elevating unit, a mounting plate, a displacement transducer, a slide member, and a sensing pin; the upright bracket being fixed to the equipment deck, the second elevating unit and the displacement transducer being secured to the upright bracket, an output extremity of the second elevating unit carrying the mounting plate, the mounting plate slidably engaging the slide member along a vertical direction, an upper stop structure and a lower stop structure being installed between the slide member and the mounting plate, and resilient members being installed between the lower stop structure and the mounting plate; the slide member being coupled to a sensing shaft of the displacement transducer; a bottom of the slide member carrying the sensing pin, the sensing pin having a cross-sectional profile identical to that of a pin of the stopper and a cross-sectional dimension not less than that of the stopper pin, the sensing pin being positioned above a receptacle formed in a housing of the seat-belt retractor at the catch-notch locating location; and the stopper mounting location being furnished with a multi-axis robotic arm and a vibratory feeder bowl, the vibratory feeder bowl conveying the stoppers.

A hubcap assembly, comprising: a shell body; a graphic laminate applied at a primary region of the shell body, the graphic laminate being built up from a stack of image sheets, wherein at least one sheet of the stack is positioned at a distinct depth relative to remaining sheets of the stack; and a series of ventilation apertures arranged in a patterned array at a secondary region of the shell body, the secondary region being spaced apart from the primary region, wherein, upon rotation and light exposure of the hubcap assembly, the graphic laminate produces a three-dimensional visual image.

A hubcap assembly, comprising: a shell; an ornamental coating applied at a initial region of the shell, the ornamental coating being built up from multiple stacked picture strata, wherein at least one stratum of the multiple stacked picture strata sits at a first distance beneath the remaining strata; and a series of heat-dissipating apertures arranged in a repeating design and situated at a secondary region of the shell, the secondary region being distinct from the initial region.

A technique for fabricating an automotive hubcap, comprising: positioning a substrate; applying a decorative overlay at a primary region of the substrate, the overlay being built up from a series of stacked imagery strata, wherein at least one stratum of the series is situated at a first spacing from the remaining strata; and creating a set of perforations arranged in a patterned configuration at a secondary region of the substrate, the secondary region being spatially distinct from the primary region.

An encircling covering element for enclosing vehicle rims, the element comprising: a textile strip shaped as a closed loop and thus defining a perimeter path due to its ring configuration, the strip being dimensioned to envelop and wrap an outer portion of a vehicle rim; wherein the textile strip possesses a middle zone extending along the perimeter path and at least one edge zone abutting the middle zone along that same perimeter path, the at least one abutting edge zone exhibiting a mass-per-area figure smaller than the mass-per-area figure of the middle zone within that same strip; wherein the strip further maintains uninterrupted fibrous continuity where the middle zone meets the at least one abutting edge zone, the strip being produced as a single unitary fabric body.

A process for producing a protective wheel-enclosing sock, the process comprising: positioning and feeding longitudinal threads from a beam and transverse threads from a bobbin rack, the beam and the rack being arranged relative to one another so as to form a textile strip; varying the quantity or characteristics of the longitudinal threads fed along one beam such that the textile strip exhibits differing mass per unit area across its extent according to that variation; and forming a loop-shaped configuration from the strip.

A transportable equipment carrier arrangement for use with a worksite container held upon runners, the runners each consisting of an unclosed multisided framework possessing a runner floor panel and runner wall panels, the arrangement comprising: (a) a top panel portion, a bottom panel portion, and a shut terminal portion; (b) a channel formed between said top panel portion and said bottom panel portion; and (c) a roller assembly coupled to said bottom panel portion.

A detachable wheel mounting system for a field equipment enclosure, comprising: (a) an equipment enclosure carried upon a set of runners, each of said runners formed as an open multisided framework possessing a runner floor panel and runner wall panels; (b) a set of detachable rolling mounts, each said mount of said set including an upper panel portion, a terminal end portion, and a lower panel portion presenting an underside face, a rolling module secured to said underside face of said lower panel portion, and a receiving channel formed between said upper panel portion and said lower panel portion; and (c) wherein said runner floor panel of each of said runners is received within said receiving channel of a chosen detachable rolling mount selected from said set of detachable rolling mounts.

A technique for equipping a worksite container with detachable rolling modules, comprising: (a) furnishing a worksite container carried upon a series of runners, each runner of said series formed as an open multi-sided framework possessing a runner floor panel and runner flank panels; (b) furnishing a series of detachable rolling modules, each detachable rolling module of said series including a top panel portion, a sealed terminal portion, and a bottom panel portion exhibiting a lower face, a rolling member affixed to said lower face of said bottom panel portion, and a receptacle defined between said top panel portion and said bottom panel portion; (c) choosing one detachable rolling module from said series of detachable rolling modules; (d) advancing said receptacle of said chosen detachable rolling module over said runner floor panel of a designated runner of said worksite container with said bottom panel portion situated beneath said runner floor panel of said designated runner; and (e) reiterating steps (c) and (d) until one said detachable rolling module is fitted onto each said runner of said worksite container.

A radial-ply pneumatic tire for a vehicle, being a warm-weather tire or a four-season tire, comprising: a patterned tread having circumferentially extending series of tread blocks and/or tread ribs; wherein the aggregate count of incisions within each series of tread blocks and/or tread ribs does not exceed 150; wherein the tread is formed as one layer or as several layers, with an outermost radial tread layer spanning at least the full width of the road-contact region; wherein the groove depth of the tread is no greater than 6.5 mm; and wherein the tread, or its outermost radial tread layer, is made of a rubber compound having a Shore A durometer hardness at ambient temperature per DIN ISO 7619-1 between 40 ShA and 55 ShA.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, comprising: a first lateral flank; a second lateral flank; a running surface having a principal zone and an auxiliary zone; and a first molding joint line running between the first and second lateral flanks; wherein: the entire principal zone is situated no more than 20 mm from the first molding joint line, the entire auxiliary zone is situated no less than 25 mm from the first molding joint line, the principal zone includes principal cuts that are oriented non-circumferentially, and the auxiliary zone includes auxiliary cuts that are oriented non-circumferentially, an average depth of the principal cuts amounts to 75% to 110% of an average depth of the auxiliary cuts, and at least one of the principal cuts includes a blade-shaped principal cut having a reinforcing element that stiffens the blade in a circumferential direction of the covering, and/or a width of at least one of the principal cuts exceeds a width of one of the auxiliary cuts.

A tyre-forming die for producing a tread band, the die comprising: a set of sectors including a leading sector, the set of sectors movable between a closed configuration, in which the sectors abut one another to define a ring-shaped cavity for an uncured carcass, and an open configuration, in which the sectors are separated from one another to allow extraction of a moulded tyre; the leading sector including: a leading edge and an trailing edge situated opposite the leading edge; a near-edge zone lying no more than 20 mm from the leading edge, the entirety of the near-edge zone; a mid-span zone lying at least 25 mm from both the leading edge and the trailing edge, the entirety of the mid-span zone; first sipes disposed within the near-edge zone that are oblique to the circumferential direction; and second sipes disposed within the mid-span zone that are oblique to the circumferential direction; wherein: the first sipes include a first near-edge sipe, the second sipes include a first mid-span sipe, an average height of the first sipes amounts to between 75% and 110% of an average height of the second sipes, and a resistance of the first sipes to flexing in the circumferential direction of the die exceeds a resistance of the second sipes to flexing in the circumferential direction of the die.

A tyre assembly comprising: a pair of bead regions, each furnished with a bead wire and a filler element that projects radially outward from the bead wire while narrowing in thickness; and a toroidal framework including a cord layer extending between the bead regions and wrapped about the bead wire in each region from the inboard side to the outboard side so as to define a pair of folded segments and a body segment disposed therebetween, the folded segments extending radially outward along the outboard faces of the filler elements, respectively, wherein at least one of the bead regions carries a bead-stiffening elastomer positioned on the outboard side of the folded segment, the bead-stiffening elastomer includes a first stiffening elastomer ply and a second stiffening elastomer ply situated inboard of the first stiffening elastomer ply, and a complex modulus E*2 of the second stiffening elastomer ply is less than a complex modulus E*1 of the first stiffening elastomer ply.

An onboard arrangement for a motorized conveyance, configured to retain CO2 recovered from the conveyance's exhaust during travel, the arrangement comprising: a CO2 separation unit; a pressurizing device linked to the separation unit through a first conduit; and a wheel having an inner pocket and an outer pocket, the wheel being connected to the pressurizing device through a second conduit.

A process for managing gas storage in a vehicle tire, the process comprising: ascertaining that a primary compartment of a first tire is able to receive carbon dioxide; ascertaining that a secondary compartment of the first tire is able to vent ambient gas held therein; on the basis, at least partly, of the ascertaining that the primary compartment can receive carbon dioxide, delivering carbon dioxide under compression at a first pressure into the primary compartment until the primary compartment is no longer able to receive it; and permitting the ambient gas held within the secondary compartment to escape until the primary compartment reaches maximum fill, wherein each of the foregoing steps is performed in that order.

One or more tangible, non-volatile machine-readable media storing instructions that, when carried out by a processing device, direct performance of acts comprising: establishing that a first compartment inside a first wheel has room to receive CO2; establishing that a second compartment inside the same wheel is able to vent the gas held within it; in response to establishing that the first compartment can receive CO2, delivering CO2 under a first pressure into the first compartment until it reaches its limit, wherein the delivered CO2 originates from a sequestration arrangement that collects carbon dioxide from an engine's exhaust; and permitting the gas held in the second compartment to escape until the first compartment is completely filled.

A puncture-sealing coupling device, comprising: a housing having a first terminal and an opposing terminal, the first terminal serving as an attachment terminal, a passageway for air being formed within the housing and passing through the attachment terminal; and a hollow shaft having a first extremity and a second extremity, a conduit for fluid being formed inside the hollow shaft, the first extremity being seated within the opposing terminal of the housing with the conduit aligned with the passageway, the second extremity being a tapered tip, the tapered tip being formed with a retaining slot, and the retaining slot having an open mouth.

A trailer alignment apparatus for coupling a trailer to a towing vehicle, the apparatus comprising: a directional funnel affixed to a towing receiver of the towing vehicle, the funnel having a pivot joint; a first flange projecting outwardly from the pivot joint; and a second flange projecting outwardly from the pivot joint in spaced relation to the first flange, the first flange and the second flange being arranged to define a gap sized to accept a drawbar of the trailer; a plurality of detection elements mounted along the funnel, the detection elements being operable to generate measurement signals representative of an orientation between the towing vehicle and the trailer; and a control processor operable to obtain the measurement signals, identify a location of the drawbar within the gap relative to the first flange and the second flange, and convey the identified location to the towing vehicle.

A coupling-assist arrangement for towing, comprising: a towing machine having an attachment fitting mounted at a posterior extremity thereof; a towed cart including a drawbar situated at an anterior extremity thereof and adapted to mate with the attachment fitting; and an alignment carriage affixed to a towing fitting of the towing machine, the alignment carriage being structured to furnish a tolerance margin for joining the towing machine and the towed cart.

A technique for coupling a towing vehicle with a trailer, the technique comprising: sensing, using one or more detectors positioned on a guiding structure, measurement signals representative of a placement and a heading of the trailer with respect to the towing vehicle; computing, using an electronic controller, a location of a drawbar of the trailer in relation to a towing coupler of the towing vehicle from the measurement signals; and conveying the computed location of the drawbar to the towing vehicle.

A wheel hub-flange member for a motor vehicle, comprising: a longitudinal reference line; a transverse reference line orthogonal to said longitudinal reference line; a web portion that possesses: an interior-facing face directed toward a center; an exterior-facing face directed away from said center; and a wall depth measured between said interior-facing face and said exterior-facing face; a perforation passing through said web portion and sized to accept a wire element, wherein said perforation comprises: an interior mouth situated at said interior-facing face; an exterior mouth situated at said exterior-facing face; a bore wall extending between said interior mouth and said exterior mouth; and a bore centerline; wherein at least one of said interior-facing face and said exterior-facing face varies in depth to define a thicker zone encircling said perforation and a thinner zone angularly displaced from said thicker zone and having diminished wall depth relative to said thicker zone; wherein said exterior-facing face includes a downwardly set concavity adjacent said exterior mouth and situated within said thicker zone; and wherein at least a segment of said concavity serves as a seating surface for contact with said wire element and for carrying wire tensile loads.

A process for fabricating a wheel rim for an automotive vehicle, said rim being a preformed workpiece comprising: an axial direction; a radial direction orthogonal to said axial direction; a spoke-supporting web having an inward-facing side oriented toward the rotational center; an outward-facing side oriented away from the rotational center; and a wall thickness measured between said inward-facing side and said outward-facing side; wherein at least one of said inward-facing side and said outward-facing side varies in radial dimension so as to define a first thickened zone encircling a spoke aperture and a second zone of diminished thickness angularly displaced from said first thickened zone; said process comprising: (a) first shaping said rim into the preformed workpiece, and (b) thereafter either displacing or excising stock from said web adjacent said outward-facing side to produce a radially depressed face within said first thickened zone, at least part of said depressed face being arranged to furnish a seating face for mating with a wheel spoke and to carry spoke tensile loads therebetween.

A castor apparatus for a tubular support post, the apparatus comprising: a wheel mount assembly having a carrier segment, a swivel segment pivotally coupled to a lower extremity of the carrier segment, and a shield segment interposed between the carrier segment and the swivel segment; a fixing assembly secured to the carrier segment and configured to attach to the tubular support post; and a locking member passing through the shield segment and the carrier segment into the fixing assembly, and displaceable vertically with respect to the fixing assembly, the carrier segment, and the shield segment between a locked configuration, in which the locking member protrudes beyond the shield segment and abuts the swivel segment to prevent rotation thereof, and a released configuration, in which the locking member is withdrawn within the shield segment and separated from the swivel segment.

An apparatus forming a radial member for a airless wheel, the member including: an apex portion; a primary flange joined to and projecting away from the apex portion; a secondary flange joined to and projecting away from the apex portion, the primary flange and secondary flange being discrete components; a primary base section; a secondary base section; and a unitary, uninterrupted apex stiffener that couples with the primary flange, the secondary flange, the primary base section, and the secondary base section, the apex stiffener being situated between the primary flange and the primary base section and between the secondary flange and the secondary base section.

A wheel support member for a airless tire, comprising: a central junction; a leading web joined to and extending outward from the central junction; a trailing web joined to and extending outward from the central junction; a leading base; a trailing base; and a lengthened junction reinforcer that bonds with the leading web, the trailing web, the leading base, and the trailing base, wherein the lengthened junction reinforcer lies between the leading web and the leading base, wherein the lengthened junction reinforcer lies between the trailing web and the trailing base; wherein the leading base presents a leading bonding face, a first leading hollow surface, and a second leading hollow surface, wherein the second leading hollow surface ends at the lengthened junction reinforcer; wherein the trailing base presents a trailing bonding face, a first trailing hollow surface, and a second trailing hollow surface, wherein the second trailing hollow surface ends at the lengthened junction reinforcer.

A support member for an airless wheel, the support member including: a central junction; a leading flank coupled to the central junction and projecting outwardly therefrom; a trailing flank coupled to the central junction and projecting outwardly therefrom; a left base portion; a right base portion; and an elongated junction brace that couples with the leading flank, the trailing flank, the left base portion, and the right base portion, wherein the elongated junction brace is positioned between the leading flank and the left base portion, wherein the elongated junction brace is positioned between the trailing flank and the right base portion; wherein the left base portion couples with the leading flank and does not couple with the trailing flank, and wherein the right base portion couples with the trailing flank and does not couple with the leading flank.

A pneumatic vehicle covering comprising: an outer contact layer adapted to engage a roadway; a reinforcing ply disposed radially beneath the contact layer; and a circumferential restraint layer interposed radially between the contact layer and the reinforcing ply and laid over the reinforcing ply, wherein the reinforcing ply incorporates a multitude of mutually parallel filaments oriented obliquely to a circumferential direction, the restraint layer comprises a filament extending substantially along the circumferential direction, the filament is an organic fiber strand, the restraint layer is formed from a spirally wrapped ribbon, the ribbon is a filament array in which a plurality of the strands are juxtaposed, a region extending from a first edge to a second edge of the reinforcing ply constitutes a regulated zone in which strand tension is controlled, residual tension of the strands within the regulated zone is not less than 15.0 N, the regulated zone includes a central portion and a pair of flank portions situated axially outboard of the central portion, residual tension of the strands in the central portion exceeds residual tension of the strands in each flank portion, and a quotient of an equatorial footprint length measured along an equatorial plane of the covering on a reference footprint obtained by placing the covering in contact with a flat roadway under a vertical load equal to 70% of a nominal load of the covering, the covering being mounted on a nominal rim with its internal pressure adjusted to a nominal pressure and its camber angle set to 0°, to a reference footprint length at a location corresponding to a width equal to 80% of a maximum footprint width, is defined as a shape index, and the shape index is not less than 1.00 and not greater than 1.30.

A process for manufacturing a pneumatic vehicle covering, the process comprising: assembling an unvulcanized blank of the covering; and curing the unvulcanized blank, wherein during the assembling, a restraining layer is established by spirally wrapping a ribbon-like strip onto a reinforcing ply while imposing a tensile force on the strip, the strip is a filament arrangement in which a plurality of reinforcing filaments are aligned, a span extending between a first margin and a second margin of the reinforcing ply is a regulated region in which tension of the reinforcing filaments is governed, a force exerted on the reinforcing filaments in the regulated region is not less than 15.0 N, the regulated region comprises a central zone and a pair of flank zones situated axially outboard of the central zone, and a force exerted on the reinforcing filaments in the central zone exceeds a force exerted on the reinforcing filaments in each flank zone; and
