query_text: A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread section having a first ground-engaging edge; a shoulder groove running circumferentially alongside the first ground-engaging edge; a shoulder rib zone bounded between the shoulder groove and the first ground-engaging edge, the shoulder rib zone including a medial-side sector, a lateral-side sector, and a series of transverse shoulder sipes; wherein the medial-side sector is delimited toward the tyre equator from a midline location of the shoulder rib zone, the lateral-side sector is delimited away from the tyre equator from that midline location, each of the transverse shoulder sipes opens onto the first ground-engaging edge and extends axially therefrom at least within the lateral-side sector, and a mean contact pressure in the lateral-side sector exceeds a mean contact pressure in the medial-side sector when the tyre is mounted on a specified rim, inflated to a specified pressure, carrying a specified load, and pressed against a planar surface at zero camber.

A tyre having a running surface region that extends circumferentially in an annular configuration, a pair of flank regions positioned at opposite axial sides of the running surface region, a pair of bead regions located radially inward of the flank regions, and a directional marking denoting the orientation for installation on a motor vehicle; four circumferential channels being cut into the running surface region, the four channels including: a vehicle-proximal central channel situated on the inboard side of a tyre midplane when fitted to the vehicle; a vehicle-distal central channel situated on the outboard side of the midplane when fitted to the vehicle; a vehicle-proximal shoulder channel situated inboard of the vehicle-proximal central channel when fitted to the vehicle; and a vehicle-distal shoulder channel situated outboard of the vehicle-distal central channel when fitted to the vehicle, five rows of ribs being delimited by the four channels, the five rows including: a central rib bounded between the vehicle-proximal central channel and the vehicle-distal central channel; an inboard intermediate rib bounded between the vehicle-proximal central channel and the vehicle-proximal shoulder channel; an outboard intermediate rib bounded between the vehicle-distal central channel and the vehicle-distal shoulder channel; an inboard shoulder rib lying inboard of the vehicle-proximal shoulder channel; and an outboard shoulder rib lying outboard of the vehicle-distal shoulder channel, wherein a plurality of inboard transverse notches extending axially, each having one end opening into the vehicle-proximal central channel and another end terminating within the inboard intermediate rib, are spaced circumferentially within the inboard intermediate rib, a plurality of outboard transverse notches extending axially, each having one end opening into the vehicle-distal shoulder channel and another end terminating within the outboard intermediate rib, are spaced circumferentially within the outboard intermediate rib, a length L1 of each inboard transverse notch and a length L2 of each outboard transverse notch satisfy L1 > L2, a distance W1 from the midplane to a center line of the vehicle-proximal shoulder channel, a distance W2 from the midplane to a center line of the vehicle-proximal central channel, a distance W3 from the midplane to a center line of the vehicle-distal central channel, and a distance W4 from the midplane to a center line of the vehicle-distal shoulder channel satisfy 0.58≤W1/Wi≤0.62, 0.20≤W2/Wi≤0.24, 0.15≤W3/Wo≤0.19, and 0.53≤W4/Wo≤0.57, where Wi and Wo denote distances from the midplane to ground contact edges on the vehicle-proximal and vehicle-distal sides, respectively, and a sum of a groove width WG1 of the vehicle-proximal shoulder channel and a groove width WG2 of the vehicle-proximal central channel is greater than a sum of a groove width WG3 of the vehicle-distal central channel and a groove width WG4 of the vehicle-distal shoulder channel.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, comprising: a raised section extending outwardly along a lateral axis from an exterior surface of a side wall region; and a wireless transponder integrated within the raised section.

An air-retaining wheel liner assembly comprising: a core element formed from a first cellular polymer; and a peripheral element formed from a second cellular polymer having a density greater or lesser than that of the first cellular polymer; wherein the peripheral element defines an interiorly directed recess dimensioned to receive the core element.

A road wheel assembly comprising a pneumatic-free tire liner, the liner having a core member formed from a first cellular polymer, and a peripheral member formed from a second cellular polymer, the second cellular polymer exhibiting a greater or smaller bulk density than the first cellular polymer; wherein the peripheral member defines an inward-opening groove dimensioned to receive the core member.

A motor transport apparatus comprising a road wheel fitted with a tyreless liner, the liner including a core section formed from a first cellular polymer, and a peripheral section formed from a second cellular polymer whose bulk density is greater or lesser than that of the first cellular polymer; wherein the peripheral section defines an inwardly open groove dimensioned to receive the core section.

A trailer-coupling lift arrangement, comprising: a) a lifting unit, designed to attach to a towing hitch receiver of an automobile; and b) a carriage base, designed to be releasably joined to the lifting unit, wherein the carriage base is adapted to hold a load item for conveyance.

A trailer-coupling lifting apparatus, comprising a lifting unit adapted to be removably secured to a receiver of a motor vehicle, such that the lifting unit is capable of receiving a removable attachment of a lifting accessory unit; wherein the lifting unit comprises: a) a first support section, which includes a first hollow tubular housing defining a first internal cavity; and b) a second support section, which includes a second tubular housing; wherein at least a top segment of the second tubular housing is arranged to telescopically slide within the first internal cavity of the first hollow tubular housing.

A method of operating a lifting coupling apparatus, comprising: a) loading a freight article onto a lift coupling unit of the apparatus; b) bringing into vertical correspondence a level of a trailing attachment element of the lift coupling unit, by raising or lowering a lower extension body with respect to an upper extension body of the lift coupling unit, such that the trailing attachment element is positioned in vertical registration with a leading coupling connector of a lifting base; and c) joining the lift coupling unit to the lifting base, by engaging the trailing attachment element with the leading coupling connector.

A towing-port insert for flat-tow installations, comprising: a single-piece body including a round leading section, a substantially box-shaped trailing section, a first elongated shank projecting from an underside of said round leading section to a second elongated shank; wherein said second elongated shank extends between an underside of said first elongated shank and an upper extremity of said substantially box-shaped trailing section; wherein said first elongated shank presents a first span and said second elongated shank presents a second span; wherein said first span measures between six and twelve times said second span; and further wherein said insert is a protective closure for shielding a sunken zone configured to receive a towing bar of a recreational vehicle on a motor vehicle.

A flat-towing receptacle sealing plug comprising: a sealing plug body of unitary construction having a leading section, a substantially angular trailing section, a first shank running from a lower face of said leading section to a second shank; wherein said leading section possesses a roughly round profile with an upper face of a smaller upper width and a lower face of a larger lower width; wherein said leading section narrows in a conical fashion between said upper face and said lower face; wherein said leading section furnishes a handhold enabling an operator to manipulate said sealing plug; wherein said second shank extends between said lower face of said first shank and an upper extremity of said substantially angular trailing section; wherein said first shank has a first extent and said second shank has a second extent; wherein said first extent of said first shank measures between six and twelve times said second extent of said second shank; and further wherein said sealing plug serves as a shield for closing off a sunken zone employed for housing a motorhome towing bar on a motor vehicle.

A technique for shielding flat-tow receptacle cavities, the technique comprising: supplying a matched set of shielding plugs; each said plug possessing an upper segment, a substantially squared lower segment, an elongated barrel coupling a base face of the upper segment to an intermediate barrel; the upper segment being substantially round and presenting an upper face of a first measure and a base face of a second measure, the first measure being smaller than the second measure, the upper segment further exhibiting a conical taper between the upper face and the base face; the intermediate barrel extending from the base face of the elongated barrel to an apex of the substantially squared lower segment; the elongated barrel having a first extent and the intermediate barrel having a second extent, the first extent exceeding the second extent; gripping the upper segment as a handhold for an operator to seat and withdraw the plug from a cavity of a vehicle; seating each said plug within a corresponding cavity of the vehicle while the vehicle is not under tow; and extracting each said plug from the corresponding cavity to admit an RV tow bar while the vehicle is under tow.

A bicycle wheel core arrangement comprising: a central rotatable member; and a set of spoke anchoring components; wherein the anchoring components are arranged in a pair of axially offset series encircling the rotatable member, wherein each anchoring component includes at least one aperture for accommodating at least a portion of at least one spoke, and wherein at least two neighboring anchoring components are linked by at least one connecting strut, wherein at least a section of said connecting strut exhibits a breadth narrower than a breadth of at least one anchoring component joined to said connecting strut.

A process for fabricating at least one bicycle wheel core, the process comprising: supplying a central hub body; and furnishing a multitude of spoke anchoring components; wherein the anchoring components are arranged in two axially offset circumferential series encircling the hub body, wherein each anchoring component includes at least one aperture for accommodating at least a portion of at least one spoke, and wherein at least two neighboring anchoring components are joined through at least one connecting strut, wherein at least a segment of said connecting strut exhibits a breadth less than a breadth of at least one anchoring component coupled to said connecting strut.

An apparatus for a ground-engaging rolling member, comprising: a primary driven element arranged to turn around a first pivot line; a force conveying element arranged to draw motive energy from the primary driven element; and an adjustable rolling element arranged to (i) take up a turning force from the force conveying element so as to spin around a second pivot line when the primary driven element turns, and (ii) shift in position relative to the primary driven element so that the first pivot line and the second pivot line either coincide with one another or are displaced apart from one another.

A sealing member for a tire-and-hub assembly having a pair of mating wheel segments, the sealing member comprising: a tubular element defining an internal void, a first terminal portion shaped to engage a first interior face of one wheel segment, a second terminal portion shaped to engage a second interior face of the other wheel segment, and one or more apertures; the tubular element including a sidewall through which the one or more apertures are arranged to divert foreign material away from the internal void while permitting moisture to exit the internal void through the one or more apertures, the tubular element being formed from a rubber-like polymeric composition.

A hub closure arrangement for a wheel, the closure arrangement comprising: a first felly segment presenting a first interior circumferential face; a first journal disposed within and encircled by the first felly segment; a second felly segment presenting a second interior circumferential face; a second journal disposed within and encircled by the second felly segment; and a pliable gasket possessing a tubular shell that defines an inner void, a first gasket terminus shaped to engage the first interior circumferential face of the first felly segment, and a second gasket terminus shaped to engage the second interior circumferential face of the second felly segment, the tubular shell of the pliable gasket encompassing a region lying between the first journal and the second journal.

A method of sealing a hub arrangement, the hub arrangement having a first wheel section defining a first interior face, a first rolling-element support disposed within the first wheel section, a second wheel section defining a second interior face, and a second rolling-element support disposed within the second wheel section; the method comprising: positioning, between the first wheel section and the second wheel section, a pliable gasket having a tubular member with an internal cavity, a first gasket terminus engaging the first interior face of the first wheel section, and a second gasket terminus engaging the second interior face of the second wheel section, the tubular member of the pliable gasket encircling a region located between the first rolling-element support and the second rolling-element support.

A caster mounting system for an article of furniture, comprising: a support body; a primary rolling caster having at least one roller and one carrier, wherein: the roller is journaled for turning about a first rotational axis on the carrier, the carrier is joined at least indirectly for pivoting about a second rotational axis on the support body, and the first rotational axis resides within a first reference plane while the second rotational axis extends orthogonally to the first reference plane; and a U-profiled retainer having a pair of arms and a crosspiece joining the arms, wherein: the arms are coupled at least indirectly for pivoting about a third rotational axis to the support body, which third rotational axis lies within the first reference plane or within a plane parallel thereto, the U-profiled retainer being swingable about the third rotational axis between an initial orientation and a secondary orientation, and the U-profiled retainer being shifted into the secondary orientation when the first rotational axis and the third rotational axis are substantially parallel or coincident, wherein: the roller in the secondary orientation is positioned between the arms of the U-profiled retainer such that unimpeded pivoting of the carrier about the second rotational axis is curtailed, and the roller in the initial orientation is positioned outside the arms of the U-profiled retainer such that unimpeded pivoting of the carrier about the second rotational axis is permitted, the U-profiled retainer is swung through an angle of less than 90° to transition from the initial orientation to the secondary orientation, and vice versa, and the caster mounting system further comprises retention members operable to maintain the U-profiled retainer in the initial orientation.

A heavy equipment vehicle, comprising: a drive spindle; a set of tires, each tire secured to an external terminus of the spindle and possessing a tubular casing running coaxially along the spindle; and a set of shielding modules, each shielding module fitted at an external terminus of the spindle, wherein each tire is attached to the spindle so as to overlie a respective shielding module, each shielding module including: a drive reducer carried in rotation at an external terminus of the spindle and incorporating a ring-shaped gasket spanning between moving and stationary parts of the reducer; a turning member coupled to a respective tire; a moving shield joined to the drive reducer; and a stationary shield secured to the spindle.

A procedure for running a heavy equipment vehicle, the procedure comprising: furnishing a vehicle possessing a drive unit mounted for rotation on a distal extremity of a spindle, and a tire attached to a distal extremity of the drive unit, the tire including a tubular casing running axially and coaxially around the spindle; enabling debris to enter an inside of a tire drum; impeding the debris from traveling through a first clearance between the spindle and a turning member coupled to the tire drum; confining the debris within a first chamber delimited by the spindle, the turning member, and an inner shield secured to the spindle; impeding the debris from traveling through a second clearance between the turning member and the inner shield, the second clearance becoming reachable by the debris once a first accumulated quantity of additional debris has collected within the first chamber; impeding the debris from traveling through a third clearance between the inner shield and a rotating shield; confining the debris within a second chamber delimited by the inner shield and the rotating shield; impeding the debris from traveling through a fourth clearance between the inner shield and the rotating shield, the third clearance becoming reachable by the debris once a second accumulated quantity of additional debris has collected within the second chamber; confining the debris within a third chamber delimited by the rotating shield, the inner shield, the spindle, and the drive unit; impeding the debris from traveling through a passageway formed between the turning member and the rotating shield, the passageway becoming reachable by the debris as an alternative route to the third clearance; impeding the debris from traveling through a fifth clearance between the turning member and a rotating shield; and allowing the debris to reach a sealing region contacting an annular gasket extending over the drive unit, or a surplus region separate from the sealing region.

A protective shield for a sealing member of a wheel-driven industrial vehicle, the shield comprising: a ring-shaped housing having a primary flange, a secondary flange possessing an upper section and a lower section, and a linking section spanning between the primary flange and the secondary flange; wherein the primary flange projects inwardly toward a center from the linking section and defines a plurality of apertures; wherein the upper section is shaped to enter a matching recess formed in a revolving member of a wheel of the wheel-driven industrial vehicle; and wherein the lower section is shaped to project toward a shaft of the wheel-driven industrial vehicle.

A tread compound for a pneumatic tire, the compound including a polymer matrix and a reinforcing filler; wherein the polymer matrix contains at least 5 wt% of a functionalized polybutadiene and at least 10 wt% of a non-functionalized polybutadiene; and the reinforcing filler is a furnace black exhibiting a CTAB surface area of 130 m2/g or greater, a CTAB-to-iodine number ratio of from 0.92 to 1.06 inclusive, and a hydrogen release content of 3,500 to 4,800 ppm by mass.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a pair of annular bead cores positioned at an axial separation from each other; a casing having at least one layer routed about both bead cores, each layer of the at least one layer delimiting a couple of folded-back extremities running from the bead cores to terminal points of each layer; first and second bead zones enveloped by the at least one layer so that the bead zones are laterally confined by the at least one layer and the folded-back extremities, and radially confined by innermost radial surfaces of the respective annular bead cores and outermost radial terminal points of the respective folded-back extremities; a belt arrangement located radially outside the casing, the belt arrangement including a radially innermost belt possessing first and second lateral end sections that terminate at respective first and second lateral margins of the radially innermost belt; and first and second sidewall rubber strips each extending along a face of the at least one layer from a leading end to a trailing end, the leading end situated axially inboard of a corresponding lateral margin of the radially innermost belt and radially between the at least one layer and a corresponding lateral end section of the radially innermost belt, the trailing end situated within a corresponding bead zone of the first and second bead zones.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a crown layer; a casing having at least one layer routed around first and second axially separated annular beads, each layer of the at least one layer delimiting a pair of folded-back terminations extending from the beads to outermost terminal points of each layer; a belt assembly situated between the casing and the crown layer, the belt assembly including a radially innermost reinforcing band with opposed first and second axial margins; a pair of flank portions, wherein radially outermost regions of each flank overlie axial end regions of the crown layer; a pair of bead zones each incorporating an annular bead of the first and second beads, wherein the casing extends about the pair of bead zones such that the zones are bordered axially by the at least one layer and the folded-back terminations, and bordered radially by radially innermost edges of the respective annular beads and radially outermost terminal points of respective folded-back terminations; and a pair of flank rubber strips, wherein a first flank rubber strip extends along a face of the at least one layer from a first extremity located axially inward of the first axial margin of the radially innermost reinforcing band to a second extremity within a first bead zone of the pair of bead zones, and wherein a second flank rubber strip extends along the face of the at least one layer from a first extremity located axially inward of the second axial margin of the first reinforcing band to a second extremity within a second bead zone of the pair of bead zones.

A tire for pneumatic inflation, the tire having: an annular casing layer that is wrapped about first and second spaced-apart annular beads, each layer of the casing defining a pair of upturned terminal segments running from the beads out to outer terminal points; a reinforcing assembly positioned radially outside the casing, the reinforcing assembly including an innermost reinforcing band having two lateral edge sections; a pair of heel zones, wherein the casing layer folds around the heel zones such that each zone is bounded laterally by the casing layer and the upturned terminal segments, and bounded radially by innermost faces of the corresponding annular beads and outermost terminal points of the respective upturned segments; a pair of flank portions, each flank portion lying axially beyond one of the heel zones; and a pair of flank rubber strips, wherein a first flank strip lies axially between a first flank portion of the pair and extends along a face of the casing layer from a leading end situated between the casing layer and the first lateral edge section of the innermost reinforcing band to a trailing end positioned inside a first heel zone of the pair, and wherein a second flank strip lies axially between a second flank portion of the pair and extends along the face of the casing layer from a leading end situated between the casing layer and the second lateral edge section of the innermost reinforcing band to a trailing end positioned inside a second heel zone of the pair.

A radial-ply vehicle tyre comprising: a pair of circular bead wires spaced apart along an axial direction; a pair of elastomeric filler strips projecting upward from the respective bead wires; at least one carcass layer, a reinforcing band having opposed side margins; and a pair of flank rubber laminates, each possessing an upper extremity and a lower extremity, wherein the lower extremity sits radially beneath the corresponding elastomeric filler strip.

A tyre comprising: a tread foundation layer; a tread outer portion including a first outer sub-layer and a second outer sub-layer formed of dissimilar elastomeric blends, the tread presenting a middle region M and a pair of flank regions F flanking the middle region M and positioned on opposite axial sides thereof, wherein the first outer sub-layer lies radially above the tread foundation layer and extends axially across the middle region M and both flank regions F, wherein the second outer sub-layer is disposed within the middle region M and radially above both the tread foundation layer and at least a portion of the first outer sub-layer, wherein the tread includes a central land projection bordered by channels situated on each side thereof, wherein the central land projection is constituted by the first outer sub-layer and the second outer sub-layer, and wherein a first tongue-shaped extension of the second outer sub-layer projects radially inward beneath at least one of the channels.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering comprising: a running surface section possessing an outermost lateral boundary at a first contact limit; and a sidewall flank projecting axially away from the first contact limit, wherein the running surface section incorporates: a central location positioned axially between the first contact limit and a median plane of the covering, a central zone spanning from the median plane to the central location, and an edge zone extending between the first contact limit and the central location, the sidewall flank exhibits a first void-to-solid ratio measured between the first contact limit and a second site spaced radially inward from an outermost radial extent of the running surface section by a offset equal to 23 percent of an overall sectional height Ha, and a second void-to-solid ratio of the edge zone exceeds both a third void-to-solid ratio of the central zone and the first void-to-solid ratio of the sidewall flank.

A vehicle pneumatic covering comprising: a tread band including a middle zone straddling a mid-circumferential plane, a first flank-adjacent zone oriented toward an exterior lateral side of the covering, and a second flank-adjacent zone oriented toward an interior lateral side of the covering, the middle zone being spaced from the first flank-adjacent zone by two first peripheral channels each exhibiting a least breadth of approximately 5 mm; wherein: the first flank-adjacent zone and the second flank-adjacent zone each contain a series of first lateral incisions, each having an initial extremity positioned substantially at a corresponding margin of the tread band, a breadth at least equal to approximately 4 mm, and an axial span of at least 50% of the breadth of the zone in which it resides; the two first peripheral channels consist of one first peripheral channel facing the exterior lateral side and one first peripheral channel facing the interior lateral side; the count of first lateral incisions in the first flank-adjacent zone is fewer than the count of first lateral incisions in the second flank-adjacent zone; the middle zone possesses two peripheral ridges, a first and a second peripheral ridge respectively, each comprising a plurality of second lateral incisions; the middle zone includes a single second peripheral channel delimiting said first and second peripheral ridges, the first peripheral ridge being axially bounded by the first peripheral channel facing the exterior lateral side and the second peripheral channel, the second peripheral ridge being axially bounded by the first peripheral channel facing the interior lateral side and the second peripheral channel; and the second lateral incisions possess a maximum breadth less than or equal to approximately 3 mm and establish in said at least one peripheral ridge a void-to-elastomer fraction below 0.06.

A wheel assembly comprising: a multiplicity of pliable spoke structures coupled between a central hub and an outer rim; wherein each of said multiplicity of pliable spoke structures includes a woven filament core.

A tire-mounting assembly, comprising: a wheel hub defining a channel bordered by a pair of flanges projecting around its circumference; a pneumatic casing fitted onto the wheel hub and configured to hold pressurized gas, said casing having a pair of side walls terminating in respective bead rings that abut the pair of flanges, each bead ring presenting an interior face and an exterior face; and a sealing gasket positioned in the channel between the bead rings, said gasket comprising a resilient polymer that deforms into a flattened profile when subjected to a compressive load, whereby the gasket widens to bear against the channel and the interior faces of the bead rings, thereby urging the exterior faces of the bead rings against the flanges so as to close the junction between the bead rings and the wheel hub and inhibit escape of the pressurized gas from the casing; and a load-imparting support member coupled to the polymer of said gasket that delivers the compressive load to flatten said polymer so that it expands and presses against the channel and the interior faces of the bead rings to close the junction between the bead rings and the wheel hub.

A wheel assembly, comprising: a wheel hub having a circumferential flange; a pneumatic tyre fitted onto the flange and pressurizable with gas, said tyre having two lateral walls each terminating in a bead seated against the flange; a deformable sealing compound positioned on the flange in the space separating the beads; and a clamping plate encircling the flange and resting atop the sealing compound, said clamping plate being drawn toward the flange so as to squeeze the sealing compound therebetween, whereby said sealing compound deforms, migrates circumferentially along the flange, and bears against the flange and the beads to close the junction between the beads and the flange and thereby inhibit escape of the pressurizing gas from the tyre through said junction.

A wheel assembly, comprising: a hub-engaging wheel body; a pneumatic tyre fitted onto the wheel body and configured to hold pressurized gas, said tyre having a pair of lateral walls terminating in respective bead portions that rest upon the wheel body; a series of elastomeric sealing strips arranged in abutting sequence and encircling the wheel body; a series of rigid bracing members arranged in abutting sequence, each resting atop a corresponding one of said elastomeric sealing strips; a series of confinement inserts each enclosed within a corresponding one of said elastomeric sealing strips; and a series of clamping devices coupled to the wheel body and arranged to drive respective ones of said rigid bracing members toward the wheel body and against the underlying elastomeric sealing strips and the enclosed confinement inserts, whereby said elastomeric sealing strips are squeezed by said rigid bracing members to spread circumferentially along the wheel body and form a seal against the wheel body and the tyre bead portions, said confinement inserts limiting the spreading of said elastomeric sealing strips.

A wheel assembly, comprising: a wheel hub having a circumferential flange; a pneumatic tyre seated on the flange and pressurizable with gas, the tyre having a pair of lateral walls terminating in respective annular bead portions that bear against the flange, each bead portion presenting an interior face and an exterior face; and a deformable sealant body positioned on the flange between the bead portions and responsive to an applied squeezing load, such that the sealant body changes configuration and migrates along the flange to bear against the flange and the interior faces of the bead portions, thereby urging the exterior faces of the bead portions toward the flange and establishing a fluid-tight barrier at a first contact surface between the sealant body and the flange and at a second contact surface between the sealant body and the interior faces, whereby the gas is retained within the tyre through said first and second contact surfaces.

An assembly for a vehicle road engagement member, comprising: a unitary wheel body defining a central channel and a pair of flanges projecting continuously along the circumference of the channel; a pneumatic envelope fitted onto the unitary wheel body and configured to retain pressurized gas, said envelope including a pair of lateral walls each carrying a bead portion seated within the channel and abutting the pair of flanges, each bead portion presenting an interior face and an exterior face opposite thereto; and a compliant gasket positioned within the channel between the bead portions of the lateral walls, said compliant gasket deforming in response to gas pressure within the envelope such that it is forced against the channel and the interior faces of the bead portions, thereby urging the exterior faces against the flanges and establishing a first sealing boundary between the gasket and the unitary wheel body and a second sealing boundary between the gasket and the interior faces, whereby escape of the pressurized gas from the envelope is inhibited.

A drive axle and wheel bearing unit, comprising: a drive shaft having a constant velocity joint housing and a journal projecting from the housing, the housing defining a first end face with a circumferential recess, the drive shaft including a first beveled step having a bevel angle; a wheel bearing having a sleeve with an aperture passing axially through it that accepts the journal, the sleeve including a second end face facing the first end face across a spacing interval and a second beveled step mating with the first beveled step, the wheel bearing including a mounting collar projecting outward from the sleeve; and a sealing gasket seated within the circumferential recess of the first end face and abutting the second end face of the wheel bearing.

A drive shaft and wheel bearing unit, comprising: a drive shaft having a constant velocity joint housing and a journal projecting from the housing, the housing having a first end surface, the drive shaft having a first beveled step with a bevel angle; a wheel bearing having a sleeve with an aperture passing therethrough that accepts the journal, the sleeve having a second end surface facing the first end surface of the housing and a second beveled step mating with the first beveled step, the second end surface being separated from the first end surface by a separation distance, the wheel bearing having a mounting flange projecting outward from the sleeve; and a sealing gasket positioned between the first end surface of the housing and the second end surface of the wheel bearing.

A drive axle and wheel bearing unit, comprising: a drive shaft including a constant velocity joint outer member and a journal projecting from the outer member, the outer member having a front face provided with a circumferential channel, the drive shaft including a first tapered step defining a taper angle, a lubricant reservoir recessed into the first tapered step; a wheel bearing including a housing having an aperture passing therethrough that accommodates the journal, the housing including a rear face facing the front face of the outer member and a second tapered step mating with the first tapered step, the rear face being offset from the front face by a clearance, the wheel bearing including a mounting flange projecting outward from the housing; and a sealing ring seated within the circumferential channel of the front face of the outer member and bearing against the rear face of the wheel bearing.

A hub bearing component for a vehicle wheel mount, the component comprising: a radial plate lying across a rotational centerline and provided with a set of apertures for securing a rim; and a unitary sleeve section extending axially away from the plate and defining a series of multi-sided cavities.

A hub assembly for a vehicle, comprising: a bearing race component defining a rotational axis and including a radially extending plate oriented perpendicular to the rotational axis, the plate bearing a series of bolt apertures distributed around the rotational axis for securing a rim, and a cylindrical sleeve extending axially away from the plate and provided with a set of multi-sided cutouts distributed around the rotational axis.

A twin-filament strand intended to serve as a load-bearing element within a belt ply of a pneumatic road tire, the strand being formed from precisely two filaments joined by twisting at their terminal regions, the first filament exhibiting a normalized stress value at one percent strain of at least 600 mN/tex, the second filament exhibiting a normalized stress value at one percent strain of no more than 75 mN/tex and a normalized stress value at four percent strain of no more than 150 mN/tex, the normalized stress values being defined by force divided by linear density at the stated strain points of the force-strain curve, and the ratio of the linear density of the first filament to the linear density of the second filament lying between 1.0 and 1.3, inclusive; and wherein the strand is thereby configured for dimensional stabilization of the belt ply.
