query_text: A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a pair of bead cores; a casing ply extending between the pair of bead cores in a toroidal configuration; and a reinforcing structure formed of at least one belt stratum positioned radially outward of a crown region of the casing ply, wherein the belt stratum is assembled from strip-shaped elements each incorporating a plurality of parallel reinforcing filaments coated with elastomer and arranged successively along the circumferential direction of the tyre, each strip-shaped element having a width of 1 to 10 mm, and wherein, along the equatorial plane of the tyre, two circumferentially neighboring strip-shaped elements are disposed with their circumferential terminal edges abutting one another.

A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a pair of bead cores; a casing ply extending between the bead cores in a toroidal configuration; and a reinforcing structure formed of at least one ply disposed radially outward of a crown region of the casing ply, wherein the reinforcing ply is built from strip-shaped elements, each containing multiple parallel reinforcing filaments encased in elastomer, the strip-shaped elements being aligned sequentially along the circumferential direction of the tyre, each strip-shaped element having a width of 1 to 10 mm, and wherein, at edge regions of the reinforcing ply, mutually neighboring strip-shaped elements in the circumferential direction are positioned such that their reinforcing filaments fail to coincide when projected along the radial direction of the tyre.

A method of manufacturing a pneumatic tyre, the tyre having a pair of bead cores, a casing ply extending in toroidal fashion between the bead cores, and a breaker formed of at least one breaker stratum situated radially outward of the crown region of the casing ply, the method comprising: a green-tyre building step in which a toroidally contoured inflexible former, whose exterior face shapes the inner liner of the tyre, is employed and unvulcanized tyre constituents, including casing plies and breaker plies, are successively applied onto the forming face of the former to assemble a green tyre; the green-tyre building step including a breaker-ply building operation in which the breaker ply is formed over the casing ply on the forming face of the former; the breaker-ply building operation including an application operation in which strip-shaped elements, each having a strip width of 1 to 10 mm and comprising a plurality of belt cords disposed in mutually parallel relation and coated with rubber, are laid successively along the circumferential direction of the tyre at a prescribed inclination to that direction so as to form a breaker ply made up of the strip-shaped elements arrayed circumferentially; and wherein, in the application operation, at the tyre equatorial plane, two of the strip-shaped elements that are mutually adjacent in the circumferential direction are laid such that their circumferential terminal edges abut one another.

A method of manufacturing a pneumatic tyre, the tyre having a pair of bead cores, a casing ply extending across the pair of bead cores in a toroidal configuration, and a reinforcing band formed of at least one layer situated radially outward of a crown region of the casing ply, the method comprising: a green tyre building step in which a toroidal, non-deformable mandrel having a building face that defines an inner liner surface of the tyre on its exterior is provided, and uncured tyre constituents, including casing plies and band plies, are successively applied onto the building face of the mandrel to assemble a green tyre; the green tyre building step including a band ply assembly step in which a band ply is formed over the casing ply on the building face of the mandrel; the band ply assembly step including an application step in which strip-shaped elements, each having a width of 1 to 10 mm and comprising a series of parallel reinforcing filaments coated with elastomer, are laid down one after another along the circumferential direction of the tyre at a set inclination relative to that circumferential direction so as to form a band ply made of the strip-shaped elements aligned in the circumferential direction; and in the application step, at edge portions of the reinforcing band, two of the strip-shaped elements that are adjacent in the circumferential direction are applied such that their reinforcing filaments do not overlap one another in the radial direction of the tyre.

A pneumatic tyre for a commercial truck, the tyre including a tread designed to engage a roadway through a contact face, the tread having grooves defining land portions, at least one groove being a peripheral composite incision whose centreline runs along a circumferential axis (XX′) of the tyre, the composite incision including, in an unworn state of the tyre, a succession of surface recesses opening at the contact face and subsurface recesses that do not open at the contact face, each adjacent pair consisting of a surface recess and a subsurface recess being joined by a linking passage, each surface recess having an extent (L 1) measured along the centreline on the contact face of the tyre in an unworn, unloaded condition, wherein the extent (L 1) of each surface recess is at least 1.5% and at most 12% of an outer diameter (D) of the tyre measured in the same unworn, unloaded condition; and wherein said linking passages connect each surface recess to the subsurface recess adjacent thereto.

A vehicle tyre for pneumatic use, comprising: a running surface having at least one peripheral channel, the channel being machined to a depth (T P ) and possessing a bottom and lateral sidewalls (2 b ); unattached ribs spaced apart along the peripheral direction, extending lengthwise in that direction, presenting an outer face parallel to the running surface periphery, and rising to a height (h S ) equal to 7% to 30% of the depth (T P ), the ribs being situated on the channel bottom; at least one projecting ledge that rests on the channel bottom, extends lengthwise in the peripheral direction, and is disposed between consecutive ribs along and against each sidewall, one ledge partially overlapping another ledge in the peripheral direction so as to leave a bottom passage between the ledges having a uniform axial breadth (b RG ) bounded by ledge borders formed on the ledges that run at a uniform depth (t 1 ) along the peripheral direction; and wherein each rib is locally broadened on each flank at its midsection by an outwardly curved flank portion, partly bounded by the outer face of the rib, one flank portion facing the other, the rib exhibiting at its flank portions a maximum axial width (b S, MAX ), measured at the level of the outer face, not exceeding 100% of the breadth (b RG ) of the bottom passage.

A computer-executed prediction process for estimating a count of remaining touchdowns before a replacement limit is reached by a specified tyre mounted on a specified airframe, the process comprising: supplying influencing variables pertaining to the specified tyre into a computing arrangement that performs the process, the arrangement including a data network that governs data entry into the arrangement, the data network having one or more network host machines that handle data relating to the influencing variables, and having at least one sensing unit that records and relays such data to the host machines, this supplying comprising: acquiring influencing variables for the specified tyre, performed by the network host machines of the arrangement, wherein the acquired influencing variables include data reflecting prior history and general characteristics of the specified tyre; and constructing a degradation-state learning dataset that is fed into a model for estimating the count of remaining touchdowns before the replacement limit of the specified tyre is reached; training the estimation model to anticipate the count of remaining touchdowns before the replacement limit, during which a machine-learning routine accepts as input the acquired influencing variables and the learning dataset so that a processor may obtain known degradation states corresponding to the touchdowns already performed by the specified tyre; estimating the count of remaining touchdowns before the replacement limit of the specified tyre, during which the count is calculated from data representing the influencing variables; and a comparison step in which the count of remaining touchdowns, output by the estimation model, is compared with a value of the replacement limit of the specified tyre, whereupon the arrangement generates a servicing timetable for the specified tyre.

A tire-condition apparatus comprising: a gauge element arranged to emit a signal representative of inflation level of a wheel; a first transmitter unit coupled to the gauge element and incorporating a first phase-locked loop (PLL) stage, the first transmitter unit adapted to impress data derived from the signal upon a first carrier having a first radio frequency; a second transmitter unit coupled to the gauge element and incorporating a second PLL stage, the second transmitter unit adapted to impress the data upon a second carrier having a second radio frequency that differs from the first radio frequency; a first radiating member through which the first transmitter unit emits the first carrier at the first radio frequency; a first impedance-matching network connected to the first transmitter unit and to the first radiating member; a second radiating member through which the second transmitter unit emits the second carrier at the second radio frequency; and a second impedance-matching network connected to the second transmitter unit and to the second radiating member.

A process for setting up a tire-pressure surveillance device to relay tyre telemetry to a set of remote processors, the process comprising: identifying a initial radio carrier at which the surveillance device will send the telemetry to a primary processor; identifying a secondary radio carrier at which the surveillance device will send the telemetry to a secondary processor; choosing a first RF impedance-matching network corresponding to the initial radio carrier; choosing a second RF impedance-matching network corresponding to the secondary radio carrier; establishing a first signal generator to produce first transmission signals conveying the telemetry at the initial radio carrier; establishing a second signal generator to produce second transmission signals conveying the telemetry at the secondary radio carrier; radiating the first transmission signals through a first aerial; and radiating the second transmission signals through a second aerial.

A tire surveillance apparatus installed on an automotive vehicle, comprising: a motor vehicle; a set of wheel assemblies mounted to the motor vehicle; an onboard processing unit carried by the motor vehicle; an off-board processing unit positioned separately from the motor vehicle; and a tire surveillance device comprising: a pneumatic transducer configured to produce a pressure reading indicative of inflation of a wheel assembly; a first signal handling unit electrically connected to the pneumatic transducer and including a first phase-locked loop (PLL) stage, the first signal handling unit configured to imprint data derived from the pressure reading onto a first carrier wave having a first radio frequency directed to the onboard processing unit; a second signal handling unit electrically connected to the pneumatic transducer and including a second PLL stage, the second signal handling unit configured to imprint the data derived from the pressure reading onto a second carrier wave having a second radio frequency directed to the off-board processing unit, wherein the second radio frequency differs from the first radio frequency; a first radiating element through which the first signal handling unit emits the first carrier wave at the first radio frequency toward the onboard processing unit; a first impedance adaptation network coupled to the first signal handling unit and to the first radiating element; a second radiating element through which the second signal handling unit emits the second carrier wave at the second radio frequency toward the off-board processing unit; and a second impedance adaptation network coupled to the second signal handling unit and to the second radiating element.

An apparatus for attaching a monitoring unit to a pneumatic tyre, comprising: a mounting body having a recess configured to receive, at least in part, a first section of at least one tyre monitoring unit; and a shell configured to receive, at least in part, a second section of the monitoring unit, wherein the shell includes a pocket sized to accommodate, at least in part, the mounting body; wherein the mounting body includes a first region disposed adjacent the recess and a second region that encircles, at least in part, the recess; wherein the shell includes a first region that encloses, at least in part, the pocket of the shell and a second region that encloses, at least in part, the second section of the monitoring unit; wherein the first region of the mounting body includes a bearing face on a side of the mounting body facing away from the second region of the mounting body; wherein the first region of the shell includes a bearing face on a side of the shell facing away from the second region of the shell, the bearing face of the shell being configured to be bonded to an inner surface of the tyre; and wherein the first region of the mounting body includes a raised rim that at least partially surrounds the first region of the mounting body.

A process for attaching a monitoring unit to a pneumatic wheel using an apparatus that includes a mounting plate having a receptacle sized to receive a first region of at least one tire monitoring unit, and a shroud configured to receive at least partially a second region of the monitoring unit, the shroud having a recess that accommodates the mounting plate, the mounting plate having a first region adjacent its receptacle and a second region encircling the receptacle, the shroud having a first region encircling its recess and a second region enclosing the second region of the monitoring unit, the first region of the mounting plate having a bearing face on a side facing away from its second region, the first region of the shroud having a bearing face on a side facing away from its second region, the bearing face of the shroud being configured to bond against an inner wall of a tire, the first region of the mounting plate having a raised lip that circumscribes its first region, the process comprising the steps of: placing the monitoring unit between the mounting plate and the shroud; and securing the combined mounting plate, monitoring unit and shroud to a tire surface using an adhesive film positioned on the bearing face of the mounting plate and on the bearing face of the shroud.

An apparatus for reversing a tyre, comprising: a foundation having a middle mount; a support frame positioned at a spacing from the foundation, the support frame being arranged to work with a tyre gripping assembly and to bear a second bead or a second flank of a tyre undergoing reversal; a thrusting assembly having a proximal terminus projecting from the middle mount of the foundation, a distal terminus, and a telescopic span extending between the proximal terminus and the distal terminus, the thrusting assembly and the middle mount defining a central spindle; the support frame is arranged and positioned to retain the thrusting assembly with its longitudinal extent coaxially aligned with the middle mount and the central spindle; the tyre gripping assembly is adjustable and arranged to adjustably retain a first bead of the tyre to the support frame and is arranged and positioned to hold the first bead of the tyre undergoing reversal at a first offset from the foundation and coaxially aligned with the central spindle; the thrusting assembly has its distal terminus arranged to engage the second bead of the tyre undergoing reversal, upon an extension of the telescopic span of the thrusting assembly; the thrusting assembly is arranged and positioned to displace its distal terminus and the engaged second bead of the tyre undergoing reversal along the central spindle and to a second offset from the foundation; and wherein the second offset from the foundation exceeds the first offset from the foundation by a magnitude sufficient to reverse the tyre undergoing reversal.

A process for reversing a pneumatic tire, comprising: positioning a support hub on a foundation; maintaining a platform spaced from, and at a set separation from, the foundation; securing a proximal extremity of a thrust member to the support hub; bearing a distal extremity of the thrust member on the platform and orienting an expandable span of the thrust member, running between the proximal and distal extremities, to define a longitudinal axis of a tire reversing apparatus; seating a lower bead or lower flank of a tire under reversal upon the platform and coaxially registering a rotational axis of the tire with the longitudinal axis of the tire reversing apparatus; retaining an upper bead of the tire against the platform using a releasable clamping assembly positioned at a first spacing from the foundation; calibrating the clamping assembly to hold the upper bead of the tire at the first spacing from the foundation; axially lengthening the expandable span of the thrust member along the rotational axis of the tire and the longitudinal axis of the apparatus and engaging the distal extremity of the thrust member against the lower bead of the tire; advancing the lower bead of the tire, by means of the thrust member, to a second spacing from the foundation; and wherein the second spacing exceeds the first spacing by a magnitude adequate to reverse the tire, thereby reversing the tire.

A towing coupling apparatus for a motor vehicle to attach an implement, comprising: a load-bearing coupling member furnishing an attachment site for the implement, the apparatus being shiftable between a retracted arrangement and an extended arrangement and being extendable from the motor vehicle during operation; wherein the coupling member is attachable to the motor vehicle via at least two elastic restraint lines that are slack in the retracted arrangement and tensioned in the extended arrangement, and that together form a quasi-rigid framework in the extended arrangement defining a mounting zone such that the attachment site is displaceable; whereby the quasi-rigid framework yields in a controlled manner to an excessive load and returns to its operating state without sustaining damage.

A coupling apparatus comprising: an extensible framework transitionable from a folded, retracted state into an operative state by drive units and tension-activated linkages that stiffen upon being pulled taut, thereby defining a coupling site, wherein the framework is configured to yield upon contacting an impediment and to restore its operative geometry after the impediment is cleared.

A roller apparatus, comprising: a hub body, the hub body possessing a primary flange of a first span at a leading extremity of the hub body; a secondary flange of the first span at a trailing extremity, situated opposite the leading extremity, of the hub body; a face portion that spans from a second span to a third span disposed coaxially with the primary flange at the leading extremity within a plane oriented transversely to a rotational axis of the hub body; and a recess bounded inwardly from the secondary flange, proceeding from the trailing extremity toward the leading extremity; and a ring member, joined to the hub body within a peripheral zone delimited at the leading extremity between the first span and the second span.

An assembly, comprising: a hub body, having: a primary flange of a first width at a leading extremity; a secondary flange of the first width at a trailing extremity opposite the leading extremity; and a shell coupled to the primary flange and the secondary flange, the shell exhibiting a second width smaller than the first width; wherein the leading extremity presents: a peripheral zone, recessed from the primary flange toward the trailing extremity, the peripheral zone encircling a region between the first width and a third width smaller than the first width; a bearing surface, oriented transverse to a rotational axis of the hub body, the bearing surface encircling a region between the third width and a fourth width smaller than the third width; and a depression, recessed from the bearing surface toward the trailing extremity, the depression lying within the fourth width; wherein the trailing extremity defines: a hollow, extending inward from the secondary flange toward the leading extremity; a first ring member, having: a first coupling mechanism, adapted to releasably secure to the leading extremity within the peripheral zone; and a first contact surface, defining a first set of apertures arranged about a perimeter of the first ring member; and a second ring member, having: a second coupling mechanism, adapted to releasably secure to the leading extremity; and a second contact surface, defining a second set of apertures arranged about a perimeter of the second ring member, wherein the second set of apertures differs in configuration from the first set of apertures.

A process for modifying a vehicle hub assembly, comprising: positioning a first insert bearing a first set of channels within a peripheral zone of a hub body, between an outer lip having a first width and a face surface lying transverse to a rotational centerline of the hub body, the face surface spanning from a second width to a third width, wherein the second width is smaller than the first width and the third width is smaller than the second width; fastening the first insert to the hub body; detaching the first insert from the hub body; extracting the first insert from the peripheral zone; placing a second insert into the peripheral zone, the second insert having a second set of channels that differs in configuration from the first set of channels; and fastening the second insert to the hub body.

A wheel assembly for a motor vehicle, comprising: a ring-shaped rim having a central rotational axis and opposite first and second lateral faces; the rim including: a first tire-retaining seat; a second tire-retaining seat; a first sloped shoulder joined to the first seat and descending radially toward the first lateral face's opposing side; a second sloped shoulder joined to the second seat and descending radially toward the second lateral face's opposing side; and a central trough portion situated between the first and second shoulders, the trough being composed of a series of arcuate and rectilinear sections joined end to end, the trough possessing at least three junction zones exhibiting differing wall-thickness profiles; and a disc member fixed to the rim, the disc member having a central boss positioned at its midpoint and provided with a plurality of fastener apertures.

A heavy-duty truck road wheel comprising: a disc member fixed to the barrel, wherein the disc member has a central boss positioned at its middle and a series of fastener apertures provided therein; and a ring-shaped barrel attached to the disc member, wherein the barrel establishes a rotational centerline and opposed interior and exterior faces, the barrel including: an exterior bead support surface; an interior bead support surface; an exterior drop-center wall joined to the exterior bead support surface and angling radially toward the interior face of the barrel; an interior drop-center wall joined to the interior bead support surface and angling radially toward the exterior face of the barrel; and a channel section bounded between the exterior and interior drop-center walls, wherein the channel section comprises: a first graded segment whose wall thickness grows moving from the exterior face toward the interior face; a second graded segment whose wall thickness shrinks moving from the exterior face toward the interior face; a straight cylindrical segment interposed between the first and second graded segments; a third graded segment whose wall thickness grows moving from the exterior face toward the interior face; a bent segment interposed between the second and third graded segments; and a fourth graded segment whose wall thickness shrinks moving from the exterior face toward the interior face.

A process for fabricating a rim for a road vehicle, the process comprising: (a) supplying a workpiece; (b) shaping the workpiece into a ring having a cylindrical interior face and a cylindrical exterior face; (c) applying flow forming to one of the interior and exterior faces of the ring so as to produce at least three zones exhibiting differing wall-thickness profiles in cross section; and (d) after step (c), executing at least one roll-forming step on the ring to create an outboard seating ledge, an outboard transition flank, an inboard seating ledge, an inboard transition flank, and a shaped central recess situated between the outboard and inboard transition flanks, wherein the central recess comprises at least three zones having differing wall-thickness profiles inherited from the flow forming of step (c), thereby yielding the rim.

A technique for manufacturing a road-vehicle rim assembly, comprising: (a) supplying a preform sheet; (b) shaping the preform sheet into a tubular band presenting a cylindrical interior face and a cylindrical exterior face, the band having a first lateral end and a second lateral end; (c) incrementally thinning the exterior face of the band by roller shaping so as to produce a series of junction locations at which wall thickness varies, such that a plurality of first zones tapers in thickness moving from the first lateral end toward the second lateral end and a plurality of second zones thickens in thickness moving from the first lateral end toward the second lateral end; (d) after step (c), executing at least one forming pass on the band to produce a first seat for a tire bead, a first sloped shoulder, a second seat for a tire bead, a second sloped shoulder, and a shaped trough section situated between the first and second sloped shoulders, the trough section incorporating transition regions of differing cross-sectional geometry inherited from the roller shaping of step (c); (e) furnishing a disc member; and (f) affixing the disc member to the band, thereby yielding the road-vehicle rim assembly.

A wheel rim comprising: a tubular body having a first flange and a second flange projecting outwardly in a radial direction from respective opposite ends of the tubular body, the tubular body including a first bead support and a second bead support positioned axially inward of the first flange and the second flange, respectively; wherein the tubular body and the first and second flanges are formed from plies of reinforcing filaments embedded in a resin; wherein a preformed reinforcement is interleaved between the plies of reinforcing filaments and is made of a material that absorbs, redirects, and/or dissipates energy from a load or impact exerted axially and/or radially on the rim, and/or that raises the hoop rigidity of the wheel; and wherein the reinforcement, in a cross-sectional view taken with the rim axis lying in the plane of the section, has two elongated segments, a first elongated segment extending into one of the first or second flanges, and a second elongated segment extending beneath the first or second bead support, respectively, such that the first and second segments together define an approximately L-shaped profile in cross-section.

A wheel for a motor vehicle, comprising: a ring-shaped barrel establishing a rotational center line and opposed first and second lateral faces, the barrel incorporating: a first tire-retaining shoulder; a second tire-retaining shoulder; a ring-form drop wall extending from the first tire-retaining shoulder radially toward the rotational center line and angling toward the second lateral face; a planar bottom surface joined to the drop wall and establishing the smallest radial extent of the barrel; and a shaped connecting zone positioned between the drop wall and the second tire-retaining shoulder, the connecting zone presenting a circumferentially undulating contour having: a concave outer trough joined to the bottom surface at a first point of tangency; a convex crest directly joined to the outer trough at a second point of tangency; and a concave inner trough directly joined to the crest at a third point of tangency, the inner trough being joined to the second tire-retaining shoulder at a fourth point of tangency; and a disc member fixed to the barrel, the disc member including a central hub disposed at its center and provided with a plurality of fastener apertures formed therein; wherein the connecting zone has an exterior face and an interior face separated by a wall thickness that remains uniform between the first and fourth points of tangency.

A wheel rim having an axial centerline and opposed inboard and outboard faces, the rim comprising: an outboard seat for a tire bead; an inboard seat for a tire bead; a ring-shaped drop wall joined to the outboard seat and sloping radially toward the inboard face; a central trough joined to the drop wall, the trough presenting a planar cross-section and establishing the smallest radius of the rim; and a connecting zone positioned between the drop wall and the inboard seat, the connecting zone exhibiting a circumferentially undulating contour comprising: a concave outboard depression meeting the trough at a first point of tangency; a convex crest meeting the outboard depression directly at a second point of tangency; and a concave inboard depression meeting the crest directly at a third point of tangency, the inboard depression meeting the inboard seat at a fourth point of tangency.

A process for fabricating an automotive road wheel, the process comprising: furnishing a ring-shaped barrel having a central rotational axis and opposed first and second faces, the barrel incorporating: a first seat for receiving a tire bead; a second seat for receiving a further tire bead; an annular drop flank joined to the first seat and sloping radially inward toward the second face of the barrel; a drop floor coupled to the drop flank, the drop floor exhibiting a planar cross-section and constituting the smallest radial extent of the barrel; and a shoulder zone interposed between the drop flank and the second seat, the shoulder zone being shaped by a spin-forming operation and presenting a circumferentially undulating contour comprising a concavely curved first trough meeting the drop floor at a first point of tangency, a convexly curved crest directly meeting the first trough at a second point of tangency, and a concavely curved second trough directly meeting the crest at a third point of tangency, the second trough meeting the second seat at a fourth point of tangency; and attaching a wheel face to the barrel to yield the automotive road wheel, the wheel face having a central boss positioned at its middle and provided with a plurality of lug apertures.

A road wheel assembly comprising: a ring-shaped barrel delimiting a rotational axis and opposed inner and outer faces, the barrel including: an outer seat for a tire bead; an inner seat for a tire bead; an annular drop region joined to the outer seat and sloping radially inward and toward the inner face of the barrel; and a shoulder zone situated between the drop region and the inner seat, wherein the shoulder zone exhibits a circumferentially undulating contour having: a concavely curved outer trough meeting the drop region at a first point of tangency, the outer trough establishing the smallest radial extent of the barrel; a convexly curved crest joined directly to the outer trough at a second point of tangency; and a concavely curved inner trough joined directly to the crest at a third point of tangency, the inner trough further meeting the inner seat at a fourth point of tangency; and a disc element fixed to the barrel, the disc element carrying a central hub having a plurality of fastener apertures formed therein.

A rim for a road vehicle wheel having a rotational axis and opposed inner and outer faces, the rim comprising: an outer seating surface for a tyre bead; an inner seating surface for a tyre bead; an annular drop region joined to the outer seating surface and sloping radially inward toward the inner face of the rim; and a shoulder zone located between the drop region and the inner seating surface, wherein the shoulder zone exhibits a wavy circumferential contour including: a concavely curved outer trough joined to the drop region at a first point of tangency, the outer trough establishing the lowest radial extent of the rim; a convexly curved crest joined directly to the outer trough at a second point of tangency; and a concavely curved inner trough joined directly to the crest at a third point of tangency, the inner trough being joined to the inner seating surface at a fourth point of tangency.

A technique for fabricating a road-vehicle wheel, comprising: furnishing a ring-shaped barrel body that establishes a central rotational axis and opposing first and second lateral faces, the barrel body comprising: a first tire-retaining shoulder; a second tire-retaining shoulder; a sloping trough wall joined to the first shoulder and extending radially inward while tilting toward the second lateral face; and a blending zone interposed between the trough wall and the second shoulder, the blending zone being shaped by a roll-forming operation and exhibiting a wavy circumferential contour including: a concavely curved first hollow joined to the trough wall at a first point of tangency, the first hollow establishing the innermost radial extent of the barrel body; a convexly curved crest directly joined to the first hollow at a second point of tangency; and a concavely curved second hollow directly joined to the crest at a third point of tangency, the second hollow being connected to the second shoulder at a fourth point of tangency; and affixing a wheel face to the barrel body to yield the road-vehicle wheel, the wheel face including a central hub positioned at its middle and provided with a plurality of fastener apertures formed therein.

A hub-and-wheel arrangement, comprising: a rotor unit possessing front and rear coupling plate subassemblies, each coupling plate subassembly including a face panel fastened to a bearing body, the bearing body defining a shaft opening, locating protrusions, half-round recesses, and fastener openings, each half-round recess aligned with one of the fastener openings and shaped to accept and seat a fastener within that fastener opening such that the associated coupling plate subassembly is held against rotation relative to that fastener; a hub body including front and rear hub subassemblies and adapted to retain a tyre, each hub subassembly including a rim section defining a recess, a rotor seat located at the midpoint of the recess and sized to receive the corresponding rotor unit, the seat having a shaft opening at its midpoint, radial spokes extending outward from the seat to a wall of the recess, and fastener openings spaced circumferentially about the seat, each spoke provided with a locating cutout spaced circumferentially about the seat; and wherein each coupling plate subassembly is arranged to sit within the seat of the corresponding hub subassembly with the locating cutouts of that hub subassembly engaging and rotationally fixed to the locating protrusions of that coupling plate subassembly, such that the fastener and shaft openings of the coupling plate subassemblies and the hub subassemblies are brought into registration to permit a fastener to pass through the fastener openings and thereby secure the hub-and-wheel arrangement.

A wheel mounting arrangement, comprising: a rubber covering defining a central opening; a rim assembly comprising a front and a rear bushing panel assembly, each bushing panel assembly including a plate cover secured to a bushing body, the bushing body defining a shaft opening, locating protrusions, arc-shaped recesses, and fastener openings, each arc-shaped recess corresponding to one of the fastener openings and shaped to receive and seat a fastener within that fastener opening so that the associated bushing panel assembly is fixed against rotation relative to that fastener; and a hub comprising a front and a rear hub section configured to retain the rubber covering, each hub section having a rim forming a recess with a rim receiving socket located at a middle of the recess and sized to accept the corresponding rim assembly, the socket including a shaft opening at its middle, spokes extending radially from the socket to a wall of the recess, and fastener openings arranged around a periphery of the socket, each spoke having a locating notch positioned around the periphery of the socket; and wherein each bushing panel assembly is arranged within the socket of the corresponding hub section with the locating notches of that hub section engaged with and fixed against rotation to the locating protrusions of that bushing panel assembly such that the fastener and shaft openings of the bushing panel assemblies and the hub sections line up to permit a fastener to be passed through those fastener openings to fasten the wheel mounting arrangement together.

A castor with several foot-operated controls, comprising: a support body; a shaft member rotatably joined to the support body with one terminal portion received inside the support body, the terminal portion carrying a first toothed ring and a second toothed ring rigidly secured thereto, the first toothed ring defining a first notch and the second toothed ring defining a second notch; a steering arrangement including a combined control pedal and a first latch plate, the control pedal presenting an actuating section while a second terminal region carries a driving projection and a bearing projection, one end of the first latch plate being a driven region engaged by the driving projection, an opposite end of the first latch plate forming a first catch that faces the first notch so as to lock into or release from the first notch upon pivoting of the first latch plate; a braking arrangement including the control pedal, a secondary brake element and a second latch plate, the secondary brake element having at one end a receiving surface pressed against the bearing projection, a lateral projection on one side of its other end and a thrust projection on the opposite side of the lateral projection, the secondary brake element sharing a common axis with the control pedal and being pivotally mounted to the support body through a third pin; one end of the second latch plate presenting a driven surface pushed by the thrust projection, an opposite end of the second latch plate forming a second catch facing the second notch, and two lateral flanges extending from the second latch plate; a return arrangement including a steering return pedal and a brake release return pedal positioned side by side, both pivotally mounted coaxially to the support body by a second pin, each having a return actuating end, the steering return pedal presenting a first pressing face and the brake release return pedal presenting a second pressing face which act upon the driving projection and the lateral projection; a pair of rolling members including a first lateral wheel and a second lateral wheel, each having facing sides provided with a limiting toothed gear presenting a plurality of recesses into which the lateral flanges selectively engage or disengage as the second latch plate pivots; and three resilient members including a first spring coaxial with the first and second latch plates with one end pressing the second latch plate, a second spring coaxial with the steering return pedal and the brake release return pedal passing through each and having one end pressing the first latch plate, and a third spring passing through the coaxial control pedal and secondary brake element with one end pressing the control pedal and a second end positioned beneath the second latch plate.

A mobile machine, comprising: a pair of powered tires disposed at a leading extremity of the machine; a drive unit operatively linked to turn the pair of powered tires; a control module configured to transmit a caster engagement command; one or more swivel castors disposed at a trailing extremity of the machine opposite the leading extremity, the one or more swivel castors supported by corresponding rotary mounts pivotally joined to a chassis of the machine, each rotary mount including a contact face and at least one recess passing through the contact face; and in connection with each of the one or more swivel castors: an actuator secured to the chassis and electrically driven to reciprocate a rod along a line inclined at a non-perpendicular angle relative to the contact face of the rotary mount; a latch bolt attached to the rod and positioned to align with the recess when the rotary mount is turned to a designated angular position; wherein, responsive to the engagement command, the actuator switches between a released condition, in which the latch bolt is withdrawn away from the contact face, and an engaged condition, in which the latch bolt is advanced toward the rotary mount to enter the recess when the rotary mount sits at the designated angular position.

A procedure for controlling a utility machine having a pair of powered wheels at a leading extremity and at least one swivel wheel at a trailing extremity opposite the leading extremity, the procedure comprising: transmitting a swivel-securing command through an electronic control unit; in reaction to the swivel-securing command, energizing a coil actuator to shift a latch plunger back and forth along a linear path inclined at a non-perpendicular angle relative to a contact face of a rotating mount of the swivel wheel, wherein: in a released condition, the latch plunger is withdrawn from the contact face; and in a secured condition, the latch plunger is advanced toward the rotating mount to enter a recess of the rotating mount when the rotating mount is positioned at a designated turning angle; and wherein the coil actuator is a solenoid.

A traction aid for supplying grip to a vehicle's tire or tread, the traction aid comprising: a body presenting a forward margin and a rearward margin aligned with a travel path, a spacing between the forward margin and the rearward margin establishing an overall extent of the body, the body including: an upper face adapted to contact the vehicle's wheel or tread, the upper face carrying outboard rows of exterior traction projections spaced apart from one another and an inboard row of traction projections situated between the outboard rows, wherein crests of the outboard rows of exterior traction projections sit at a greater height than crests of the inboard row of traction projections measured across the travel path, such that a recessed channel is defined between the outboard rows of exterior traction projections.

A traction aid for supplying grip to a wheel or belt of a motor vehicle, the traction aid comprising: a body presenting a forward margin and a rearward margin situated along a travel path, a spacing separating the forward margin from the rearward margin establishing an extent of the body, the body exhibiting a generally hollowed contour adjacent the forward margin and a generally bulged contour extending from the hollowed contour to the rearward margin, the body including: an upper face configured to contact the wheel or belt of the vehicle, the upper face bearing laterally separated ridges of outboard traction projections and an inboard row of traction projections positioned between the laterally separated ridges of outboard traction projections.

A tyre for a vehicle wheel, comprising: a sub-tread layer situated between a fabric-based ply and an outer tread band, the sub-tread layer being a temperature-responsive rubber mixture that incorporates a reinforcing particulate, a processing aid, vulcanizing agents, and a polymer blend including a first elastomeric species exhibiting a first glass transition point and a second elastomeric species exhibiting a second glass transition point, the two species being poorly compatible with one another; wherein the mixture comprises the first species at 20 to 80 phr and the second species at 20 phr or more, the first species is a solution-prepared styrene-butadiene copolymer, the second species is natural polyisoprene, and the difference between the first and second glass transition points is 20 K or greater, the glass transition points being identified from a derivative curve obtained by differential scanning calorimetry under a nitrogen atmosphere over 123 K to 373 K at a heating rate of 10 K/min per ISO 11357-2.

A process for producing a tyre having a heat-responsive subcoat, the process including: choosing a first polymer possessing a first vitrification point and a second polymer possessing a second vitrification point that are poorly compatible with one another; blending the polymers, a reinforcing particulate, a processing aid, and vulcanizing agents mechanically to yield a compounded elastomeric mixture containing a polymer blend; forming the compounded mixture into a rubber member destined for a subcoat layer of a tyre; disposing the rubber member on an unvulcanized carcass such that it lies between a fabric ply and a tread band; and vulcanizing the unvulcanized carcass to yield a tyre incorporating the heat-responsive subcoat, wherein: the rubber member comprises the first polymer in a quantity between 20 and 80 phr and the second polymer in a quantity of at least 20 phr, the first polymer is solution-styrene-butadiene rubber, the second polymer is natural rubber, and the difference between the first and second vitrification points is at least 20 K, the vitrification points being determined from a derivative signal obtained by differential scanning calorimetry under nitrogen in a range of 123 K to 373 K at a linear heating rate of 10 K/min according to ISO 11357-2.

A threaded securing device comprising: a main member extending along a longitudinal axis, the main member including a drive-receiving section configured to accept an applied rotational force and a male-threaded section adapted to engage a complementary threaded component; the main member further including a sleeve-supporting section oriented about the longitudinal axis; a casing coaxially seated upon the sleeve-supporting section, the casing presenting an interior face confronting an exterior face of the sleeve-supporting section; the casing being held for free turning movement relative to the main member, such that the casing turns with respect to the main member under an externally applied torque before the main member turns upon engagement with an outside structure at a predetermined seating torque; a transmission linkage configured to rotationally couple the main member and the casing; the transmission linkage including a keyed portion configured to rotationally mate with the drive-receiving section of the main member; the transmission linkage including a casing-mating portion configured to rotationally mate with a coupling region of the casing; and the casing including a grip section to which an outside rotational force may be applied; wherein the transmission linkage is arranged to remain in rotatable engagement with both the drive-receiving section and the coupling region such that the main member turns about the longitudinal axis in step with turning of the casing about the longitudinal axis under an outside rotational force applied about the longitudinal axis to the grip section at the predetermined seating torque.

A non-engaging seal arrangement for a hub bearing, positioned between a knuckle and at least one of a rotating hub, a bearing assembly, or a spindle journal, the arrangement comprising: a rotary seal element secured to at least one of the rotating hub, the bearing assembly, or the spindle journal and defining a clearance channel with a counter-surface provided on the knuckle or on a part attached to the knuckle; said rotary seal element including spokes and pockets positioned between adjacent spokes; and a barrier flange bounding said pockets on an outer radial side and bounding said clearance channel on an inner radial side, such that upon rotation of said rotary seal element a flow is induced in front of and/or within said clearance channel that resists penetration of contaminants past the seal.

A wheel bearing unit defining a central pivot line, comprising: a fixed outer race positioned around an inner rotating member; a flanged rotor situated radially within the fixed outer race, the flanged rotor being turnable about the pivot line and relative to the fixed outer race, the flanged rotor including a splined section and a cylindrical shank located axially inward of the splined section; an inner race seated axially against the flanged rotor; and a splined collar disposed axially next to the inner race and rotationally linked with the splined section of the flanged rotor; wherein the flanged rotor exhibits a smoothly tapering contour extending from a radially outward face of the splined section to an outer circumferential face lying radially beyond the shank of the flanged rotor.

A rotary transmission member adapted to be fixed to and turn together with a hub unit and establishing an axial orientation, the member comprising: a first end face and a first peripheral face surrounding the axial orientation; the first end face bearing a plurality of pawl-shaped projections distributed about the axial orientation and a plurality of radially oriented recesses; the first peripheral face bearing a plurality of first toothed protrusions distributed about the axial orientation and meshing with the hub unit; wherein each recess is situated between two adjacent pawl-shaped projections of the plurality.

An apparatus for outdoor cutting, comprising: a chassis having a bracket; a ground-engaging member carried by the chassis; a motor that selectively drives the ground-engaging member; a steerable caster module mounted to the chassis separately from the ground-engaging member, the caster module including a swivel bracket journaled to the chassis for angular movement about a swivel axis, the swivel bracket establishing a datum point spaced radially from the swivel axis, a directional wheel rotatably joined to the swivel bracket, a first transducer that senses an angular orientation of the swivel bracket, and a second transducer that senses the datum point; and one or more processors secured to the chassis in signal communication with the first transducer and the second transducer, the one or more processors being jointly arranged to obtain a positional reading from the first transducer, derive a heading value from the positional reading, obtain a registration indication from the second transducer signaling sensing of the datum point, and correct the derived heading value using the obtained registration indication.

A grass-cutting machine comprising: a chassis having a bracket extension; a handle assembly mounted to the chassis; a traction member joined to the chassis; an electric motor driving the traction member; a caster-style wheel unit fastened to the bracket extension separate from the traction member, the wheel unit including a swivel block journaled to the chassis for turning about a swivel axis, the swivel block establishing a benchmark location offset radially from the swivel axis, a ground-engaging wheel carried by the swivel block, a first transducer sensing a rotational state of the swivel block, and a second transducer sensing the benchmark location; and at least one processing unit secured to the chassis and in signal communication with the first transducer and the second transducer, the at least one processing unit being jointly operable to obtain a rotation signal from the first transducer, compute a heading value from the rotation signal, obtain a benchmark signal from the second transducer signaling passage of the benchmark location, and correct the computed heading value using the obtained benchmark signal.

A solid-core wheel covering suitable for a mobile elevated support of a field-deployed sprinkler installation, said covering comprising: a flexibly deformable covering body presenting an exterior perimeter extending about a fixed spin axis upon which said covering body is capable of turning; and, arranged in evenly spaced succession about said spin axis at a location set back radially toward said spin axis from said exterior perimeter of the covering body, a ring-shaped series of enclosed voids formed within said covering body; wherein each enclosed void of said ring-shaped series: when viewed along planes oriented perpendicular to said spin axis, exhibits an elongated transverse profile having a dimension extending along the direction encircling said spin axis that surpasses a narrower dimension extending along the direction radiating relative to said spin axis.

A resilient wheel covering for a mobile riser of an in-field watering installation, the covering comprising: a deformable, radially yielding body possessing an exterior perimeter extending about a fixed spin axis around which the body turns; and, arranged in evenly spaced succession about said spin axis at a radial offset set inward from said exterior perimeter, a ring-like series of enclosed voids formed within said body; wherein: when viewed in transverse slices taken perpendicular to said spin axis, each void presents a profile having an extent measured along a path encircling the spin axis and a extent measured along a path directed toward or away from the spin axis, the former exceeding the latter; each void traverses the body entirely in a direction parallel to the spin axis, and the radial extent of each void narrows in an axially inboard sense toward a central plane of the body that runs transversely to the spin axis midway between the opposed lateral faces of the body; and the body is further distinguished by one or more of the following: (a) the body is constructed to permit complete radial compression of the radial extent of each void at its slimmest location, where that extent is least in an unloaded condition, while that location passes through a lower ground-engaging segment of the circular path described by the body about the spin axis; (b) a radial dimension of the exterior perimeter, across untreaded zones overlying the voids, is larger over the portion of such zone lying atop the slimmest location of the void than over other portions lying atop broader regions of the void; and (c) said voids of the ring-like series all sit at an identical radial spacing from the spin axis, and said ring-like series constitutes the only such series of elongated-profile voids.

A resilient wheel covering for a mobile riser of a field-deployed watering apparatus, said covering comprising a radially yielding carcass body having a perimeter surface encircling a central spin axis about which said carcass body revolves; wherein the perimeter surface of the carcass body includes inclined zones, along each of which a radial dimension of the carcass body diminishes while progressing axially inward toward a median plane of the carcass body, said inclined zones comprising a first group and a second group of inclined zones whose axially inward progressions are respectively gauged from opposite lateral faces of the carcass body.

A process for running a ground-engaging irrigation apparatus across a cultivated plot, said process comprising: deploying airless wheels on said apparatus that each define converging internal voids whose radial extent narrows progressively in an axially inboard sense toward a mid-plane situated perpendicular to a central spin axis of the wheel and halfway between opposed axial flanks; while each airless wheel rolls across the plot, radially compressing each converging void at its most constricted interior zone as said void travels through a lowermost ground-touching arc of the wheel's circular path, and thereby expelling entrained sludge from the internal voids via unobstructed exterior openings at the opposed axial flanks of the wheel, whereby the wheels self-purge said internal voids; and

query_text: A method of running a ground-based watering apparatus across a cultivated plot, said method comprising: employing airless wheels on said apparatus that each present inclined regions along an exterior perimeter of the wheel body where a radial dimension of the wheel body diminishes while progressing axially inward toward a central axial plane of the wheel body, wherein said inclined regions comprise a first group and a second group whose respective inward axial progressions are gauged from facing lateral faces of the wheel body; and, during rolling travel of each airless wheel across the plot, leveraging said first and second groups of inclined regions, as they pass through a lowermost ground-engaging arc of a circular orbit of the wheel, to pull soil inwardly toward a mid-plane of the wheel so as to backfill the earth beneath the wheel and thereby curb excessive furrow development in the plot.

A tire tread assembly having plural strata, the assembly including: a foundation stratum formed from a first elastomeric compound; and an outer stratum disposed upon and bonded to the foundation stratum, the outer stratum having: a left-hand flank portion formed from a second elastomeric compound; a right-hand flank portion formed from a third elastomeric compound; and an intermediate portion positioned between the left-hand flank portion and the right-hand flank portion and formed from a fourth elastomeric compound; wherein the first elastomeric compound exhibits a greater elastic modulus than the fourth elastomeric compound, and wherein the fourth elastomeric compound exhibits a greater elastic modulus than both the second elastomeric compound and the third elastomeric compound.

A laminated running surface assembly for a motor vehicle tyre, including: a foundation ply formed from a first elastomeric compound; an outer ply disposed over and bonded to the foundation ply; the outer ply incorporating: a first lateral zone formed from a second elastomeric compound; a second lateral zone formed from a third elastomeric compound; and a middle zone positioned between the first lateral zone and the second lateral zone and formed from a fourth elastomeric compound; wherein the first elastomeric compound exhibits a greater elastic modulus than the fourth elastomeric compound, and the fourth elastomeric compound exhibits a greater elastic modulus than both the second elastomeric compound and the third elastomeric compound; the elastic modulus of the first elastomeric compound lies between 13 and 16 MPa; the elastic modulus of the second elastomeric compound lies between 7 and 10 MPa; the elastic modulus of the third elastomeric compound lies between 7 and 10 MPa; the elastic modulus of the fourth elastomeric compound lies between 12 and 15 MPa; the foundation ply carries, on the face oriented toward the outer ply, a raised ridge of material extending along the full length of the running surface assembly, wherein the middle zone is bipartite and comprises a first middle portion and a second middle portion; the first middle portion and the second middle portion are situated on opposite flanks of the raised ridge; the raised ridge is preferably joined integrally at its sides to the first middle portion and the second middle portion; and the thickness of the outer ply does not exceed the height of the raised ridge.

A ground-engaging roller for an endless-belt drive, comprising: a central boss section and an outer rim section encircling the boss section; the rim section including a set of channels opening from a first flank of the rim toward a second flank of the rim, the channels spaced apart around the circumference of the rim; a channel depth measured radially being larger adjacent the first flank than adjacent the second flank; and the channel having an oval, egg-shaped cross-section profile.

A ground-engaging traction arrangement for a motorized conveyance, the arrangement comprising: a chassis; a powered sprocket assembly pivotally coupled to the chassis and selectively linkable to the conveyance; a roller assembly pivotally coupled to the chassis; and a looped belt encircling the sprocket assembly and the roller assembly, the looped belt being driven by the sprocket assembly, wherein the roller assembly includes a rotor having a core and a rim circumscribing the core, the rim including: a series of channels extending transversely from a first flank of the rim toward a second flank of the rim, the channels being spaced apart around the circumference of the rim, a depth of a first channel from the series being larger adjacent the first flank than adjacent the second flank, the first channel exhibiting an oval contour.

A tread-bearing vehicle tyre comprising: a ground-engaging rib region defined in a tread face; a set of fine incisions formed in at least one such rib region, the fine incisions being interlinked so as to define a linked incision, the linked incision forming an incision module, and the incision modules being recurrently disposed across the rib region; wherein at least one terminal extremity of at least one of the fine incisions, measured along its lengthwise direction, stops short of a boundary of the rib region; wherein the product of a width of the linked incision taken along the axial direction (w1) and a depth of the fine incision (h), expressed in millimetres, does not exceed 150 square millimetres; and wherein a density of the incisions, computed as the reciprocal of a mean circumferential spacing between adjacent incisions, which spacing is derived from a count of equivalent incisions and an equivalent circumferential length of the rib region, is 0.15 per millimetre or greater.

A tread-bearing vehicle tyre comprising: a ground-contacting rib exposed at a running face, wherein a series of fine incisions is formed in the rib, the fine incisions separated by gaps forming grouped cells that recur along the rib, one extremity of at least one fine incision in a lengthwise direction stopping short of the rib boundary, a product of the lateral span w2 and the incision depth h of each fine incision being 150 square millimetres or less, and, with n denoting the count of fine incisions in the rib, BW denoting the greatest lateral width of the rib, and BL denoting the outline area of the rib divided by BW, a dimensionless count N equal to w2 times n divided by BW, and an incision frequency SD equal to (N+1) divided by BL being 0.15 per millimetre or greater.

A pneumatic vehicle covering comprising: a ground-engaging face provided with a rib section, wherein the rib section includes a blade arrangement formed of two incisions, each incision extending so that its two longitudinal extremities are confined within the rib section; and the two incisions face one another across the circumferential direction of the covering only over a portion of their lateral extent in the axial direction.

A bicycle wheel hub arrangement comprising: a spindle; a barrel member, wherein the spindle passes through the barrel member along a lengthwise axis, wherein the barrel member turns about the spindle by way of at least one antifriction bearing, wherein an inner race of the antifriction bearing sits on the spindle and an outer race of the antifriction bearing sits on or within the barrel member, and wherein a seating portion of the barrel member oriented toward the antifriction bearing as considered along the lengthwise axis rests on the outer race of the antifriction bearing; a terminal piece affixed to or on the spindle at a side of the antifriction bearing remote from the barrel member, wherein a seating portion of the terminal piece oriented toward the antifriction bearing as considered along the lengthwise axis rests on the inner race of the antifriction bearing; and a shim element positioned between the seating portion of the terminal piece and the inner race of the antifriction bearing and/or between the seating portion of the barrel member and the outer race of the antifriction bearing, wherein the shim element exhibits a changeable dimension as measured along the lengthwise axis.

A road wheel apparatus comprising: a rim structure including a main section; a central fastener component coupled to the rim structure and turnable so as to selectively clamp or release the rim structure relative to an axle flange of a motor vehicle upon which the rim structure is installable; and a handle member that rests within or adjacent to the rim structure in a stowed configuration and that is swung out of the stowed configuration into a deployed configuration, wherein turning of the handle member in the deployed configuration causes the central fastener component to rotate.

A road-going vehicle drivetrain arrangement comprising: a frame structure; a rolling assembly; and a damping linkage joining the rolling assembly to the frame structure, wherein the rolling assembly includes: a rim member; a central fastener element coupled to the rim member and turnable so as to selectively draw the rim member toward or release it from a hub of the vehicle to which the rim member is attachable; and a crank handle movable between a stowed placement within or adjacent the rim member and an engaged placement from which the crank handle is pivoted from the stowed placement to permit the central fastener element to be turned in response to turning of the crank handle.

A synchronizing device for aligning a pair of caster wheels of a human-propelled cart along a single common heading, comprising: a stiff bar having attachment hardware for coupling the synchronizing device to a chassis of the cart; and a first restraint and a second restraint configured to be affixed respectively to the pair of caster wheels and to hold both caster wheels oriented along the common heading so as to inhibit their pivoting.

A wheeled transport device comprising: a chassis; at least two caster wheels fastened by bolts to an underside of the device; and an alignment arrangement that holds the at least two caster wheels aligned along a single common orientation, wherein the alignment arrangement includes a stiff bar having attachment elements for securing the alignment arrangement to the chassis, and two retaining elements configured to be installed on the caster wheels so as to hold them in the common orientation and thereby block their pivoting movement.

A pneumatic covering for road-vehicle rims, comprising: a ply framework having lateral margins coupled to corresponding bead assemblies; optionally, a reinforcing girdle positioned outwardly, in the radial direction, of the ply framework; a running cap disposed outwardly, in the radial direction, of the ply framework and/or the girdle; wherein the running cap includes a cured elastomer body derived from, prior to curing, an uncured elastomer formulation which, prior to kneading, comprises an elastomer composition, the elastomer composition containing (i) 100 phr of a polymer blend comprising: a. at least one styrene-butadiene copolymer (SBR) present in a proportion of 70 phr to 100 phr, and b. 0 phr to 30 phr of at least one elastomer chosen from isoprene-based polymers (IR) and butadiene-based polymers (BR), (ii) 50 phr to 100 phr of a resin blend, a softener oil blend, or a combination of both, (iii) at least one reinforcing filler in a quantity of 50 phr to 130 phr, (iv) at least one curing agent in a quantity of 0.1 phr to 12 phr, and (v) 0.1 phr to 5 phr of an organic zinc salt having the structural formula: wherein R 1, R 2 and R 3, identical to or differing from one another, are each a hydrogen atom or a straight or branched alkyl chain of 1 to 10 carbon atoms, and wherein R 1, R 2 and R 3 together contain a total of 8 to 10 carbon atoms.

A curable rubber mixture prior to processing, comprising an elastomer blend formed of: (a) from 100 phr of a polymer system including at least one styrene-butadiene copolymer present at 70 phr to 100 phr, and (b) between 0 phr and 30 phr of at least one further rubber selected from polyisoprene (IR) and polybutadiene (BR); (ii) 50 phr to 100 phr of a resin component, a plasticizer oil component, or a combination of both; (iii) at least one reinforcing filler present at 50 phr to 130 phr; (iv) at least one curing agent present at 0.1 phr to 12 phr; and (v) 0.1 phr to 5 phr of a zinc carboxylate salt represented by the following formula, wherein substituents R1, R2 and R3, which may be identical or distinct, each denote hydrogen or a linear or branched alkyl radical having 1 to 10 carbon atoms, and wherein R1, R2 and R3 together contain a sum of 8 to 10 carbon atoms.

A tyre assembly comprising: a running surface portion; and a pair of lateral flanks disposed at opposite edges of the running surface portion and each defining an annular contour, wherein the running surface portion includes: a first channel and a second channel recessed into an outer face of the running surface portion and extending along a peripheral direction of the annular contour; and a multiplicity of incisions recessed into the outer face to extend along an axial direction of the annular contour, the multiplicity of incisions comprising a first group located between a first of the lateral flanks and the first channel, a second group located between the first channel and the second channel, and a third group located between the second channel and a second of the lateral flanks, wherein each of the incisions comprises: a linear segment extending in the axial direction; a first inwardly curved segment extending from the linear segment in the axial direction and having a first radius of curvature; a first outwardly curved segment extending from the first inwardly curved segment in the axial direction and having a second radius of curvature; a second inwardly curved segment extending from the first outwardly curved segment in the axial direction and having a third radius of curvature; a second outwardly curved segment extending from the second inwardly curved segment in the axial direction and having a fourth radius of curvature; and a terminal linear segment extending from the second outwardly curved segment in the axial direction, wherein, for the second group of incisions, an end of the linear segment remote from the first inwardly curved segment reaches the first channel, and an end of the terminal linear segment remote from the second outwardly curved segment reaches the second channel, and wherein the multiplicity of incisions has a trapezoidal cross-section in a depth direction of the running surface portion.

A tread assembly for a vehicle wheel, comprising: a first bead-adjacent flange having an annular profile; a second flange having the annular profile and separated axially from the first flange; and a running surface disposed between the first and second flanges and defining an outer envelope about the periphery of the flanges, wherein the running surface incorporates: first and second channels arranged in mutually parallel relation and extending along the envelope in a peripheral direction; and a plurality of slits positioned between at least one of (a) the first and second channels, (b) the first channel and the first flange, or (c) the second channel and the second flange, wherein each of the slits follows an undulating path along an axial direction of the annular profile and possesses a predetermined contour along its depth, the undulating path being formed by a first recessed segment having a first curvature radius and a first protruding segment having a second curvature radius, and wherein the predetermined contour along the depth comprises a first straight run extending orthogonally from the envelope, a second straight run extending at a first inclination from the first straight run, a third straight run extending at a second inclination from the second straight run, and a fourth straight run extending at a third inclination from the third straight run, the first and third straight runs being mutually parallel and the second and fourth straight runs being mutually non-parallel.

A tire-mounted pressure sensing device, comprising: one or more processing circuits and storage holding instructions that direct the device to: generate a nonce; compute, using at least the nonce, a derived input; produce a result by applying a keyed hash to the derived input together with a shared confidential key held also by a host automobile; extract a verification code from a leading segment of the result; extract a passcode from a trailing segment of the result; transmit a discovery-phase frame including a rotating random device address; measured tire condition readings; the nonce; and the verification code; detect that the device is attached to the automobile; carry out a bonding exchange with the automobile that comprises confirming the automobile knows the passcode; and only after the bonding exchange confirms the automobile: open an encrypted channel with the automobile; and obtain an integrity key from the automobile over the encrypted channel.

A computer-readable storage device holding program instructions that, when carried out by one or more processing circuits of an onboard control unit of a motor vehicle, direct the control unit to: obtain a plurality of learning-phase broadcast frames from a tire-mounted pressure sensing module, each frame including a resolvable private address (RPA), pressure reading data gathered by the module, a nonce value, and a verification token; infer, from the pressure reading data, that the module is probably mounted on the vehicle; derive, from the nonce value and a shared secret key also held by the module, an expected verification token; confirm that the expected verification token agrees with the verification token received from the module; derive, from the nonce value and the shared secret key, a pairing code; carry out a pairing exchange with the module using the pairing code; set up an encrypted link with the module; and transmit an integrity key (IK) to the module over the encrypted link.
