query_text: A procedure for a vehicle tire monitoring arrangement, comprising: generating, by a wheel-mounted pressure sensing module, an unpredictable number; computing, by the wheel-mounted pressure sensing module, a verification code and a numeric passkey from the unpredictable number together with a shared secret; broadcasting, by the wheel-mounted pressure sensing module, a series of learning-phase beacons carrying initial reading data, the unpredictable number, and the verification code; recognizing, by an onboard control unit of the motor vehicle, that the wheel-mounted pressure sensing module is a pending enrollment candidate; calculating, by the onboard control unit, the numeric passkey from the unpredictable number, the verification code, and the shared secret; carrying out a validated enrollment handshake between the onboard control unit and the wheel-mounted pressure sensing module; setting up an encrypted channel between the onboard control unit and the wheel-mounted pressure sensing module; and swapping a message integrity credential and address-resolution credentials between the onboard control unit and the wheel-mounted pressure sensing module.

A wheel assembly and energy harvesting apparatus, comprising: a pneumatic wheel; a compressible conduit at least partly bounded by one or more sidewalls exhibiting shape-restoring behavior and possessing one or more ports, the conduit positioned within or next to the wheel so that, during rotation of the wheel, working liquid inside the conduit is driven toward one of the one or more ports through peristaltic displacement; and an electrical generator in communication with the one of the one or more ports and arranged to convert motive energy of the liquid passing through that port into electrical power.

A wheel-handling device comprising: a support plate; a leading portion, the support plate being attached to the leading portion; a trailing portion joined to the leading portion; at least one hinge mounted to the leading portion; at least one catch fixed to the trailing portion; wherein the device is movable between a supporting configuration and a tilted configuration while standing on a ground face; in the supporting configuration, the at least one hinge contacts the ground face and the at least one catch is held above the ground face; and in the tilted configuration, the at least one hinge and the at least one catch both contact the ground face.

A towing bracket arrangement for coupling a trailer attachment to a motor vehicle, comprising: a coupling bar having a insertion stem end configured for sliding nested engagement inside a socket conduit secured to the motor vehicle, a lateral arm extending along an axis normal to the insertion stem, the lateral arm having a forward face opposite the insertion stem end, and wherein the lateral arm further defines a plurality of apertures passing transversely through the lateral arm at right angles to its axis, the apertures being evenly spaced rearward from the forward face of the lateral arm; a mounting block having a foundation section with a back face flanked between a pair of spaced ribs projecting outwardly from the back face and a socket end opposite the back face, wherein the pair of spaced ribs are shaped for sliding mating with the lateral arm of the coupling bar, the pair of spaced ribs including aligned paired bores in parallel registration for receiving a securing pin to thereby fix the mounting block in joined relation with the coupling bar; a cushioning pad bonded to at least a region of the flat back face of the foundation section situated between the pair of spaced ribs; and at least one securing pin fitted through one of the apertures of the lateral arm between the paired bores of the spaced ribs such that seated reception of the securing pin within the bores squarely clamps the lateral arm between the pair of spaced ribs so that a rear face of the lateral arm is brought into alignment with the forward face of the back face of the foundation section, thereby compressing the cushioning pad against the back face of the foundation section.

A trailer coupling apparatus for attaching a towed implement to a motor vehicle, comprising: a mounting bracket including a stem element having a projecting insertion section configured for sliding engagement inside a hitch socket secured to the towing vehicle, a groove element including a set-back web positioned between two outward lips, the stem element being fixed to a rear face of the set-back web so that the groove element extends lengthwise along an axis oriented transversely to the insertion section, and wherein a series of spaced, aligned apertures pairs are formed through the outward lips; a coupling body including a foot portion adapted for sliding fit with the groove element, the foot portion presenting a flat reverse face bounded by straight lateral margins, a pair of facing upright flanks extending perpendicularly from the lateral margins, and at least one bore extending parallel to the flat reverse face between the facing upright flanks; a damping pad secured to at least a segment of the set-back web of the groove element; a connecting end located opposite the flat reverse face, the connecting end carrying a plurality of implement attachments radiating outward in different directions from a central post; and at least one retaining fastener configured to pass through the bore of the foot portion and between a corresponding aperture pair of the groove element such that tightening the foot portion in squared registration within the groove of the mounting bracket presses the damping pad against the groove element.

A towing coupling apparatus, comprising: a chassis adapted to be affixed to a structural part of a motor vehicle; a socket assembly having a pivoting top section joined to the chassis, and a bottom section that delimits an aperture and a hollow interior; a plug member slidably positioned inside the hollow interior; a socket retention device adapted to hold the socket assembly in a tucked orientation relative to the chassis, and to hold the socket assembly in an extended orientation relative to the chassis; and a plug retention device adapted to fix the plug member relative to the socket assembly.

A towing apparatus arrangement, comprising: a towing apparatus, including: a chassis designed to be fixed to a structural part of a motor vehicle, a socket, joined to the chassis, that can be placed in a retracted configuration or an extended configuration, and a plug connected to the socket; and a front fascia assembly, including: a shell designed to be affixed to the structural part, including a bottom section that delimits an aperture through which the plug protrudes when the socket is in the extended configuration, and a powered shutter, designed to obscure and reveal the aperture in the bottom section of the shell, that can be placed in a shut position or an open position.

A process for placing a towing coupler into service, the process including a chassis mount, a coupling housing, and a sliding carrier, the process comprising: releasing a retention device of the coupling housing; pivoting the coupling housing relative to the chassis mount from a tucked orientation to an operative orientation; re-engaging the retention device so as to hold the coupling housing in the operative orientation; freeing a latch associated with the sliding carrier from the coupling housing; advancing the sliding carrier along the coupling housing from a withdrawn location to a projected location; and securing the sliding carrier at the projected location.

A spoke assembly for a bicycle wheel, comprising: an inverted-V-profile member; an apex region of the member provided with an aperture receiving a fastener for coupling the member to a rim; and two arms extending from the apex region, each arm including a distal portion that defines a further aperture receiving a fastener for coupling the arm to one of a left-side and a right-side mounting flange of a hub.

A spoke member for a bicycle wheel, the spoke member being angled in a generally V-profile, comprising: a lower region defining an aperture adapted to receive a fastener for securing the spoke member to a rim; two arms extending upwardly from the lower region, each arm terminating in a coupling portion; wherein the coupling portions are configured to engage flange surfaces situated on opposite lateral sides of a hub.

A brake-drum-free road wheel carrier element for a heavy-duty truck or trailer, comprising: a substantially radial mounting flange configured to attach to a hub; a substantially tubular barrel portion configured to couple with a rim; a shoulder zone bridging the barrel portion and the mounting flange; cooling apertures arranged at intervals around the periphery of the shoulder zone, the cooling apertures extending radially from a first inboard reference circle situated nearer the mounting flange to a second outboard reference circle situated nearer the barrel portion; wherein a segment of the shoulder zone lying between the mounting flange and the first inboard reference circle exhibits a wall thickness diminished by at least thirty percent relative to a wall thickness of the mounting flange, and/or wherein each cooling aperture possesses a widened portion whose circumferential span grows from the first inboard reference circle toward the second outboard reference circle.

A wheel for rail vehicles, comprising: a tread-bearing outer ring portion, an axle-receiving central boss having a bore extending therethrough, and a spoke-like intermediate plate joined to both the outer ring portion and the boss; wherein the alloy makeup of the wheel consists, by weight percent, of C: greater than 0.80% up to 1.35%, Si: no more than 1.00%, Mn: 0.10 to 1.50%, P: 0 to 0.050%, S: 0 to 0.030%, N: no more than 0.0200%, Al: 0 to 1.500%, Cu: 0 to 0.50%, Ni: 0 to 0.50%, Cr: 0 to 0.50%, V: 0 to 0.12%, Ti: 0 to 0.010%, Mo: 0 to 0.20%, and Nb: 0 to 0.050%, with the remainder being Fe and unavoidable contaminants; and wherein, on a section of the boss taken through a plane containing the bore's longitudinal axis, when the section is partitioned into 15 mm by 15 mm cells bounded by lines parallel to that axis spaced 15 mm apart radially outward from the bore wall and by lines perpendicular to that axis spaced 15 mm apart axially from the face where the bore opens, the mean carbon content within each cell is 1.40% by weight or less.

A climbing robot capable of ascending vertical faces, comprising: a chassis; a leading roller and a trailing roller coupled to the chassis, each selectively adherable to a support face and selectively releasable therefrom; a drive actuator that turns the leading roller and the trailing roller; and a controller that toggles each of the leading roller and the trailing roller between an adhered condition and a released condition and governs turning of the leading roller and the trailing roller, wherein the leading roller and the trailing roller are spaced apart along a direction of advance in which the chassis translates when the leading roller and the trailing roller are turned, and the controller executes a first locomotion regime for moving across a floor surface from the trailing roller toward the leading roller, and a second locomotion regime for advancing by placing the leading roller in the released condition and the trailing roller in the adhered condition while the trailing roller bears on the floor surface, and turning the trailing roller until the leading roller engages a wall surface extending upward from the floor surface while the leading roller is raised clear of the floor surface.

A reduction-free drive apparatus for a wheel end, comprising: a pair of toothed rotary members together with a matching inverted-lamination endless linkage of any construction; an enclosure divided into a near section coupled to an axle and/or suspension member of any kind; and a far section carrying any wheel-mounting hardware whatsoever.

A modular drive apparatus comprising: a housing module configured to couple a first bifurcated section situated nearer an input and a second bifurcated section situated farther from the input, the coupling permitting exact mounting onto a plurality of present and forthcoming vehicle input and output configurations; and a direct-coupled, non-geared transmission core retained within the housing module, the transmission core preserving its structural soundness throughout the coupling.

A chassis suspension unit comprising a hollow beam member and a trailing linkage arrangement, wherein the linkage arrangement includes: a forward bracket element formed monolithically with the beam member; a aft bracket element rigidly joined to a face of the beam member opposite the forward bracket element, the aft bracket element being secured to the beam member by pins and fasteners, the aft bracket element comprising an upper panel, a lower panel, an upper anchor block, a lower anchor block, and a gas strut adapter tab, the upper and lower anchor blocks being rigidly joined to a common end of the upper and lower panels, the upper panel being rigidly joined to the lower anchor block, and the gas strut adapter tab being joined to the upper panel at an end remote from the upper anchor block, a bottom end of the adapter tab being rigidly joined to an end of the lower panel remote from the lower anchor block, a cross-sectional thickness of the upper and lower panels tapering progressively from root to tip, the lower panel having a greater thickness than the upper panel; wherein a central stiffener is rigidly joined midway between the upper and lower panels, a forward stiffener lies on a side of the central stiffener remote from the lower anchor block and has opposite ends rigidly joined to facing sides of the upper and lower panels, a bottom stiffener lies on a side of the central stiffener remote from the forward stiffener and is rigidly joined to the outer wall of the lower panel and to the lower anchor block, respectively, and an aft stiffener is rigidly joined between the lower anchor block and the upper panel, the aft stiffener being joined to the root of the upper panel at a forward location, and the aft stiffener and the outer wall at the junction of the lower panel and lower anchor block being provided with chamfered corners.

A vehicle axle arrangement comprising: a hollow beam member extending along a lengthwise axis; a forward mounting flange projecting radially outward from the beam member along a transverse direction orthogonal to the lengthwise axis for coupling to a chassis; a rearward mounting flange projecting radially outward from the beam member along a direction diverging from the transverse direction for supporting a spring element; and a braking backing plate protruding peripherally from the outer surface of the beam member; wherein the hollow beam member, the forward mounting flange, the rearward mounting flange and the braking backing plate are formed as a single unitary casting.

A chassis module incorporating a unitary axle arrangement, comprising: a hollow axle housing running along a longitudinal axis; a forward mounting flange projecting radially from the housing along a transverse axis orthogonal to the longitudinal axis for coupling to a vehicle body; a rearward mounting flange projecting radially from the housing along a direction diverging from the transverse axis for supporting a flexible suspension member; and a brake anchor plate projecting outwardly from the periphery of the housing; wherein the housing, the forward flange, the rearward flange and the anchor plate are formed as a single casting; and wherein the chassis module further comprises: a shock absorber having one end engaged with the vehicle body and an opposite end engaged with the unitary axle arrangement; and a pneumatic spring unit seated on the rearward flange and engaged with the vehicle body.

A technique for fabricating a airless wheel tyre, the technique comprising: supplying a set of extended strips made of metallic substance; forming the set of extended strips into curved to create a series of metallic struts; molding a first polymer base over a first extremity of every one of the series of metallic struts; furnishing an internal annular member made of metallic substance; securing the internal annular member to the first polymer base; furnishing an external annular member made of metallic substance; attaching the external annular member to a second extremity of every one of the series of metallic struts; furnishing a tread elastomer; and bonding the tread elastomer to the external annular member.

A tyre-less wheel structure comprising: a circumferentially continuous hub band made of a metallic substance; a circumferentially continuous tread band made of a metallic substance; a set of curved metallic struts; a first polymer cap injection-moulded about a first extremity of each curved metallic strut, each first polymer cap being joined to the hub band through one of soldering, fusion bonding, die casting, or bonding by a glue; and a second polymer cap at a second extremity of each curved metallic strut, each second polymer cap being joined to the tread band through one of soldering, fusion bonding, die casting, or bonding by a glue.

A process for fabricating a airless wheel tyre, the process comprising: supplying a set of metallic reinforcing members; encapsulating a first elastomeric base by injection moulding about one extremity of each reinforcing member of the set; encapsulating a second elastomeric base by injection moulding about an opposite extremity of each reinforcing member of the set; furnishing a metallic annular hub; joining the metallic annular hub to the first elastomeric base; furnishing a metallic annular band; joining the metallic annular band to the second elastomeric base; furnishing tread compound; and bonding the tread compound to the metallic annular band.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a set of two annular beads; a casing formed of one or several cord-reinforced sheets running from one bead to the opposite bead while wrapping into a donut-like shape; a crown band encircling the donut-shaped casing; and a belt assembly positioned between the casing and the crown band, the belt assembly including a principal belt stack, a first rubber stratum free of reinforcement situated on the outward-facing side of the principal belt stack, a second rubber stratum free of reinforcement embedded within the principal belt stack, and a shielding belt ply located outward of the first reinforcement-free rubber stratum and inward of the crown band, wherein an outermost belt ply of the principal belt stack carries a multitude of reinforcing filaments, each having a width, the first reinforcement-free rubber stratum possessing a radial depth between 0.5 and 4.0 times the width of those reinforcing filaments, the second reinforcement-free rubber stratum possessing a radial depth between 0.5 and 2.5 times that width, and the second reinforcement-free rubber stratum having an axial span between 0.5 and 1.1 times an overall axial span of the belt assembly, and the first reinforcement-free rubber stratum having an axial span exceeding the overall axial span of the belt assembly.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a pair of annular bead reinforcements; a casing possessing one or several ply layers running from one bead reinforcement to the opposing bead reinforcement in a torus-shaped configuration; a crown region encompassing the torus-shaped casing around its periphery; and a reinforcing belt arrangement located radially between the casing and the crown region, the belt arrangement including a principal belt stratum, a first rubber stratum lacking reinforcement disposed radially outward of the principal belt stratum, a second rubber stratum lacking reinforcement embedded within the principal belt stratum, a third rubber stratum lacking reinforcement embedded within the principal belt stratum, and a protective belt stratum disposed radially outward of the first rubber stratum and radially inward of the crown region, wherein a radially outermost belt ply of the principal belt stratum carries a plurality of reinforcing filaments each of a given diameter, the first rubber stratum has a first radial dimension between 0.5 and 4.0 times said given diameter, the second rubber stratum has a second radial dimension between 0.5 and 2.5 times said given diameter, the third rubber stratum has a third radial dimension between 0.5 and 2.5 times said given diameter, the second rubber stratum has an axial extent between 0.5 and 1.1 times an overall axial extent of the belt arrangement, and the first rubber stratum has an axial extent exceeding the overall axial extent of the belt arrangement.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a crown reinforcement formed of one or more plies; a tread portion; and a sensing unit mounted within the tread portion; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, a quotient of SW divided by an overall diameter OD of the tyre is no greater than 0.26, and the reinforcing filaments of the crown plies are non-metallic.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a crown reinforcement formed of at least one ply of belting; a ground-contacting rubber portion; and a transponder unit embedded within the ground-contacting rubber portion; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, the section width SW in millimetres and an overall diameter OD of the tyre in millimetres obey the inequality OD ≥ −0.0187×SW² + 9.15×SW − 380, the reinforcing cords of the crown reinforcement are textile or polymeric cords lacking any steel filament, and the transponder unit is disposed inside the ground-contacting rubber portion.

A tread cavity cut for a tyre, comprising: facing tread block sections divided by the cut; each facing block section carrying a set of raised lugs and a set of recessed grooves, wherein the raised lugs and recessed grooves present three roughly four-sided flat faces, each flat face set at a right angle to another flat face, the three flat faces converging at a curved end region; the cut having an outer upper zigzag segment; the cut having an inner three-dimensional segment positioned radially beneath the outer upper zigzag segment; and the cut having a lower zigzag segment positioned radially beneath the inner three-dimensional segment.

A pneumatic tread arrangement incorporating a lamella, comprising: first and second tread block flanks bounding the lamella on either side, each flank carrying a series of raised lugs and recessed grooves, wherein the lugs and grooves are defined by three generally four-sided flat faces, each face meeting an adjacent face at a right angle, the three faces converging at a curved apex; wherein the lamella presents an upper undulating segment, a central segment of spatial contour located beneath the upper undulating segment, and a lower undulating segment located beneath the central segment; and wherein the lower undulating segment comprises protrusions extending radially and recesses extending radially opposite the protrusions.

A drivetrain wheel mounting arrangement, comprising: a driveshaft flange adapted to turn around a spin axis; and at least one securing bolt adapted to join the flange with a wheel's outer ring, wherein an axial terminus of the flange presents a first confronting face directed toward one side of the ring, wherein the first confronting face has a section oblique relative to the spin axis, and the securing bolt passes into a region of the one side of the ring that opposes the oblique section of the first confronting face, extending transversely to the oblique section, so as to unite the flange and the ring.

A drive unit arrangement for a powered vehicle, the arrangement comprising: a shaft constructed to turn around a central spin axis; a road wheel affixed to a terminal section of the shaft; and one or more primary securing elements, wherein the terminal section of the shaft presents a first confronting face oriented toward a face of a wheel rim, and each primary securing element passes into a region of the face of the wheel rim together with a region of the first confronting face and joins the shaft to the rim, the primary securing element being angled relative to the spin axis at a first slope.

A hub assembly, optionally for an automobile, comprising: a propeller shaft; a rotating hub member; a threaded fastener having a head portion; and a preload member positioned and/or compressed between the head portion, optionally a lower face of the head portion, and the rotating hub member; wherein the rotating hub member is coupled to the propeller shaft via the threaded fastener.

A caster device, comprising: a mounting frame, an upper section of the mounting frame being coupled to a swivel unit permitting full circumferential pivoting of the caster device; a traction unit including a spindle and a wheel body journaled on the spindle, a planar reference system being defined with a hub of the wheel body as a zero point, a rolling path of the wheel body as a leftward-pointing horizontal axis, and a vertical direction orthogonal thereto pointing upward as a positive vertical axis, the mounting frame defining a guide slot situated in an upper-forward quadrant, the spindle being slidably engaged within the guide slot along a radius of the wheel body; and a damping unit including a dampened elastic member whose lower terminal is attached to the spindle and whose upper terminal is attached to the mounting frame, a first force component being defined as the component, resolved along a travel direction of the spindle, of the tension exerted by the elastic member upon the spindle, a second force component being defined as the component, resolved along the travel direction of the spindle, of a greatest supportable load borne by the spindle, the first force component exceeding the second force component such that the spindle is constrained to remain at a lower extremity of the guide slot absent any externally applied force; and wherein the caster device is configured for enhanced cushioning and elevated capacity to traverse protrusions.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, including a tread; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, and either a quotient SW/OD of that section width over an outside diameter OD of the tyre is 0.26 or smaller, or SW (mm) and OD (mm) obey OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); in a meridional section of the tyre under reference conditions of mounting on a rim, inflation to a specified pressure, and no applied load, a first line m1 through a tread-surface point on the equatorial plane and running parallel to the width direction, and a second line m2 through ground-contact edges E and running parallel to the width direction, with a radial separation between m1 and m2 defined as a drop height L CR and a tread width TW, a ratio L CR/TW exceeding 0.045; and the tread contact surface carries solely one circumferential main groove extending around the tyre, positioned on a vehicle-outboard half of the tread bounded by the equatorial plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising a tread portion, wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, a quotient SW/OD of the section width SW divided by an overall diameter OD of the tyre is 0.26 or smaller, or the section width SW (mm) and the overall diameter OD (mm) of the tyre fulfil the expression OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm), a footprint length measured along a tyre equatorial plane exceeds a mean of footprint lengths taken at locations displaced 20% of a footprint width inwardly in a tyre width direction from both footprint edges, a ground-engaging surface of the tread includes solely one circumferential main groove extending in a tyre circumferential direction, and said circumferential main groove is situated in a half of the tyre lying on a vehicle-outboard side, which is one side of the tyre in a tread width direction bounded by the tyre equatorial plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tire, comprising: a tread portion wherein a section width SW of the tire is below 165 mm; a quotient of the section width SW divided by an overall diameter OD of the tire is 0.26 or smaller, or the section width SW (in mm) and the overall diameter OD (in mm) fulfill the expression OD (mm) being at least −0.0187×SW (mm) squared plus 9.15×SW (mm) minus 380 (mm); a thickness of rubber at the tire equator of the tread exceeds a mean thickness of the rubber measured at locations spaced inwardly along the tire width direction by 20% of a ground-contact width from each ground-contact edge; a tread ground-contacting face bears solely one circumferential primary channel extending along the tire circumference; and the circumferential primary channel sits within the half of the tire lying on a vehicle-outboard side, being the side in the tread width direction bounded by the tire equatorial plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic tire, comprising: a tread portion; wherein a section width SW of the tire is below 165 mm, and a quotient SW/OD of the section width SW divided by an overall diameter OD of the tire is not greater than 0.26, or the section width SW (mm) and the overall diameter OD (mm) meet the expression OD (mm) being at least −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); in a meridional section taken along the width direction, with the tire fitted to a specified rim, inflated to a prescribed pressure, and carrying no load, where a line m1 passes through a tread-surface point lying on the equatorial plane parallel to the width direction, a line m2 passes through ground-contact edges E parallel to the width direction, a radial separation between m1 and m2 defines a drop height L CR, and a tread width of the tire is TW, a ratio L CR/TW exceeds 0.045; when the tire is fitted to the rim, inflated to the prescribed pressure, and subjected to a maximum rated load, the footprint contains only grooves whose width is 2 mm or less, and the footprint includes at least one block-shaped land section bounded by two or more circumferential channels extending along the circumferential direction or inclined at less than 45 degrees thereto and by two or more transverse channels extending along the width direction or inclined at 45 degrees or less thereto.

An automobile-use pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a tread portion; wherein a cross-sectional breadth SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, and a quotient SW/OD of that breadth over an overall diameter OD of the tyre is no greater than 0.26, or the breadth SW (mm) and the diameter OD (mm) of the tyre fulfil the expression OD (mm)≥−0.0187×SW (mm)² +9.15×SW (mm)−380 (mm); a ground-engaging length measured along a tyre equatorial plane exceeds a mean of ground-engaging lengths taken at locations displaced inwardly in a tyre width direction by 20% of a ground-engaging width from both ground-engaging margins, when the tyre is seated on a rim, inflated to a specified internal pressure, and loaded to a maximum load; recesses within a ground-engaging footprint consist exclusively of recesses having a width of 2 mm or less; and the footprint includes at least one block-shaped rib section bounded by two or more circumferential channels that run along a tyre circumferential direction or at an angle below 45° relative thereto and by two or more transverse channels that run along a tyre width direction or at an angle of 45° or less relative thereto; and.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a tread portion; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, a quotient SW/OD of the section width SW over an overall diameter OD of the tyre is 0.26 or smaller, or the section width SW (mm) and the overall diameter OD (mm) of the tyre fulfil the relation OD (mm) being at least −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm), a thickness of the tread measured on a tyre equatorial plane exceeds a mean of tread thicknesses taken at locations displaced 20% of a ground contact width inward in a tyre width direction from both ground contact edges, a ground contact region incorporates one or more block-form land sections bounded by two or more circumferential channels running along a tyre circumference or inclined at less than 45° relative thereto and by two or more lateral channels running along a tyre width or inclined at 45° or less relative thereto, and the ground contact region comprises solely channels having a width of 2 mm or less.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising a tread portion; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, and a quotient of the section width SW divided by an overall diameter OD of the tyre is 0.26 or smaller, or the section width SW (mm) and the overall diameter OD (mm) of the tyre fulfil the expression OD (mm) being greater than or equal to −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); in a meridional cross-section of the tyre under reference conditions in which the tyre is seated on a rim, inflated to a specified pressure, and carries no load, where a first straight line passing through a point on a tread surface located on a tyre equatorial plane and extending parallel to the tyre width direction is designated m1, a second straight line passing through ground-contact edges E and extending parallel to the tyre width direction is designated m2, a radial separation between m1 and m2 is a drop height LCR, and a tread width of the tyre is TW, a ratio LCR/TW exceeds 0.045; a ground-contacting surface of the tread possesses solely two circumferential principal grooves extending along a tyre circumferential direction, and a centroid of the two circumferential principal grooves lies within a half of the tyre situated on a vehicle-inboard side, being one side of the tyre in the tread width direction bounded by the tyre equatorial plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tire, comprising: a tread portion; a cross-sectional width SW of the tire being below 165 mm, with a ratio of the cross-sectional width SW to an overall diameter OD of the tire being 0.26 or smaller, or the cross-sectional width SW (mm) and the overall diameter OD (mm) fulfilling the expression OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); a ground-engaging length measured along a tire equatorial plane exceeding a mean of ground-engaging lengths taken at locations displaced inwardly across the tire width by 20% of a ground-engaging width from both ground-engaging edges; a tread contact face provided with solely two circumferential principal grooves running in a tire circumferential direction; and a centroid of the two circumferential principal grooves lying within a half of the tire on an inboard side when mounted on a vehicle, said half being one lateral side of the tire bounded by the tire equatorial plane in a tread width direction.

A passenger-car pneumatic tire, comprising: a tread band; a cross-sectional width SW below 165 mm with a ratio of SW to overall diameter OD not exceeding 0.26, or SW (mm) and OD (mm) satisfying OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); a tread thickness measured at the equatorial plane exceeding the mean thickness measured at points spaced inwardly 20% of the ground-contact width from both contact edges; a ground-engaging face provided with exactly two circumferential primary channels extending around the tire; and a centroid of the two primary channels located within the half of the tire lying on the inboard side when mounted on a vehicle, bounded by the equatorial plane; the tire being a radial construction.

A pneumatic tyre provided with a lamella, the tyre including: a lamella configured as a spatial slit extending radially downward into the tyre from an outer ground-contacting face of the tyre, the lamella comprising a lateral wave segment having at least one lateral central section and at least one lateral crest section; and a vertical wave segment of the lamella exhibiting a first vertical excursion VA 1 at the at least one lateral central section and a second vertical excursion VA 2 at the at least one lateral crest section, wherein the first vertical excursion VA 1 exceeds the second vertical excursion VA 2.

A pneumatic tread element comprising: a groove-like slit cut radially downward into the rubber body from an outer ground-contacting face, the slit being spatially three-dimensional; a lateral waveform segment having at least one central crest region and at least one lateral apex region; a vertical waveform component exhibiting a first height H1 at the central crest region and a second height H2 at the lateral apex region, the first height H1 exceeding the second height H2; wherein the magnitude of H1 falls between the magnitude of H2 and 1.50 mm, and wherein the magnitude of H2 falls between 0.00 mm and the magnitude of H1.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread section having at least one of a tread band element or a tread lug; a lamella formed within the tread band element or the tread lug, the lamella incorporating a medial sinuous segment disposed axially between two laterally oriented linear segments; a plurality of primary segments inclined toward a first peripheral direction; a plurality of secondary segments inclined toward a second peripheral direction, the secondary segments joining the primary segments; and wherein a leading primary segment crosses a contact face of the tread band element or the tread lug.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering, comprising: a ground-engaging portion including at least one of a circumferential land strip or a discrete raised element; a cut-out formed within the land strip or the raised element, wherein the cut-out includes a series of inclined segments oriented toward a first peripheral direction at an included angle KA measured from a peripheral line parallel to a running face; wherein the cut-out further includes a series of reverse segments oriented toward a second peripheral direction at an included angle RA measured from a peripheral line parallel to the running face, the reverse segments joining adjacent inclined segments; wherein a leading one of the inclined segments breaks through the running face; and wherein a quotient of angle KA divided by angle RA is no less than 5 to 1.

A blade for molding a tire sipe, the blade comprising: an upper insertion section configured to be received within a mold; a lower forming section extending from the upper insertion section and including a set of primary segments inclined toward a first circumferential side at a first inclination angle, a set of secondary segments inclined toward a second circumferential side at a second inclination angle, the secondary segments joining adjacent primary segments, and a leading primary segment coupled to the upper insertion section; wherein a ratio of the first inclination angle to the second inclination angle is no less than 5:1.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering, comprising: an inner liding; a set of reinforcing layers stacked against the inner liding; a running surface situated against the set of reinforcing layers on a side away from the inner liding; and a wear-indicating element mounted within the inner liding, the wear-indicating element including: a foundation member disposed on an inward-facing side of the inner liding; and an elongated conduit projecting from the foundation member through the inner liding and the set of reinforcing layers to a first depth within the running surface, such that a terminal portion of the elongated conduit becomes visible at the exterior of the covering once the running surface has been abraded down to the first depth.

A process for equipping a pneumatic tyre with wear indication, comprising: obtaining a wear-monitoring element possessing a conduit and a mounting flange affixed to a first extremity of the conduit, the wear-monitoring element being arranged to generate a distinctive leakage profile once a tread reaches a predetermined depth of abrasion; and passing the conduit through a liner layer of the tyre so that a second extremity of the conduit resides within the tread at the predetermined depth and the mounting flange lies against the liner layer.
A sensing device, comprising: a plate defining an aperture; a rod projecting outward from the plate; and a conduit linking the aperture of the plate to a far end of the rod.

A tire assembly comprising: a pneumatic casing whose sidewall region, when the casing is seated upon a specified wheel rim, inflated to a designated pressure, and carrying no load, serves as a baseline state; wherein in that baseline state, the weight of the sidewall material lying within a radial band extending from a point located 15% of section height radially inward and a point located 15% of section height radially outward of the widest axial station, is between 1.5% and 5% of the total weight of the tire.

A bicycle wheel circumferential member, comprising: a crown portion adapted to receive a tire; a base portion provided with a series of apertured nipple-receiving mounts; and a pair of lateral walls joining the crown portion to the base portion; wherein at least one of the lateral walls includes at least one indentation whose depth measured parallel to the rotational axis grows progressively in a radial direction within the indentation, moving from the crown portion toward the base portion.

An axle hub assembly for journaling a road wheel to a chassis, the assembly comprising: a turning member that spins in unison with the road wheel; a stationary member secured to the chassis; a series of balls or rollers interposed between the turning member and the stationary member; and a seal arrangement positioned between the turning member and the stationary member to block the entry of debris from outside, wherein the seal arrangement includes a first component fitted to one of the turning member and the stationary member; a second component fitted to the other of the turning member and the stationary member; and a vacuum relief element affixed to the first component, the first component of the seal arrangement defines an aperture that opens into an enclosed cavity formed within the seal arrangement, the vacuum relief element includes a pressure venting passage that places a bearing cavity, which houses the balls or rollers, in fluid communication with the enclosed cavity, and the pressure venting passage is arranged to connect with the bearing cavity at a first location and to connect with the enclosed cavity through the aperture at a second location spaced from the first location.

A hub assembly for journaling and carrying a road wheel relative to a chassis, the hub assembly comprising: a revolving member that turns in unison with the road wheel; a stationary member secured to the chassis; a series of antifriction balls interposed between the revolving member and the stationary member; and a seal arrangement positioned between the revolving member and the stationary member to block ingress of contaminants, wherein the seal arrangement includes a first component fitted to one of the revolving member and the stationary member; and a second component fitted to the other of the revolving member and the stationary member, the first component of the seal arrangement defines a pressure relief passage that places an enclosed seal cavity formed within the seal arrangement in fluid communication with a bearing chamber housing the antifriction balls, and the pressure relief passage is arranged to connect with the bearing chamber at a first location and to connect with the enclosed seal cavity at a second location spaced from the first location.

A rolling assembly comprising: a hub unit having a peripheral shell and a central core; a ground-engaging ring carried on an exterior surface of the peripheral shell; a releasable coupling mechanism that secures the peripheral shell to the central core and that, when disengaged, permits the peripheral shell to rotate relative to the central core; and a rotational support positioned between the central core and the peripheral shell to diminish resistance to such relative rotation.

A castor apparatus for bearing a load and positionable on a floor surface, the apparatus comprising: a housing having a lower aperture and an upper cover; a carrier member received inside the housing and movable along a vertical axis relative to the housing; at least one wheel secured to a first lateral side of the carrier member and engaging the floor surface; at least one resilient member disposed on a second lateral side of the carrier member and bearing against an underside of the upper cover of the housing; and wherein, upon application of a prescribed load to the load supported by the housing, the resilient member is squeezed, causing a lower rim of the housing to engage the floor surface, whereby frictional resistance between the apparatus and the floor surface is increased, rendering the apparatus hard to displace.

A rubber formulation for tire use, including: 100 parts per hundred rubber of at least one diene-based elastomer (A); a minimum of 0.1 phr of at least one reinforcing particulate material (B); between 0.1 and 20 phr of a curing component (C); and a minimum of 0.1 phr of an auxiliary crosslinking package (D) containing at least one methylene-supplying compound (D1) together with at least one methylene-receiving compound (D2) chosen from furoic acid, furoate esters, and furoate salts.

A non-pneumatic wheel component, comprising: a outer contact layer configured to engage a driving surface; an inner support layer configured to mount to a wheel hub; and a lateral wall spanning radially from the outer contact layer down to the inner support layer; a transponder chip being enclosed within the component, the transponder chip being positioned adjacent the lateral wall, and a spacing between the transponder chip and the lateral wall lying in a range of 0.5 mm to 10.0 mm.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, presenting an exterior face and an interior face, comprising: a belt assembly positioned beneath a radially exterior wear layer; the wear layer including a multiplicity of relief blocks aligned at least in part along the peripheral direction and a multiplicity of channels running at least in part along the peripheral direction, each peripheral channel being bounded by an axially inward sidewall, an axially outward sidewall, and a channel floor; at least one of the relief blocks incorporating at least one peripherally extending stiffening member formed from a mixture exhibiting a complex dynamic shear modulus at least double that of a mixture forming the remaining relief blocks, the at least one stiffening member having an axial thickness that tapers progressively with increasing radial closeness to the outermost surface, the axial thickness reaching a peak value below 40% of the axial thickness of the relief block; wherein the mixture of the at least one stiffening member is founded on at least one diene rubber, one reinforcing filler comprising a carbon black possessing an STSA surface area, determined per standard D6556-2016, of at least 90 m2/g, one epoxy resin, one amine-containing hardener, and one vulcanization system.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tyre casing; and an encapsulated transponder unit partially incorporated within the tyre casing, wherein the encapsulated transponder unit includes: a radio module; and an enclosure sheath enveloping a perimeter of the radio module, and the enclosure sheath has a discernible feature that can be visually set apart from an adjacent region of the tyre casing when viewed in a cross-section taken through the encapsulated transponder unit.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre having a signal transmitter; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is under 165 millimetres, and a quotient SW/OD of that section width divided by an overall tyre diameter OD is 0.26 or below; and wherein, when viewed in cross-section along the axial direction under a standard state in which the tyre is seated on a wheel rim, inflated to a specified pressure, and carries no load, the signal transmitter sits within a tyre region bounded by a first imaginary line running radially through a contact patch boundary and a second imaginary line running axially through the location of greatest axial width of the tyre.

An automobile tyre of radial construction intended for light vehicles, the tyre incorporating a wireless transponder unit; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 millimetres, and the section width SW in millimetres and an external diameter OD in millimetres of the tyre fulfil the expression: OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187 × SW(mm)² + 9.15 × SW(mm) − 380; and wherein, when viewed in cross-section along the axial direction of the tyre under a reference state in which the tyre is fitted to a wheel rim, inflated to a specified internal pressure, and carries no load, the transponder unit is disposed within a tyre region bounded by a first imaginary line extending radially through a ground-engaging edge and a second imaginary line extending axially through a maximum-width location of the tyre.
