query_text: A non-pneumatic wheel component, comprising: an outer compound layer positioned toward a ground-engaging face; and an inner compound layer oriented toward a wheel-mounting seat; the inner compound layer exhibiting a Shore-type durometer reading of at least 80 on the JIS-A scale, and a radio-frequency identification transponder being enclosed within the inner compound layer.

A rim assembly for an automobile, the rim assembly comprising: a. an attachment feature adapted to secure the rim assembly to a spindle of the automobile; b. a tinted base layer; and c. a sculpted mirror-like face shaped to redirect tint emanating from the tinted base layer outward from the rim assembly, such that the mirror-like face seems to change in hue.

An ornament retaining apparatus for a wheel cover, comprising: a pair of gripping legs disposed in facing relation on a rear face of an ornament main piece and a resilient wire bracket for bearing the gripping legs; the gripping legs being secured to the ornament main piece by a mounting base; the ornament main piece, the gripping legs and the mounting base being molded as one unitary piece by injection; each of the gripping legs including an upright panel and a holding jaw situated at an upper region on an inner face of the upright panel; the mounting base defining openings along both lateral sides; the resilient wire bracket being shaped from bent and joined wire stock, having a linking section and two bearing sections at opposite ends of the linking section; the linking section being composed of two linking wires whose terminal portions are bent upwardly and joined to form the two bearing sections; the two bearing sections contacting an outer face of the gripping legs, and the two linking wires lying on opposite sides of the mounting base and within the openings.

A tacky film laminate for closing an aperture through a cycle wheel hoop, the laminate comprising: a carrier sheet, and an adhesive coating disposed on a face of the carrier sheet; wherein a 180-degree peel resistance of the laminate, measured after applying the laminate to an aluminum panel and waiting ten seconds, at a pull speed of 300 mm/min and a temperature of 0 degrees Celsius, is at least 2 N per 20 mm; and wherein a static shear holding force of the laminate, measured against an aluminum panel at a temperature of 0 degrees Celsius, is at least 200 N per 400 mm2.

A drive wheel apparatus, the apparatus including a roller that turns around an axle, the roller held by a set of linking elements to pivot about a group of actuators mounted on the axle, the group of actuators being operable to manipulate the linking elements so as to vary a spacing between the axle and a perimeter of the roller.

A drive-wheel apparatus, the apparatus including: a rotor configured to turn around an axle; a set of linkage elements carrying the rotor and coupled to a series of actuators disposed upon the axle; and the actuators being driven to manipulate the linkage elements so that a rotational axis of the rotor is displaceable in an adjustable manner with respect to a rotational axis of the axle.

A drive module comprising: a plurality of actuators mounted on a spindle; a set of linkage elements coupling the actuators to a rim such that the rim is turned by the actuators about a rotational axis of the spindle, the spindle being held stationary and free of rotation about its own longitudinal axis; wherein the actuators are configurable to manipulate the linkage elements so as to selectively displace a rotational axis of the rim laterally with respect to the rotational axis of the spindle.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, comprising: a vulcanizable compound formed at least from a polymeric material and a resinous oligomer; wherein the resinous oligomer is derived from a ring-containing feedstock chosen from a fraction obtained by fractionating a petroleum refining stream, C4, C5 and C6 cyclic alkenes, and combinations thereof; wherein the resinous oligomer exhibits a proportion of aromatic hydrogens (HAr, in mol %), a glass transition temperature (Tg, in degrees Celsius), and a number-average molar mass (Mn, in g/mol) satisfying: 12 mol % ≤ HAr ≤ 19 mol %; Tg ≥ 95 − 2.2 × HAr; Tg ≥ −53 + (0.265 × Mn); and 300 g/mol ≤ Mn ≤ 450 g/mol.

A pneumatic tread article, comprising: a vulcanizable compound built upon at least one elastomeric network containing between 50 and 100 parts per hundred rubber of a butadiene-vinylaromatic interpolymer, wherein vinylaromatic content falls between 0 and 5 weight percent and the glass transition is situated from −110° C. to −70° C.; and a resinous oligomer derived from a cyclic feedstock chosen from a refinery-derived fraction, C4, C5 and C6 cycloolefins, and blends thereof; wherein the oligomer exhibits an aromatic proton fraction HAr in mole percent, a glass transition value Tg in degrees Celsius, and a number-average molar mass Mn in grams per mole satisfying 12 mol % ≤ HAr ≤ 19 mol %, Tg ≥ 95 − 2.2 × HAr, Tg ≥ −53 + 0.265 × Mn, and 300 g/mol ≤ Mn ≤ 450 g/mol.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering comprising: an outer ground-contacting band having a pair of lateral edge regions, each edge region defining a recessed channel; a reinforcing structure disposed radially inward of the band and including a pair of inclined crossing plies together with a near-circumferential ply, the near-circumferential cords forming an orientation of under five degrees relative to the equatorial direction; wherein the near-circumferential ply includes a primary sheet extending across at least seventy percent of the axial extent of the widest inclined ply, and wherein each supplemental sheet of the near-circumferential ply is positioned beneath one of the recessed channels and spans no more than fifty percent of the axial extent of the widest inclined ply.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering comprising: a ground-engaging outer layer and a reinforcing band assembly disposed radially inward of the outer layer, wherein the reinforcing band assembly includes a pair of crossed bracing plies and a near-zero bias band formed from a spirally wrapped strip, the strip having generally aligned cords oriented at less than 5 degrees relative to a peripheral direction of the covering; and wherein the pair of crossed bracing plies includes a leading bracing ply and a trailing bracing ply, each having generally aligned cords, the cords of the leading bracing ply and the cords of the trailing bracing ply intersecting with opposed inclinations, wherein an absolute inclination of the cords of each bracing ply relative to the peripheral direction falls between 10 and 50 degrees, and wherein a magnitude difference between the absolute inclination of the leading bracing ply cords and the absolute inclination of the trailing bracing ply cords is no less than 2 degrees.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering comprising: an outer contact surface and a radially inward band assembly disposed beneath said contact surface, wherein the contact surface presents a first flank region along one lateral edge and a second flank region along an opposite lateral edge; wherein the band assembly includes a pair of inclined stabilizing strata and a near-parallel reinforcement package, the near-parallel reinforcement package incorporating at least one spirally wrapped strip carrying an elongated filament oriented at an angle below 5° relative to the circumferential direction of the covering, and wherein the reinforcement package includes a first stratum, a second stratum and a third stratum formed from said at least one spirally wrapped strip, the first stratum spanning at least 70% of the axial extent of the widest inclined stabilizing stratum, the second stratum positioned radially beneath the first stratum and beneath the first flank region, the third stratum positioned radially above the first stratum and beneath the second flank region, and each of the second stratum and the third stratum spanning no more than 50% of the axial extent of the widest inclined stabilizing stratum.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a tread band; wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, and either a ratio SW/OD of that section width to an overall diameter OD is no more than 0.26, or SW (mm) and OD (mm) obey OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); wherein, in a meridional section of the tyre under reference conditions of mounting on a rim, inflation to a specified pressure and no load, a first line through a tread-surface point on the equatorial plane and parallel to the axial direction is m1, a second line through the ground-contact edges E and parallel to the axial direction is m2, the radial separation of m1 and m2 is a drop height LCR, and the tread width is TW, such that LCR/TW exceeds 0.045; wherein the tread contact face bears one or more circumferential main grooves running in the tyre circumferential direction; and wherein a negative (void) ratio of the half of the tyre on a vehicle-outboard side, bounded by the equatorial plane, exceeds the negative ratio of the half on a vehicle-inboard side, bounded by the same plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising a tread portion; wherein a cross-sectional width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, a quotient SW/OD of that width over an overall diameter OD of the tyre is no more than 0.26, or the width SW in millimetres and the diameter OD in millimetres obey the expression OD ≥ −0.0187×SW² + 9.15×SW − 380; a footprint length measured along the tyre median plane exceeds the mean of footprint lengths taken at locations displaced inboard by 20% of the footprint width from each footprint edge; a ground-engaging face of the tread is provided with one or more circumferentially continuous principal channels; and a void-to-solid ratio of the half of the tyre lying on the outboard side when mounted on a vehicle, bounded by the median plane, is larger than the void-to-solid ratio of the opposite half lying on the inboard side.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a tread portion; a section width SW of the tyre being below 165 mm, a SW-to-overall-diameter OD proportion of 0.26 or lower, or SW (mm) and OD (mm) together obeying the expression OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187 × SW (mm)² + 9.15 × SW (mm) − 380 (mm); a rubber thickness of the tread measured at the tyre centreline exceeding a mean of such thicknesses taken at locations displaced inwardly across the tyre width by 20% of the footprint width from each footprint boundary; a ground-engaging surface of the tread bearing one or more circumferential primary channels running along the tyre circumference; and a void fraction of the half-tyre facing the outboard side when mounted on a vehicle, measured relative to the centre plane as the dividing line, exceeding the void fraction of the opposite half-tyre facing the inboard side, and wherein the foregoing features are present in combination; and wherein the tread is arranged to meet all stated conditions simultaneously.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread section having at least one of a tread land or a tread element; a lamella formed within the tread land or the tread element, the lamella including a medial segment positioned axially between two lateral segments, each of the medial segment and the lateral segments having a radially outward zone and a radially inward zone; wherein the radially outward zone of each lateral segment exhibits a circumferential extent WT1, the radially outward zone of the medial segment exhibits a circumferential extent WT2, and WT1 exceeds WT2; wherein the radially inward zone of each lateral segment includes an axially outboard part with a radial extent DB1E and an axially inboard part with a radial extent DB1I, and DB1E is smaller than DB1I.

A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a tread section having at least one of a tread band or a tread element; a lamella formed within the tread band or the tread element, the lamella having a central segment positioned axially between two opposed lateral segments, the central segment and each lateral segment each having an outer radial region and an inner radial region; wherein the outer radial region of each lateral segment exhibits a peripheral extent WT1 exceeding a peripheral extent WT2 of the outer radial region of the central segment; wherein the inner radial region of each lateral segment exhibits a peripheral extent WB1 smaller than WT1; wherein the inner radial region of the central segment exhibits a peripheral extent WB2 larger than WT2; and wherein WB1 is smaller than WB2, and WB2 is smaller than WT1.

A lamella blade for a tire, the blade having: a middle portion positioned along the axial direction between two opposed lateral portions, the middle portion and each lateral portion each comprising an upper zone and a lower zone; wherein the upper zone of each lateral portion exhibits a peripheral extent W1, the upper zone of the middle portion exhibits a peripheral extent W2, and W1 exceeds W2; and wherein the lower zone of each lateral portion includes an outboard region with a depth D1E and an inboard region with a depth D1I, D1E being smaller than D1I.

A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a tread provided with a groove running uninterrupted around the circumference; wherein the groove includes an upper section, a lower section, and an intermediate section positioned between the upper section and the lower section, wherein a greatest lateral breadth of the groove at the upper section measures 2 mm, wherein the groove is bounded by two facing flanks, and wherein the facing flanks converge toward one another at the lower section, while the facing flanks in the intermediate section diverge from one another.

A tread for a pneumatic vehicle tyre, the tread comprising: a pair of outer shoulder zones including a first outer shoulder zone and a second outer shoulder zone; a central zone disposed axially between the pair of outer shoulder zones, wherein the first outer shoulder zone includes a first peripheral shoulder band and the second outer shoulder zone includes a second peripheral shoulder band, and wherein each shoulder band is bounded by a peripheral shoulder channel; wherein the central zone includes at least two neighboring peripheral tread bands bounding a peripheral tread channel, the tread channel having an upper region, a lower region, and a mid region situated radially between the upper region and the lower region; wherein the tread channel, along substantially all of its peripheral extent, presents a cross-section in which a greatest axial breadth in the upper region is at least 5% less than an axial breadth in the lower region, measured at 5% of an overall radial depth of the tread channel from the floor of the tread channel; in which the axial breadth in the lower region, measured at 5% of the overall radial depth from the floor of the tread channel, is at least 5% less than a greatest axial breadth of the tread channel in the mid region; and in which the greatest axial breadth of the tread channel in the mid region lies within a range of 15% to 50% of the overall radial depth of the tread channel.

A caster element mounted for free rotation about the periphery of a wheel body, the caster element comprising: a core piece defining a bore that receives an axle pin; and an outer sleeve enveloping the exterior surface of the core piece, wherein the core piece and the outer sleeve are formed as a single unit by dual-material injection molding.

A caster assembly comprising: a hub body and a multiplicity of idler elements mounted for free rotation about a periphery of the hub body, each idler element including an inner component defining a bore that receives an axle pin, and an outer component enveloping an exterior surface of the inner component, wherein the inner component and the outer component are unitarily produced via dual-shot injection molding.

A motorcycle-type rotor hub shell, the hub shell being made from a casting or moulding and including: a hollow tubular barrel portion and a rim portion projecting from the barrel portion at each of its two opposing axial ends; and a ring-shaped sleeve press-seated against an interior wall surface of the barrel portion at one of the opposing axial ends.

A brake-hub housing for a two-wheeled motor vehicle, the housing being manufactured by casting or moulding and including: a hollow barrel portion having a tubular wall; a radial rim provided on the barrel portion at each of its two opposed extremities; and a tapered restriction situated on an inward-facing surface of the barrel portion, the restriction narrowing in internal diameter progressively toward an outer face of the barrel portion.

A process for producing a wheel hub shell for a two-wheeled motor vehicle, the process comprising: fabricating a hollow shell main part by casting or moulding, the main part having a tubular wall portion and a radially projecting rim portion situated at each of two opposed end regions of the wall portion; separately fabricating a ring-shaped insert by casting or moulding, the insert being a discrete component apart from the main part; and attaching the ring-shaped insert to an inner surface of the main part at one of the two opposed end regions.

A rotatable carrier for a heavy-duty transport axle assembly, comprising: a tubular body spanning from a leading end to a trailing end, the tubular body including bearing portions that establish a locating external dimension for seating at least one tire mounting ring on the tubular body, the bearing portions being spaced apart about the perimeter by relief zones, each of the relief zones being set inwardly with respect to the bearing portions, the relief zones being produced by cutting material from the tubular body between the bearing portions; and a collar portion extending from the leading end of the tubular body, the collar portion protruding outwardly beyond the tubular body, the at least one tire mounting ring being attachable to the collar portion.

A lug-alignment apparatus comprising: a rod member; a bushing member dimensioned to receive a fastener protruding from a hub of a road wheel; and a linkage joining the rod member to the bushing member, the linkage permitting displacement of the bushing member relative to the rod member.

A tyre assembly, comprising: a set of bead regions; at least one ply structure stretching across the set of bead regions; a reinforcing band arranged radially outward of the ply structure; and an innermost elastomeric liner positioned toward a hollow interior of the tyre relative to the ply structure; the tyre further including an elongated electrically conductive member that runs without interruption from at least one of the bead regions up to the reinforcing band and is laid upon the innermost elastomeric liner; and the elongated electrically conductive member being at least partly embedded within the innermost elastomeric liner and exhibiting a bulk resistivity below 1×10{circumflex over ( )}8 Ω·cm.

A reinforcing wire element coated with a sulfur-vulcanizable rubber compound that is substantially free of cobalt, wherein the reinforcing wire element is a steel cable composed of one or more strands, each strand comprising a steel base wire and a layer that fully or partially envelops the base wire, the layer being formed of a copper-zinc alloy and being doped with iron as dispersed particles between 10 and 10,000 nm in size within the alloy, and wherein the rubber compound incorporates 0.5 to 3 phr, relative to 100 parts by weight of total elastomer, of at least one sulfenimide accelerator and/or at least one dibenzylamine-derived sulfenamide accelerator.

A tire for a vehicle wheel, the tire including: a belt assembly having an inner ply positioned radially inward of a tread portion and an outer ply stacked radially outward of the inner ply; wherein a gauge of the inner ply and a gauge of the outer ply, measured at a central zone of the tire, are each no greater than 1.00 mm; wherein, letting a be the minimum spacing between a cord of the outer ply and a cord of the inner ply at the central zone and letting b be the minimum spacing between the cord of the outer ply and the cord of the inner ply at a shoulder edge, the ratio b/a satisfies 1.8 ≤ b/a ≤ 4.0; and a topping compound encasing the inner ply and the outer ply, the topping compound comprising a rubber base containing natural rubber, a resinous modifier, and a sulfenamide-type curing promoter.

A pneumatic tire comprising: a ground-engaging tread section, bounded by a first shoulder boundary and a second shoulder boundary, and incorporating a number of circumferential channels running uninterrupted in the circumferential sense between the first shoulder boundary and the second shoulder boundary so as to delimit a set of rib-like blocks separated by those channels; the set of blocks including an inner block situated between the first shoulder boundary and the equatorial plane of the tire, and a further inner block situated between the second shoulder boundary and the equatorial plane; each of the inner block and the further inner block exhibiting a first flank oriented toward the first shoulder boundary, a second flank oriented toward the second shoulder boundary, and an external contact face lying between the first flank and the second flank; the inner block furnished with a plurality of first transverse notches extending from the first flank to the second flank of the inner block; the further inner block furnished with a plurality of second transverse notches extending from the first flank to the second flank of the further inner block; each first transverse notch being slanted relative to the axial direction of the tire toward a first heading proceeding from the first flank toward the second flank; each second transverse notch comprising a first slanted segment running from the first flank toward the second flank while being tilted relative to the axial direction, and a second slanted segment running from the second flank toward the first flank while being tilted relative to the axial direction in a sense opposite to the first slanted segment; and wherein, in a top plan view of the tread section, when imaginary extension bands are formed by projecting the circumferential spans of the respective second transverse notches toward the first shoulder boundary parallel to the axial direction, the imaginary extension bands each overlap apertures of the first transverse notches such that an overlapping region between each imaginary extension band and one of the apertures amounts to no more than fifty percent of the area of said one of the apertures.

A procedure for installing a set of four tire assemblies onto a motor vehicle having a leading axle and a trailing axle, the procedure comprising: furnishing four tires, namely a first tire, a second tire, a third tire, and a fourth tire, wherein each tire possesses an outboard face, an inboard face, and a ring-shaped tread encircling the tire, wherein the outboard face of every tire is essentially identical, wherein the inboard face of every tire is essentially identical, wherein the ring-shaped tread of every tire is essentially identical, and wherein the ring-shaped tread of every tire comprises a multitude of tread blocks, each tread block having a ground-contacting face and lateral margins, each tread block carrying a slit arrangement composed of a plurality of slits inclined relative to a depth direction of the tire, wherein the slits are located on a first half of the tread block and no slits are located on a second half of the tread block, wherein the slit arrangement imparts to the tire a first performance attribute when the tire is fitted to the vehicle in a first disposition and turned in a first forward direction of rotation, and a second performance attribute differing from the first performance attribute when the tire is fitted to the vehicle in a second disposition and turned in a second forward direction of rotation, the performance attribute being chosen from the set consisting of braking, dry traction, acoustic emission, tread wear, and snow traction; affixing the first tire to a first rim; affixing the second tire to a second rim; affixing the third tire to a third rim; affixing the fourth tire to a fourth rim; securing the first rim to a left terminus of the leading axle in the first disposition, such that the outboard face of the first tire points away from the vehicle; securing the second rim to a right terminus of the leading axle in the first disposition, such that the outboard face of the second tire points away from the vehicle; securing the third rim to a left terminus of the trailing axle in the first disposition, such that the inboard face of the third tire points away from the vehicle; and securing the fourth rim to a right terminus of the trailing axle in the first disposition, such that the inboard face of the fourth tire points away from the vehicle.

A technique for rotating a set of four tread-identical pneumatic tires among the axles and corners of a motor vehicle having a leading axle and a trailing axle, the technique comprising: supplying four tires, namely a first tire, a second tire, a third tire, and a fourth tire, each tire presenting an outboard-facing first flank, an opposite second flank, and a ring-shaped tread extending about its periphery and carrying a multiplicity of tread blocks, each tread block bearing an arrangement of slits angled through its depth, the slits confined to one half of the block while the other half is solid, whereby the tire yields a first traction characteristic when installed in a first attitude and driven in a first forward sense, and a second traction characteristic distinct from the first when installed in a second attitude and driven in a second forward sense, the first flanks of all four tires being essentially identical, the second flanks being essentially identical, and the treads being essentially identical; fitting the first tire to a first rim; fitting the second tire to a second rim; fitting the third tire to a third rim; fitting the fourth tire to a fourth rim; securing the first rim on a left terminal of the leading axle with the first flank of the first tire directed away from the vehicle and the first tire held in the first attitude; securing the second rim on a right terminal of the leading axle with the second flank of the second tire directed away from the vehicle and the second tire held in the first attitude; securing the third rim on a left terminal of the trailing axle with the first flank of the third tire directed away from the vehicle and the third tire held in the first attitude; securing the fourth rim on a right terminal of the trailing axle with the second flank of the fourth tire directed away from the vehicle and the fourth tire held in the first attitude; detaching the first rim and first tire from the leading axle; detaching the second rim and second tire from the leading axle; detaching the third rim and third tire from the trailing axle; detaching the fourth rim and fourth tire from the trailing axle; securing the first rim and first tire on the right terminal of the trailing axle with the first flank directed away from the vehicle and the first tire held in the second attitude; securing the second rim and second tire on the left terminal of the trailing axle with the second flank directed away from the vehicle and the second tire held in the second attitude; securing the third rim and third tire on the right terminal of the leading axle with the first flank directed away from the vehicle and the third tire held in the second attitude; and securing the fourth rim and fourth tire on the left terminal of the leading axle with the second flank directed away from the vehicle and the fourth tire held in the second attitude.

A technique for fitting a tread assembly onto a motor vehicle, the technique comprising: furnishing a tread assembly possessing an outboard face, an inboard face, and an annular contact band encircling the assembly, wherein the outboard face establishes a first advancing spin sense that is counterclockwise when the assembly is affixed to a vehicle in a first attitude as observed from the outboard face, wherein the inboard face establishes a second advancing spin sense of the assembly that is counterclockwise when the assembly is affixed to the vehicle in a second attitude reversed relative to the first attitude as observed from the outboard face, wherein the annular contact band comprises a plurality of tread blocks, wherein at least one of the tread blocks comprises a lamella arrangement including a plurality of lamellae inclined through a thickness dimension of the assembly, wherein the lamellae are confined to a first moiety of the tread block with none located on a second moiety of the tread block, wherein the lamella arrangement induces the assembly to display a first tire behavior selected from the set consisting of stopping, dry grip, acoustics, abrasion resistance, and snow grip when the assembly is affixed to the vehicle in the first attitude and turned in the first advancing spin sense, and wherein the lamella arrangement induces the assembly to display a second tire behavior differing from the first tire behavior when the assembly is affixed to the vehicle in the second attitude and turned in the second advancing spin sense; installing the assembly on the vehicle in the first attitude for propelling the vehicle under a first set of circumstances; and installing the assembly on the vehicle in the second attitude for propelling the vehicle under a second set of circumstances.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising a tread portion, wherein a section width SW of the tyre is below 165 mm, and either a quotient SW/OD of that section width over an overall diameter OD is no greater than 0.26, or the section width SW in millimetres and the overall diameter OD in millimetres obey the inequality OD ≥ −0.0187×SW² + 9.15×SW − 380; wherein, on a meridional section taken under a standard condition in which the tyre is seated on a rim, inflated to a specified pressure and carrying no load, a first line m1 is drawn through a point on the tread surface lying on the equatorial plane parallel to the axial direction, a second line m2 is drawn through ground-contacting edges E parallel to the axial direction, and a radial separation between m1 and m2 defines a drop height LCR, a tread width TW being given, such that the ratio LCR/TW exceeds 0.045; a ground-contacting surface of the tread being provided with at least one circumferential main groove running in the circumferential direction; and a negative-space proportion of a half of the tyre lying on a vehicle-inboard side of the equatorial plane, measured across the tread width direction, being larger than a negative-space proportion of the other half lying on a vehicle-outboard side of the equatorial plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic radial tyre, comprising: a tread band; a cross-sectional breadth SW of the tyre below 165 mm, with a SW/OD proportion of 0.26 or less, or with SW (mm) and an overall diameter OD (mm) satisfying the expression OD (mm) ≥ −0.0187×SW (mm)² + 9.15×SW (mm) − 380 (mm); a footprint length measured along the equatorial plane of the tyre exceeding the mean of the footprint lengths taken at locations displaced 20% of the footprint width inwardly in the tyre width direction from both footprint edges; a tread-facing surface provided with one or more principal circumferential channels running in the tyre circumferential direction; and a void ratio of the half of the tyre lying on a vehicle-inboard side, delimited from the other half by the equatorial plane, being larger than a void ratio of the half lying on a vehicle-outboard side, likewise delimited by the equatorial plane.

A passenger-car pneumatic tire comprising: a tread portion, wherein a cross-sectional width SW is below 165 mm, and a quotient of SW divided by an overall diameter OD is 0.26 or smaller, or SW (in mm) and OD (in mm) obey the expression OD ≥ −0.0187×SW² + 9.15×SW − 380; a thickness of the tread measured along the equatorial plane exceeds a mean thickness of the tread taken at locations spaced inwardly, in the axial direction, by 20% of the footprint width from each footprint boundary; a ground-engaging surface of the tread includes at least one longitudinally extending principal channel; and a void-to-land proportion of a half of the tire lying on an inboard side when mounted on a vehicle, bounded by the equatorial plane, exceeds the void-to-land proportion of the opposite half lying on an outboard side, bounded by the same plane; and wherein the tire is a radial-ply construction.

A wheel-mounting bearing assembly defining a central spin axis, comprising: a fixed outer race; a rotary carrier possessing an outwardly projecting collar at an outboard end and an axially elongated sleeve-like section at an inboard end, the sleeve-like section bearing an outwardly directed spline arrangement, a segment of the carrier positioned radially within the outer race, and the carrier being turnable about the spin axis relative to the outer race; an inner race fitted onto the carrier in axial contact with an external radial step of the carrier, a splined collar placed inboard of the inner race and presenting an inner bore surface with at least one channel engaging the spline arrangement; wherein the sleeve-like section exhibits an outer round cylindrical face, wherein an axial stretch of the bore surface of the splined collar sits upon or is delimited by a first virtual cylinder, wherein that axial stretch of the bore surface contacts the outer round cylindrical face, and wherein the first virtual cylinder and the outer round cylindrical face are coaxial.

A ratchet-type rear sprocket assembly for a cycle, including: a drive member and a sleeve member, each mounted on a spindle so as to turn around a shared rotational centerline; a catch element arrangement having at least one latch piece, seated within a radial pocket so as to shift between an engaged setting and a disengaged setting; and a biasing mechanism that urges the latch piece toward the engaged setting; wherein the pocket is formed in one of the drive member and the sleeve member, while the other of the drive member and the sleeve member carries a radial toothed arrangement or is coupled to it for joint rotation; wherein the outer face of the latch piece presents a transmitting face that abuts a bearing face of the pocket in the engaged setting, while a hooking section of the latch piece meshes with the toothed arrangement; such that, upon the drive member turning in a first rotational sense about the centerline, rotational force passes from the drive member to the sleeve member through the transmitting face, and wherein, in the disengaged setting, the latch piece permits the sleeve member to turn relative to the drive member in the first rotational sense, wherein over half of the transmitting face is configured as a flat zone.

A wrench tool, comprising: a grip section; a housing defining a primary receptacle bore; and a removable liner disposed inside said primary receptacle bore; wherein said liner can be extracted from said primary receptacle bore; wherein said grip section is adapted to engage an interior hex fastener to turn said interior hex fastener; and wherein said liner is adapted to engage an exterior hex fastener head to turn said exterior hex fastener.

An apparatus for fabricating a tyre having a hub defining a central axis, an outer circumferential ring coaxial with the hub, and multiple radial struts linking the hub to the outer circumferential ring, each strut including a first base fixed to an outward-facing surface of the hub providing a first seating surface and a second base fixed to an inward-facing surface of the outer circumferential ring providing a second seating surface, the apparatus comprising: a set of compression subassemblies each dedicated to securing an individual strut and each including at least one presser configured to force one of the first and second bases of a given strut against the seating surface of the hub or the outer circumferential ring respectively corresponding to that base; wherein each compression subassembly includes at least one carriage supported for radial displacement relative to the central axis under command of an actuation mechanism and carrying a bar extending radially from a fixing location, at which the bar is rigidly joined to the carriage, to a support element spaced axially from the fixing location along the central axis, the bar resting against the presser at a contact region located on a rear side of the presser, radially opposite the base and the seating surface, and also lying within an axial extent occupied by the base along the central axis, such that, when the actuation mechanism radially displaces the carriage, the bar conveys through the support element a clamping load urging the presser, and thereby the base of the strut, against the seating surface, while an elastic flexural capacity of the bar provides resilient radial compliance of the presser relative to the carriage and thus relative to the base of the strut and the seating surface; and.

A tire fabrication apparatus for joining a plurality of web members to a central boss and to an outer ring of a tire, the boss defining a rotational axis and the outer ring being concentric with the boss, each web member having an inner extremity secured to an exposed outward surface of the boss, establishing a first abutment surface, and an outer extremity secured to an exposed inward surface of the outer ring, establishing a second abutment surface, the apparatus comprising: a series of compression modules, each dedicated to securing a respective web member and each including at least one plunger configured to urge one of the inner and outer extremities of that web member toward the corresponding abutment surface of the boss or outer ring; wherein each compression module includes a driver element movable along a direction parallel to the rotational axis under the influence of an actuation mechanism, and provided with at least one inclined cam surface that gradually departs from that direction within a radial plane including the rotational axis, the cam surface engaging a follower affixed to the plunger such that axial displacement of the driver element against the follower forces the follower and the plunger to shift radially and thereby, through the follower, produces a gripping load pressing the plunger and the associated extremity of the web member radially against the abutment surface; and a frame supporting the compression modules in angularly spaced relation about the rotational axis.

A castor apparatus comprising: a swivel element that pivots about an upright centerline; a support frame defining an internal cavity and projecting diagonally downward from a bottom end of the swivel element; a transverse spindle mounted horizontally beneath the support frame; a first roller secured to a left extremity of the spindle; and a second roller secured to a right extremity of the spindle; wherein the support frame includes: a spindle carrier slidably housed within the internal cavity for vertical displacement and bearing the spindle; a helical biasing coil housed within the internal cavity and urging the spindle carrier downward; and a perimeter reinforcing wall encircling the internal cavity; and wherein the spindle carrier includes: a bearing head shaped like a tadpole body, serving as the rounded portion of that shape, and provided with a bore through which the spindle passes; and a flexible arm serving as the elongated tail of that shape, the flexible arm being integrally joined to the perimeter reinforcing wall; the bearing head being pressed against the perimeter reinforcing wall by the helical biasing coil, and the flexible arm and the helical biasing coil being configured to flex and compress, respectively, to absorb impact when the first roller and the second roller traverse a floor irregularity.

A tread compound for a pneumatic tire, the compound consisting essentially of: a. a rubber matrix totaling 100 parts, the matrix including: i. no less than 45 parts of one or more polybutadiene-styrene copolymers bearing a group reactive toward silica, and ii. between 10 and 55 parts of natural caoutchouc, polyisoprene, or a mixture thereof; b. a silica reinforcer present at 50 to 150 phr; c. between 11 and 40 phr of at least one resinous hydrocarbon possessing a glass transition temperature of roughly 35 to roughly 60 degrees Celsius; d. under 10 phr of a plasticizing oil; and e. a vulcanization system; wherein the sum of (c) and (d) is below 50 phr.

A tread compound for a pneumatic tire, the compound comprising: a. 100 parts by weight of a rubbery matrix including: i. not less than 50 parts of one or more styrene-butadiene polymers bearing a silica-interacting moiety, each exhibiting a glass transition temperature from about −65 to about −40° C., and ii. from 10 to 50 parts of natural caoutchouc, synthetic cis-1,4-polyisoprene, or a mixture thereof; b. at least one precipitated silica reinforcer present at 50 to 89 phr; c. from 11 to 40 phr of a hydrocarbon tackifying resin possessing a glass transition temperature of about 35 to about 60° C.; d. below 10 phr of a process oil; and e. a vulcanizing system; wherein components (c) and (d) together do not exceed 40 phr, and the compound includes no more than 20 phr of carbon black.

A tread compound for a pneumatic tire, the compound comprising: a. 100 parts by weight of a rubbery matrix including: i. no less than 50 parts of a pair of styrene-butadiene copolymers each bearing a functional moiety capable of bonding with silica, each copolymer exhibiting a glass transition temperature between roughly −65 and −40° C. and a weight-average molecular weight from 250,000 to 600,000 g/mol, ii. 10 to 50 parts of natural caoutchouc, synthetic cis-1,4-polyisoprene, or a mixture thereof, and iii. up to 5 phr of polybutadiene elastomer; b. 50 to 89 phr of a precipitated silica reinforcer; c. 11 to 40 phr of a hydrocarbon resinous tackifier having a glass transition temperature of about 35 to about 60° C.; d. below 10 phr of a processing oil; and e. a vulcanization system, wherein the combined quantity of (c) and (d) does not exceed 40 phr and the compound includes no more than 20 phr of carbon black.

An airplane pneumatic tire of the radial type, presenting a tread band, a belt assembly and a radially disposed casing ply structure; wherein the casing ply structure includes several plies formed from fibrous reinforcing strands aligned largely along the radius, namely at an inclination lying from 75 to 105 degrees relative to the peripheral direction, each ply being secured to at least one annular bead wire in each bead region; wherein the radially aligned strands of the casing plies are hybrid cords incorporating at least one aromatic polyamide multifilament thread whose breaking load FR, determined per standard D885/D885M-10A, and which elongate by no less than 4.6 percent and no more than 6.5 percent under an applied load equal to FR divided by four; and wherein the tenacity of the strands of the casing plies is no less than 80 daN/mm2 and the linear density of the aromatic polyamide thread or threads is no less than 210 tex.

query_text: A pneumatic tire for a light-duty truck, comprising: a pair of circular bead regions axially separated along a spin axis of the tire; a pair of flank walls axially separated along the spin axis, each flank wall of the pair extending radially outward from a respective bead region of the pair of bead regions with respect to the spin axis; a circumferential carcass section positioned laterally between the pair of flank walls and encircling the tire; the carcass section including a tread composed of an elastomer disposed circumferentially about the carcass section and presenting an outer road-contacting surface over which the tire is designed to travel, the tread possessing a radial thickness and an axial breadth, the tread defining a wear-bearing portion of the tire; the carcass section further including one or more belt layers each constituting a stratum of elastomer strengthened by a plurality of elongated filaments distributed in an ordered arrangement, the one or more belt layers disposed radially inward of and beneath the tread; the carcass section further including a pair of shoulder regions, each shoulder region forming a part of the carcass adjacent a respective flank wall; the tread incorporating a plurality of surface cut-outs extending into the radial thickness of the tread, the cut-outs including transverse slits, transverse channels, and longitudinal channels, the longitudinal channels disposed to delimit a plurality of bands, each band encircling the tread and adjacent bands being separated by one of the longitudinal channels, the plurality of bands comprising a pair of outboard bands and a plurality of inboard bands, each outboard band situated along a respective one of opposed axial margins of the outer road-contacting surface and within a respective one of the shoulder regions, the plurality of inboard bands positioned between the pair of outboard bands; the surface cut-outs extending into the tread thickness substantially to a depth establishing a tread wear limit, the wear limit being the portion of the tread thickness intended to be consumed over the service life of the tread; wherein at least one of the plurality of inboard bands is uninterrupted in the circumferential direction; and wherein the elastomer forming the carcass section exhibits a compression set exceeding 4%.

A molding apparatus comprising: a tire die including a sidewall forming face bearing a non-directional coarse relief arrangement that runs around the circumference of the sidewall forming face, thereby imprinting at least one ring-shaped outer surface of a tire flank with a roughened, uneven texture; the coarse relief arrangement establishing depressed zones distributed irregularly between elevated zones, the depressed zones possessing a depth of no less than 0.1 millimeters.

A tire-forming die assembly comprising: a die body defining a flank-forming face bearing a recessed relief pattern that runs around the circumference of the face, the recessed relief pattern imparting an uneven coarse texture to at least one ring-shaped outer region of a tire wall; wherein the recesses of the relief pattern lie at irregular spacings and exhibit a cavity depth of no less than 0.1 millimeters.

A spoked wheel assembly, including: a central boss; an outer circumferential ring; and a set of pliant airfoil-profiled struts, each strut including: a compliant filamentary core having a proximal terminus and a distal terminus, an inner sheath enveloping the filamentary core, and an outer sheath of profiled cross-section enveloping the inner sheath; wherein the proximal terminus of the filamentary core is secured to the outer ring, and wherein the distal terminus of the filamentary core is secured to the central boss.

A hubcap apparatus for an automotive tire rim, the hubcap apparatus comprising: a mounting assembly configured to receive a dome-shaped shield and to attach relative to a wheel nave, wherein the mounting assembly includes a foundation panel secured relative to a drive axle hub upon which a tire rim is also seated; a raised support frame fixed to the foundation panel; a resilient cap plate coupled to the support frame and disposed to contact the dome-shaped shield; a retention peg borne by the support frame and engaging the hubcap when fully installed so as to resist counter-rotation and disengagement from the support frame; the dome-shaped shield being arranged to slidingly couple with the mounting assembly and having an incorporated flange narrowing toward a periphery of the tire rim; and a set of posts unitary with the mounting assembly and shaped to receive the dome-shaped shield, the set of posts spanning between the support frame and the cap plate.

A hubcap apparatus for an automotive rim, the apparatus comprising: a mounting assembly configured to hold a dome-shaped shield and to be secured relative to a axle flange on which the rim is likewise carried, wherein the mounting assembly includes a foundation panel fixed to a vehicle axle flange; a vertical support member secured to the foundation panel; a resilient cap plate attached to the support member and disposed to contact the dome-shaped shield; the dome-shaped shield arranged to slidingly couple with the mounting assembly, the dome-shaped shield having a flared lip that narrows toward a rim periphery; and a set of posts unified with the mounting assembly and arranged to accept the dome-shaped shield, the set of posts extending between the support member and the cap plate.

A hub-mounted ornamental covering arrangement comprising: a base assembly configured to be secured relative to a rotating hub, the base assembly carrying a set of projecting posts; a dome-shaped shell configured to slidingly couple with the set of projecting posts such that the shell is retained in place by enlarged terminal ends of the posts, the shell possessing a unitary curved flange extending over and substantially concealing an adjacent road wheel; wherein the shell incorporates a locking element that irreversibly engages the shell with the base assembly; and an aperture formed centrally through a flat mounting section of the shell.

A rolling support apparatus, comprising: a bracket configured to be coupled to a transportable structure; a pivot unit housed inside the bracket, the pivot unit including: a rotary element possessing a first recess and a second recess; a latch arrangement having a translatable catch configured to restrict an angular travel of the rotary element by selectively entering one of the first recess or the second recess, wherein a breadth of the first recess defines a first angular travel of the rotary element and a breadth of the second recess defines a second angular travel of the rotary element; and a fork linked to the rotary element, the fork including a middle portion and a pair of limbs projecting from opposing ends of the middle portion; and a roller supported between the pair of limbs of the fork.

A rolling support apparatus comprising: a carrier housing couplable to a transportable article; a rotational coupling disposed inside the carrier housing, the rotational coupling including: a rotary element possessing one or more notches; a retention unit having a translatable latch configured to restrict an angular travel of the rotary element by selectively entering each of the one or more notches, wherein a respective breadth of each of the one or more notches matches a respective distinct angular travel of the rotary element; and a fork linked to the rotary element, the fork including a middle portion and a pair of prongs projecting from opposing ends of the middle portion; and a roller carried between the pair of prongs of the fork.

A rolling support device comprising: a base bracket configured to couple with a transportable apparatus; a pivot unit disposed inside the base bracket, the pivot unit including: a rotatable disc provided with one or more recesses; and a latch mechanism having a slidable element configured to restrict an angular travel of the rotatable disc by selectively seating within one of the one or more recesses, the slidable element movable among a first secured state, a second secured state, and a released state; and a fork coupled to the rotatable disc, the fork including a middle portion and two prongs projecting from opposing extremities of the middle portion; and a roller carried between the two prongs of the fork.

A cycle wheel covering, optionally a bike covering, comprising: a compounded elastomer blend incorporated into at least one structural member, the blend including at least one elastomeric polymer, optionally a polydiene elastomer; and at least one non-elastomeric material obtained from bio-based feedstock.

A method of fabricating a cycle tyre, ideally a pushbike tyre, the method comprising: (a) compounding at least one elastomer blend in which at least one elastomer and at least one bio-derived additive, other than rubber, are incorporated; (b) shaping the elastomer blend from step (a) into a tread or sidewall section of a cycle tyre; (c) applying the section from step (b) onto or within an unvulcanized tyre carcass; and (d) curing the unvulcanized tyre carcass from step (c).

A vehicle pneumatic tyre comprising: a casing incorporating a multitude of fabric reinforcing filaments; a crown layer disposed radially exterior to the casing; and a restraining ply of a restraining band positioned radially exterior to the crown layer, wherein the restraining ply includes a multitude of fabric cords serving as reinforcement, the fabric cords being oriented substantially in parallel with one another and encapsulated within rubber compound, wherein each cord consists of exactly two strands, the two strands being polyamide 6.6 (PA 6.6) strands of identical linear density that are twisted together at their ends to form the cord; and wherein the multitude of fabric cords exhibits a tangent modulus of 9.3 N/% to 14 N/% at an elongation of 4%.

A pneumatic tyre for a motor vehicle, comprising: a casing; a set of fabric reinforcing components incorporated in the casing; a crown layer disposed radially outward of the casing; a circumferential restraint; a restraint ply forming part of the circumferential restraint, the restraint ply disposed radially outward of the crown layer; a series of fabric filaments acting as reinforcing members within the restraint ply and oriented generally side by side; the filaments each consisting of two strands of polyamide 6.6 having identical linear density and being plied together by end-twisting to form the filament; the filaments exhibiting a tangent modulus of 9.3 N/% to 14 N/% at a 4% extension; and the filaments arranged at a pick count of 80 to 100 ends per decimetre, possessing a twist multiplier of 120 to 220, and carrying an adhesive impregnation.

A pneumatic vehicle covering having a running face section including at least an outer stratum defining the ground-engaging surface and an inner stratum positioned radially beneath the outer stratum, wherein each of the outer stratum and the inner stratum is formed from a vulcanizable elastomeric compound containing a polymeric base material and a softening oil, wherein a disparity (AE 1 −AE 2 ) between an acetone-soluble fraction AE 1 of the compound forming the outer stratum and an acetone-soluble fraction AE 2 of the compound forming the inner stratum exceeds 6.0% by mass, and wherein, when the outer stratum and the inner stratum are bonded together and subjected to a cyclic load of 0.45 MPa at a frequency of 50 Hz and a temperature of 80° C. for 120 hours, the percentage variation in the acetone-soluble fraction of the compound forming the outer stratum measured before and after such exposure is between −10% and 10%.

A pneumatic tire for a motor vehicle, comprising: a flank region bearing at least one ornamental motif extending across at least a peripheral segment of the flank; the motif including raised-pattern elements, glossy plain elements, and a background grid adjoining these elements, the grid being composed of non-forking, non-crossing grid strands; wherein the raised-pattern elements replicate a mirror image or a silhouette of at least some areas of the glossy plain elements, and the raised-pattern elements exhibit greater light absorption than the background grid; and wherein each raised-pattern element carries a surface-filling contrast lattice having forked strand segments, each forked strand segment presenting junction nodes from which it radiates along at least three separate paths.

A pneumatic tyre, comprising: a sidewall compound; a bead apex; a casing layer having a ply with a reinforcing thread; and an identification module, wherein the identification module incorporates a radio-frequency transponder and an encapsulating elastomer layer enclosing the transponder, the identification module is positioned between the sidewall compound and the bead apex, a 100% modulus M100 of the sidewall compound is lower than a 100% modulus M100 of the encapsulating elastomer layer, the 100% modulus M100 of the encapsulating elastomer layer is lower than a 100% modulus M100 of an adjoining bead apex section of the bead apex that abuts the identification module, a loss tangent tan δ of the sidewall compound exceeds a loss tangent tan δ of the adjoining bead apex section, and a thermal conductivity of the reinforcing thread exceeds a thermal conductivity of each of the adjoining bead apex section and the encapsulating elastomer layer.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, comprising: a sidewall elastomer; a bead apex; a casing structure having a ply layer incorporating a reinforcing filament; and a transponder assembly, wherein the transponder assembly incorporates a radio-frequency identification chip and an elastomeric encapsulant layer enclosing the chip, the transponder assembly is positioned between the sidewall elastomer and the bead apex, a 100% modulus M100 of the sidewall elastomer is less than a 100% modulus M100 of the elastomeric encapsulant layer, the 100% modulus M100 of the elastomeric encapsulant layer is less than a 100% modulus M100 of an adjoining bead apex section of the bead apex in contact with the transponder assembly, and a dynamic storage modulus E′ of the sidewall elastomer is less than a dynamic storage modulus E′ of the adjoining bead apex section.

An acoustic dampening apparatus comprising: a looped enclosure shell that delimits an interior cavity and can expand along its perimeter; and an unformed acoustic dampening medium that is contained within the interior cavity of the enclosure shell.

A ground-engaging wheel assembly comprising: a round hub plate joined to an inner rim of a cylindrical drum; a cylindrical drum configured at an exterior rim to receive a selected tyre; a hub plate provided with a set of stud apertures distributed about a central axis, each stud aperture positioned along a respective spoke line extending outward from the central axis; a reinforcing web secured to both the drum and the hub plate at a location midway between neighboring spoke lines; and a grip member secured to the drum at a position displaced from every spoke line; and a plurality of reinforcing webs.

An apparatus for rendering visual information on a rotating road-vehicle component, comprising: a screen unit adapted to be mounted at least in part onto a tire rim of an automobile; and a processing module adapted to: acquire imagery intended for display on a surface of the screen unit, obtain kinematic information reflecting a travel characteristic of the automobile, and modify the imagery according to both a frame update frequency of the screen unit and the travel characteristic of the automobile.

A computer-executed technique, comprising: retrieving, by an onboard wheel-mounted processing apparatus, imagery intended for display on a screen of a visual output unit, the visual output unit being adapted for partial mounting onto a rim of an automobile; acquiring, by the onboard wheel-mounted processing apparatus, automotive telemetry indicating a kinematic quantity of the automobile; and carrying out, by the onboard wheel-mounted processing apparatus, a modification of the imagery according to: (i) a frame update frequency of the visual output unit, and (ii) the kinematic quantity of the automobile.

A motorized conveyance, comprising: a rotatable road-engaging member; and an onboard data processing apparatus including: a screen module configured to be mounted at least partly upon the road-engaging member, and a processing circuitry configured to: acquire material intended for display on a visual output surface of the screen module, obtain kinematic information indicating a movement characteristic of the motorized conveyance, and carry out a modification of the material based on: (i) an image update frequency of the screen module, and (ii) the movement characteristic of the motorized conveyance.

A conveyance apparatus comprising: a chassis configured to carry a payload; a set of rolling assemblies, each rolling assembly having a central boss, a peripheral band, and a compliant coupling positioned between the boss and the band; a group of drive units delivering torque to the rolling assemblies via the bosses; wherein the rolling assemblies transmit torque from the bosses to the peripheral bands such that acceleration in a first angular sense differs from acceleration in a second, opposite angular sense; the compliant coupling comprising neighboring flexible members, each pair defining an oval gap therebetween whose long axis is oriented obliquely relative to a substantially radial line of the neighboring flexible members, and wherein an apex of curved sections of the neighboring flexible members alternates between lying nearer the peripheral band than the central boss and lying nearer the central boss than the peripheral band, such that torque is transferred from the central boss to the peripheral band more rapidly when the angular motion of the central boss proceeds along the long axis than when it proceeds opposite the long axis.

A technique for propelling a conveyance having a pair of drive assemblies, the technique comprising: furnishing a conveyance equipped with rolling members each possessing a central boss, a peripheral band, and a compliant coupling situated between the boss and band, the compliant coupling including neighboring flexible members that jointly bound oval apertures, each oval aperture presenting a long axis inclined relative to a substantially radial orientation of the neighboring flexible members, and wherein successive curved crests of the neighboring flexible members oscillate between lying nearer the peripheral band than the central boss and lying nearer the central boss than the peripheral band, whereby torque moves from the central boss to the peripheral band more rapidly when the boss turns along the long axis than when the boss turns counter to it; driving the first drive assembly to advance in a forward sense while the second drive assembly turns unimpeded; retarding the second drive assembly to decelerate forward motion while the first drive assembly turns unimpeded; driving the second drive assembly to advance in a reverse sense while the first drive assembly turns unimpeded; and retarding the first drive assembly to decelerate reverse motion while the second drive assembly turns unimpeded.

A conveyance apparatus configured to carry a payload, comprising: a chassis framework having at least two longitudinal members separated by a gap large enough to accept at least one deck panel positioned between them; and a set of rolling units, each rolling unit including a central boss, a peripheral band, and a compliant junction linking the boss to the band, the compliant junction incorporating neighboring flexible members that together bound a lens-shaped opening whose longest dimension is inclined relative to an approximately radial orientation of the neighboring flexible members, wherein the crest of each curved section of the neighboring flexible members alternately sits nearer to the peripheral band than to the central boss and nearer to the central boss than to the peripheral band.

A cycle comprising: a hub-and-spoke wheel carried by a chassis of the cycle, the wheel including a circumferential rim adapted to retain a tyre, wherein the rim possesses: a central band delimiting a seat for a tyre bead; a first lip and a second lip projecting generally outward from the central band to hold the tyre, the first lip exhibiting a first lip breadth and a first lip elevation measured from the seat, the second lip exhibiting a second lip breadth, and the first lip and second lip being separated by an interval, a ratio of the first lip breadth to the interval being no less than 0.14.

A cycle wheel assembly comprising: a circumferential hoop configured to bear a tyre, wherein the hoop includes: a central portion delimiting a bead receiving surface; and a first lip and a second lip, the first lip and the second lip projecting generally radially outward from the central portion to hold the tyre, wherein the first lip has a first lip breadth and a first lip elevation measured from the bead receiving surface, wherein the second lip has a second lip breadth and a second lip elevation measured from the bead receiving surface, and wherein the first lip and the second lip are separated from one another by a lip separation, and wherein at least one of a quotient of the first lip breadth divided by the lip separation being at least 0.14 or a quotient of the first lip breadth divided by the first lip elevation being at least 0.75.

A cycle comprising: a hub-carrying wheel bearing a chassis of the cycle, the wheel including a circumferential ring adapted to hold a tyre, wherein the ring has: a central structure containing one or more interior voids that establish one or more radially protruding void extensions; and a first rim lip and a second rim lip, the first rim lip and the second rim lip projecting generally outward from the central structure to retain the tyre, wherein the first rim lip establishes a radially outward first lip extension and the second rim lip establishes a second radially outward lip extension, and wherein none of the one or more radially protruding void extensions intersects either the first radially outward lip extension or the second radially outward lip extension.

A hub-and-joint assembly for a powertrain of an automobile, comprising: a bearing carrier having a first serrated gear profile; a homokinetic coupling of a driveshaft having a second serrated gear profile; a radially loadable biasing member seated within a pocket such that, when unloaded, it projects at least in part outward from the pocket along a radial axis (R); and a tapered outer surface that, in a partly installed condition of the assembly, faces the radially loadable biasing member across the radial axis (R), wherein during installation the biasing member and the tapered outer surface cooperate to produce an axial thrust pressing the bearing carrier and the homokinetic coupling toward one another; and

query_text: A hub-and-joint assembly for an automobile, including: a rotatable bearing carrier having a first gear profile; a driveshaft coupling having a second gear profile; a spring-loaded radial member seated within a pocket and projecting outward from the pocket when relaxed; and a tapered outer surface positioned across from the spring-loaded radial member when the assembly is partly put together, wherein, while the assembly is being put together, the spring-loaded radial member exerts an axial load on the tapered outer surface so as to press the rotatable bearing carrier against the driveshaft coupling.

A fastening arrangement comprising: a hub for a splineless centre-locking wheel, a retaining nut screwed onto the hub, a securing member coupled with both the hub and the retaining nut so as to inhibit relative turning between them, a withdrawal device having; a leading end bearing an outer screw portion, engaged with a matching bore of the securing member; a trailing end furnished with a grip feature for applying twisting force to the withdrawal device; and a seating face positioned outboard of the outer screw portion and spaced axially away from it, abutting the retaining nut.

A removal device for a retaining member of a centre-lock hub assembly, comprising: a leading extremity bearing an outwardly directed screw portion, configured to mate with a matching inner screw of the retaining member; a trailing extremity furnished with a coupling feature for transmitting turning force to the device; and a seating face for abutting a lug nut, the seating face being situated outboard of the outwardly directed screw portion and offset along the axis from the outwardly directed screw portion.

A process for detaching a road wheel from a hub arrangement of the centre-lock type, the arrangement including a retaining nut screwed onto the hub and a securing member coupled to both the hub and the retaining nut so as to inhibit relative turning between them, the process comprising: supplying a withdrawal implement capable of being screwed into the securing member; supplying a separator implement having a seating surface for abutting the retaining nut and a seating surface for abutting the withdrawal implement so as to keep a least axial spacing between them; screwing the withdrawal implement into the securing member while the separator implement is situated between the retaining nut and the withdrawal implement; and turning the withdrawal implement so as to continue the screw engagement with the securing member and thereby produce relative axial displacement of the securing member and the withdrawal implement, and wherein the separator implement is retained in position during said turning.

A rotation-restricting apparatus, comprising: a fixed frame; a driver element turnable with respect to the fixed frame about a driver axis, the driver element carrying a actuating formation displaced from the driver axis; an indexing element bearing at least one engaged formation, the indexing element being configured to be stepwise shifted relative to the fixed frame among a set of separate placements by uninterrupted turning of the driver element and through interaction between the actuating formation and the at least one engaged formation, the indexing element, when located in a first terminal separate placement, serving to restrict turning of the driver element at a first extreme of a turning span of the driver element, and, when located in a second terminal separate placement, serving to restrict turning of the driver element at a second extreme of the turning span; and a retaining assembly configured to keep the indexing element in each separate placement, the retaining assembly being disposed at least in part within the fixed frame.

A robotic apparatus including a motion-restricting assembly, comprising: a fixed frame; a rotor element turnable with respect to the fixed frame about a rotational centerline, the rotor element bearing a actuating protrusion displaced from the rotational centerline; a blocking element possessing at least one engaged protrusion, wherein the blocking element is configured to be advanced in steps relative to the fixed frame among a series of separate stations by uninterrupted turning of the rotor element and by interaction between the actuating protrusion and the at least one engaged protrusion, wherein the blocking element in a first terminal station is configured to restrict turning of the rotor element at a first extreme of a permitted angular travel of the rotor element, and in a second terminal station is configured to restrict turning of the rotor element at a second extreme of the permitted angular travel; and a retention mechanism configured to maintain the blocking element at each station, the retention mechanism being at least partially incorporated within the fixed frame.

A process for fabricating an airless wheel, the process comprising: furnishing a wheel framework having a base hoop of smaller girth, a crown hoop of larger girth positioned concentrically relative to the base hoop, and a web member bridging the base hoop and the crown hoop; furnishing a pair of flanges, each flange possessing an outer dimension and an aperture at its center establishing an inner dimension; affixing one flange to a first face of the wheel framework; affixing the other flange to a second face of the wheel framework; situating a rubber band of tread material around an exterior of the crown hoop; fastening a first margin of a heat-retaining sleeve to the first face of the wheel framework at a site beneath the web member and fastening a second margin of the sleeve to the second face of the wheel framework at a site beneath the web member; and supplying thermal energy inside the heat-retaining sleeve.

An assembly apparatus for joining a ring-shaped tread band to a spokeless wheel body having a top annular member, a bottom annular member, and load-bearing members spanning between them, the apparatus comprising: an enclosure sized to hold the wheel body together with the tread band; a first plate adapted to attach to a first face of the wheel body; a second plate adapted to attach to a second face of the wheel body; a first clamp operable to couple a first edge of the enclosure to the wheel body; and a second clamp operable to couple a second edge of the enclosure to the wheel body.

A process for fabricating a airless wheel tyre, the process comprising: furnishing an airless tyre framework; supplying a initial plate and a subsequent plate; fastening the initial plate to a first face of the airless tyre framework; affixing the subsequent plate to a second face of the airless tyre framework; disposing an elastomeric wearing layer around a crown of the airless tyre framework; enclosing a curing sheath around the elastomeric wearing layer, including attaching a leading margin of the curing sheath to the first face of the airless tyre framework and attaching a trailing margin of the curing sheath to the second face of the airless tyre framework; and introducing thermal energy inside the curing sheath.

A airless wheel element possessing a rotation axis and a mid-plane, the airless wheel element comprising: a zigzag flexible band wrapped without interruption around the rotation axis, such that the zigzag flexible band traces a meandering route spanning from a lesser radius to a greater radius, and such that the zigzag flexible band exhibits: a series of lower arcs running generally circumferentially along the lesser radius, a series of upper arcs running generally circumferentially along the greater radius, and a series of connecting segments extending radially between the lesser radius and the greater radius; an encircling rim coupled to the series of upper arcs of the zigzag flexible band; and a central boss coupled to a set of anchoring elements, the central boss possessing a rim-like projection, wherein each of the anchoring elements comprises a clamping strip and a set of fasteners securing the clamping strip to the rim-like projection of the central boss, wherein each of the series of lower arcs engages the clamping strip of a respective anchoring element, wherein the clamping strip and the set of fasteners are arranged such that tightening the set of fasteners imposes radial tension upon the zigzag flexible band.}
