query_text: A non-air-filled wheel structure comprising: a peripheral ring; a series of flexible spokes projecting radially inward from the peripheral ring; and a central mounting body possessing a set of arms, each arm joined to one of the series of flexible spokes.

A non-pneumatic wheel structure comprising: an exterior annular ring; a series of spokes projecting inwardly from the exterior ring; a central mount coupled to a set of fastening elements, the central mount possessing a collar section, wherein each of the set of fastening elements includes a clamping rod and a group of threaded fasteners joining the clamping rod to the collar section of the central mount, wherein each of the series of spokes seats against the clamping rod of a respective fastening element, wherein the clamping rod and the group of threaded fasteners are configured such that drawing the group of threaded fasteners tight imparts radially directed tension to the series of spokes.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread carrying a multiplicity of lugs; wherein, when viewed in a meridional section taken across the axial and radial directions, at least a section encompassing the axially outer edge of a ground-engaging face of each lug curves radially inwardly as it proceeds axially outwardly; and a vertical offset measured from a crest location situated at the greatest radial extent of the lug to the axially outer edge of at least one of the lugs changes in accordance with a breadth of that lug.

A system comprising: a perforated member having a panel that delimits a hole extending from a front face of the panel to a rear face of the panel, wherein: the hole has an exterior border lying on a first circular path of a first diameter and an interior border lying on a second circular path of a second diameter smaller than the first diameter, the interior border establishes a series of inward-facing curved segments that are coaxial with the first circular path and the second circular path, and the exterior border establishes a series of outward-facing curved segments that are coaxial with the first circular path and the second circular path.

A perforated element comprising: a panel having an opening extending through from a front face of the panel to a rear face of the panel, wherein: the opening includes an exterior boundary lying on a first circular path of a first diameter and an interior boundary lying on a second circular path of a second diameter smaller than the first diameter, the interior boundary establishes a series of inner contour faces forming extended arcs that are coaxial with the first circular path and the second circular path, and the exterior boundary establishes a series of outer contour faces forming extended arcs that are coaxial with the first circular path and the second circular path.

A plug member comprising: a prismatic segment exhibiting a constant cross-section over its extent; wherein the section has an exterior boundary including a perimeter contour lying on a first circle of greater diameter and an interior boundary lying on a second circle of smaller diameter; the interior boundary establishes a series of inward curved faces that are coaxial with the first circle and the second circle; and the exterior boundary establishes a series of outward curved faces that are coaxial with the first circle and the second circle.

A cycling wheel rim assembly, comprising: an outer ring section defining a peripheral face and an uppermost extremity, the outer ring section configured to receive a cycle tyre; a leading profile; and a pair of flanks, each flank projecting outwardly from the leading profile to a respective junction joining the peripheral face, such that the flanks define a body having a greatest breadth at a broadest region, a secondary breadth along a midline of the body, and a body thickness, each flank together with its respective junction creating an uninterrupted external contour extending from the uppermost extremity to the leading profile, wherein the uninterrupted external contour bends medially at the respective junction and wherein the uninterrupted external contour exhibits a curvilinear profile from the broadest region to the leading profile; and wherein the broadest region is displaced laterally from the midline of the body, and wherein the outer ring section is configured to accommodate a cycle tyre narrower than the greatest breadth of the body and narrower than the body thickness so as to establish an unbalanced cross-sectional configuration having a central axis offset from the broadest region of the body.

A cycling wheel rim, the cycling wheel rim including: a leading edge portion; and a pair of lateral walls, each lateral wall projecting radially away from the leading edge portion to define a rim structure having a crown distal from the leading edge portion, the rim structure exhibiting a greatest lateral extent at a broadest zone that lies radially inward of the crown and radially outward of a midline of the rim structure, each lateral wall merging into the crown at a respective rounded junction that bends inwardly in the lateral direction, wherein the rim structure widens from the crown to the broadest zone and narrows from the broadest zone to the leading edge portion; and wherein, the cycling wheel rim is configured to receive a tire narrower than the greatest lateral extent so as to produce an unsymmetrical cross-sectional profile in which the broadest zone is offset from a midline of the unsymmetrical cross-sectional profile and a tangent line contacts both the tire and one of the lateral walls, the tangent line forming a tangent angle below 17 degrees.

A cycling wheel hoop, the hoop including: a leading edge portion; and a pair of flanks, each flank projecting outwardly from the leading edge portion to define a hollow body having a crown situated farthest from the leading edge portion, the hollow body presenting a greatest breadth at a broadest zone that lies inboard of the crown and outboard of a midplane of the hollow body, wherein the hollow body widens from the crown toward the broadest zone and narrows from the broadest zone toward the leading edge portion, each flank merging into the crown through a rounded shoulder that bends inwardly in the lateral direction; and wherein the hoop is configured to receive a tyre that is thinner than the greatest breadth and thinner than the hollow body is deep, thereby establishing an uneven cross-sectional profile in which the broadest zone is displaced from a central plane of the uneven cross-sectional profile.

A freewheel actuation kit adaptable to pre-existing pawl-and-ratchet-ring rear hub couplings that release a set of spring-loaded latches, the kit comprising: a rotary guide disk serving as a terminal covering that seats over a flat front face of an existing tubular latch-holder body, the latch-holder carrying the set of latches arranged radially adjacent that front face, the guide disk including overlapping covering tabs formed as a set of apertures that span the front face along its extent and that engage the latches in a cam-and-follower arrangement upon relative rotation of the guide disk about a shared central axis defined along the length of the latch-holder, such that boundary edges of the apertures press the latches inward toward the shared central axis during rotation in one sense and relieve that pressure during rotation in the opposite sense; wherein each aperture corresponds to exactly one latch of the latch-holder, and a set of longitudinal boundary edges of the apertures interfere with the latches to halt relative rotation between the guide disk and the latch-holder at the end of latch travel in either rotational sense along the shared central axis; wherein the guide disk defines a central bore along the shared central axis and at least one retention notch formed at a rim of the central bore, the at least one retention notch having a length and a notch centerline running along that length parallel to the shared central axis; a tubular spacer sleeve having a length and a sleeve centerline running along that length, the sleeve centerline coinciding with the shared central axis, the tubular spacer sleeve comprising a raised collar at one end and being rotationally locked about its centerline while partially received within a socket formed at the front face of the latch-holder; at least one helical spring wound about the tubular spacer sleeve, the at least one helical spring exhibiting a grip against rotation on the tubular spacer sleeve that increases when wound tighter in one direction and decreases when unwound in the other direction, the at least one helical spring being free to rotate relative to the tubular spacer sleeve once the grip is exceeded in either direction; wherein the at least one helical spring includes a projecting tang at one of its ends having a length and a tang centerline running along that length parallel to the shared central axis, the projecting tang extending into the at least one retention notch such that the at least one helical spring is rotationally fixed to the guide disk and cannot turn relative to the guide disk; and wherein the guide disk, the latch-holder, the tubular spacer sleeve, and the at least one helical spring are axially and rotationally secured together as a unit.

A procedure for withdrawing and freeing a set of detents in a detent-and-toothed-collar clutch assembly of a bicycle hub, the procedure comprising: mounting a rotary actuator disc to the flat face of an existing tubular detent holder, the actuator disc having overhanging lips defining apertures that engage the detents so that relative turning of the actuator disc acts as a cam against each detent, driving the detents inward into the holder in a first rotational sense and permitting their outward travel in a second rotational sense; limiting the actuator disc to a predetermined angular travel relative to the detent holder, after which contact between the lips and the detents blocks further relative turning; coupling the actuator disc, through projecting ends of at least one wound spring coiled about a stationary tubular sleeve having a raised collar, to the sleeve, the spring resting against the collar and exerting a frictional resistance to turning in either direction; turning the detent holder in either direction relative to the sleeve so that the holder turns relative to the actuator disc until the lips arrest the detents at the end of the predetermined travel, whereupon the actuator disc overcomes the frictional resistance of the spring and the actuator disc, spring and holder turn together relative to the sleeve; and withdrawing or releasing the detents of the holder in dependence on the relative rotation between the actuator disc and the detent holder.

A lockable caster assembly for luggage, comprising: a frame swivelable into a travel heading (T) by way of a rotary joint, and two rollers journaled on the frame about a level axle; wherein the rotary joint is situated ahead of the axle when viewed opposite to the travel heading (T); and a stopping mechanism configurable between an arrested state, in which the stopping mechanism applies a retarding action to at least one roller, and a freely turning state, in which the stopping mechanism frees the rollers; wherein a foot lever producing the retarding action is pivotally carried on the frame by a lever pin that runs parallel to the axle and lies between the rollers, and, in both the freely turning state and the arrested state, is retained on the frame by detent elements in positive and frictional engagement; and, in the arrested state, at least one friction pad disposed on the foot lever presses in a direction parallel to the axle directly against one lateral face of at least one roller.

A lubricant circulation arrangement for a powertrain, comprising: a primary sump situated in a bottom region of a gearbox, the primary sump defining a set fluid height; a secondary sump situated in a bottom region of the gearbox, the secondary sump divided from the primary sump by a partition defining a passage; an intake conduit defining an orifice disposed in a bottom region of the primary sump beneath the set fluid height; and a supplementary intake conduit defining an orifice disposed in a bottom region of the secondary sump.

A drivetrain lubricant circulation arrangement, comprising: a gearbox housing having a first sump chamber and a second sump chamber situated along a bottom region of the housing, the second sump chamber being partitioned from the first sump chamber by a wall defining a passage, the first sump chamber maintaining a predetermined liquid height; a primary intake conduit terminating in an inlet disposed within a base area of the first sump chamber beneath the predetermined liquid height; and a secondary intake conduit terminating in an inlet disposed within a base area of the second sump chamber.

A tyre intended for road vehicle rims, the tyre incorporating at least one load-bearing portion that includes at least one reinforcing cord formed as a filament body encased by, or set within, a cured rubbery material produced by curing a rubber mixture comprising, relative to 100 parts per hundred of diene rubber polymer: (i) a premixed blend of a diene rubber polymer and lignin, supplying the mixture with between 100 and 10 parts per hundred of diene rubber polymer and a quantity of lignin of at least 25 parts per hundred; (ii) between 0 and 90 parts per hundred of an additional diene rubber polymer; (iii) no less than 30 parts per hundred of a carbon black strengthening filler; (iv) optionally, a reinforcing resin containing at least 1 part per hundred of a methylene-accepting compound combined with at least 1 part per hundred of a methylene-donating compound; and (v) from 0.1 to 12 parts per hundred of at least one curing agent, wherein at least 50 parts per hundred of said diene rubber polymer is constituted by natural or synthetic isoprene rubber.

A reinforced structural member for a tyre of a road wheel, the member including at least one strengthening element made of an elongated body that is either covered by or set within a cured rubber mixture produced by curing a rubber-forming composition containing, relative to 100 phr of diene elastomer: (i) a masterbatch of a diene elastomer together with lignin, supplied so that the composition contains 100 to 10 phr of diene elastomer and lignin in an amount of at least 25 phr; (ii) 0 to 90 phr of an additional diene elastomer; (iii) at least 30 phr of a carbon black reinforcing filler; (iv) optionally, a reinforcing resin including at least 1 phr of a methylene acceptor compound combined with at least 1 phr of a methylene donor compound; and (v) 0.1 to 12 phr of at least one curing agent, wherein at least 50 phr of the diene elastomer consists of natural or synthetic polyisoprene rubber.

A reinforcement member comprising a filamentary body encased within, or bonded into, a cured rubbery material produced by curing a rubber mixture containing, per 100 phr of diene-based polymer: (i) a pre-blend of a diene-based polymer and lignin, such that the mixture contains 100 to 10 phr of diene-based polymer and lignin in an amount of at least 25 phr; (ii) 0 to 90 phr of an additional diene-based polymer; (iii) at least 30 phr of a carbon black reinforcing filler; (iv) optionally, a reinforcing resin including at least 1 phr of a methylene acceptor compound combined with at least 1 phr of a methylene donor compound; and (v) 0.1 to 12 phr of at least one curing agent, wherein at least 50 phr of said diene-based polymer is constituted by natural or synthetic polyisoprene rubber.

A rubber mixture suitable for vulcanization, the mixture including, relative to 100 parts per hundred rubber of diene-based elastomer: (i) a masterbatch formed by pre-blending a diene-based elastomer with lignin, such that the mixture contains 100 to 10 phr of diene-based elastomer and lignin in an amount of at least 25 phr; (ii) 0 to 90 phr of an additional diene-based elastomer; (iii) at least 30 phr of a carbon black reinforcer; (iv) optionally, a reinforcing resin containing at least 1 phr of a methylene-accepting compound combined with at least 1 phr of a methylene-donating compound; and (v) 0.1 to 12 phr of at least one curing agent, wherein no less than 50 phr of the diene-based elastomer is constituted by natural or synthetic polyisoprene rubber.

A rubber mixture suitable for vulcanisation, the mixture comprising, relative to 100 parts by weight per hundred rubber of diene rubber: (i) a masterbatch of a diene rubber together with lignin, present in a proportion yielding a total of 100 phr to 10 phr of diene rubber and an amount of lignin of at least 20 phr; (ii) from 0 phr to 90 phr of an additional diene rubber; (iii) no less than 30 phr of a carbon black reinforcing agent; (iv) optionally, a strengthening resin including at least 0.5 phr of a methylene-accepting compound combined with at least 0.2 phr of a methylene-releasing compound; (v) between 0.1 phr and 10 phr of carbon nanotubes; and (vi) between 0.1 phr and 12 phr of at least one curing agent; wherein at least 50 phr of the diene rubber consists of natural or synthetic polyisoprene.

A airless wheel covering, comprising a outer contact band and an inner mounting rim that are coaxial, and a main structure joined as one piece between the outer contact band and the inner mounting rim; the main structure defines a plurality of primary hollow rings lined up side by side in a lateral direction of the covering and spread circumferentially in a zone lying between the outer contact band and the inner mounting rim; a secondary hollow ring is situated between each pair of neighboring primary hollow rings; lateral inner surfaces of the primary hollow rings each project outward to form plural groups of protrusions, a set-back section lies between adjacent groups of protrusions on the same lateral side, a first inner lip is created where the set-back section meets the inner surface of the primary hollow ring, and inner surfaces of the protrusions flanking each primary hollow ring form an arched widened area positioned at the periphery of the first inner lip; and a second inner lip is formed in the secondary hollow ring where it corresponds to the arched widened area, a flared area positioned at the periphery of the second inner lip is formed in the secondary hollow ring where it corresponds to the set-back section, and a top of the flared area has a spherical void adjacent the outer contact band.

A non-pneumatic tire assembly, comprising a central mounting unit, an exterior ground-contacting ring, and a series of struts linking the central mounting unit to the ground-contacting ring, wherein every strut of the series includes: an inner bearing member projecting outward from the central mounting unit and an outer bearing member projecting inward from the ground-contacting ring, the two bearing members being arranged to define an included angle greater than zero degrees but less than one hundred eighty degrees between a first face of the inner bearing member and a first face of the outer bearing member, the inner and outer bearing members being coated with a first vulcanizable elastomer blend; a first elastomeric coupling mass formed from a second vulcanizable elastomer blend, situated within the included angle, and bridging the free terminal ends of the inner and outer bearing members, those free terminal ends being the ends remote from the central mounting unit and the ground-contacting ring respectively; a second elastomeric coupling mass comprising a third vulcanizable elastomer blend and joining a second face of the inner bearing member, at its root end, to the central mounting unit; a third elastomeric coupling mass comprising a fourth vulcanizable elastomer blend and joining a second face of the outer bearing member, at its root end, to the ring; and wherein the first, second, third, and fourth vulcanizable elastomer blends are cross-linkable compounds each comprising, per one hundred parts by weight of rubber: from 50 to 100 parts of natural rubber; from 0 to 50 parts of a secondary rubber constituent chosen from polybutadiene rubber, a polybutadiene-styrene copolymer containing no more than 5 mol % styrene, and mixtures thereof; from 15 to 40 parts of a reinforcing filler including from 2 to 6 parts of a carbon black and from 20 to 40 parts of a silica having a surface area of 19 to 55 m2/g; and one or more curing systems for the first, second, third, and fourth blends, which curing systems may be identical or distinct; at least one of the second and third elastomeric coupling masses further includes a root shoulder at its root end, the shoulder being formed from a fifth vulcanizable elastomer blend, the shoulder occupying no more than 25% of the total volume of that coupling mass, and the fifth blend being a cross-linkable compound which may differ between shoulders and comprising, per one hundred parts by weight of rubber: from 90 to 100 parts of natural rubber; up to 10 parts of a tertiary rubber constituent chosen from polybutadiene rubber, a polybutadiene-styrene copolymer containing no more than 5 mol % styrene, and mixtures thereof; from 61 to 80 parts of a second carbon black; and a curing system for the fifth blend.

A process for fabricating a non-pneumatic wheel support, the process comprising: supplying a coiled steel strip having a carbon fraction from 0.20% to 0.60% and a gauge from 1.5 mm to 7 mm; paying out the coiled strip; differentially rolling the strip so that its gauge alternates cyclically along its longitudinal extent between a floor value of at least 1.2 mm and a ceiling value of no more than 4.5 mm; severing the strip into segments incorporating at least one heavier zone and at least one lighter zone, each segment having a length equal to the strip's transverse dimension; turning each segment by a right angle; roll shaping each segment to impart a bend across its transverse dimension, with the heavier and lighter zones running side by side along the segment length; soaking each shaped segment at a temperature from 950° C. to 1400° C. for 2 to 10 seconds; quenching each segment to below 200° C. within 10 seconds; dividing each segment into a plurality of spokes each measuring 80 mm to 400 mm in width; furnishing a inner annular member and an outer annular member; and positioning the plurality of spokes between the inner annular member and the outer annular member.

A resilient wheel support structure comprising: an inner annular member possessing a smaller span; an outer annular member possessing a larger span than the inner annular member, the outer annular member being positioned concentrically about the inner annular member; and a set of arched, metallic struts bridging the inner annular member and the outer annular member, wherein each of the arched, metallic struts exhibits an offset yield stress of at least 1300 MPa, an ultimate tensile stress of at least 1400 MPa, and a Rockwell C hardness of at least 50.

A process for fabricating a support member for a airless wheel, the process comprising: obtaining a coiled strip of steel containing from 0.28% to 0.50% carbon; uncoiling the strip; shaping the strip by roll forming to impart a bend across its breadth; raising the temperature of the strip to a value from 950° C. to 1400° C. over a span of 2 to 10 seconds; quenching the strip to below 200° C. within 10 seconds; and severing from the strip a support member having a breadth from 80 mm to 400 mm.

A railcar wheel, comprising: a hub defining an innermost annular region and configured to receive an axle of a rail carriage; a circumferential shell including a running surface for engaging an upper face of a track rail, and a guiding lip joined to an edge of the running surface and extending radially beyond it; and an annular disc linking the hub to the shell, wherein a midpoint of the shell along its axial extent is displaced toward the lip relative to a midpoint of the hub along its axial extent, a mid-thickness line of the disc is straight in a meridional section through the rotational axis and tilts relative to the radial direction so as to lie progressively farther from the lip moving radially outward, and where a spacing measured axially from the shell face more remote from the lip to a radially outermost terminus of the mid-thickness line is designated Pw, and an axial width of the shell is designated Wr, the ratio Pw/Wr being below 0.40.

A castor adapted to be mounted to a carrying frame, the castor comprising: a roller assembly, including: a balance beam having two opposing terminals and an intermediate portion positioned between the terminals; a principal roller journaled to the intermediate portion of the balance beam; a secondary roller journaled to one of the terminals of the balance beam; and a further secondary roller journaled to the other of the terminals of the balance beam; a yoke including: a leg having a bottom extremity joined to the balance beam; and a top bearing connected to the leg; and a mounting plate pivotally connected to the top bearing of the yoke and arranged for securing to the carrying frame.

A drive unit for a vehicle, the drive unit comprising: a motor assembly having a stator-supported armature configured to spin about a first longitudinal rotation line; a hub-carrying road-engaging arrangement configured to pivot about a second rotation line positioned higher than the first rotation line, wherein the road-engaging arrangement includes a flange structure configured to receive a tire rim; and a speed-reduction train having a group of cogwheels that conveys rotational force between the motor assembly and the road-engaging arrangement.

A drive unit for a vehicle, comprising: an electric machine having a stator-driven armature and an armature spindle that turn about a primary longitudinal axis; a hub assembly that revolves about a secondary axis situated higher than the primary axis, the hub assembly including a flange configured to receive a road wheel; a gearing arrangement that includes: an input pinion that turns with the armature about the primary axis; an intermediate spur that engages the input pinion and turns about a tertiary axis; a first output pinion that engages the intermediate spur and turns about the secondary axis; a second output pinion that turns with the intermediate spur about the tertiary axis; and a second output gear that engages the second output pinion and turns about the secondary axis; and a engagement device that selectively links either the first output pinion or the second output gear to a hub spindle that revolves about the secondary axis and is coupled to the hub assembly.

A drive unit for a vehicle comprising: an electrical machine having a stator-driven armature and an armature shaft that turn about a primary rotational centerline; a hub assembly configured to turn about a secondary rotational centerline positioned higher than the primary rotational centerline, the hub assembly including a flange that accepts attachment of a road wheel; a speed-reduction train including: a input pinion turning together with the armature about the primary rotational centerline; a first intermediate gear that engages the input pinion, turns about a tertiary rotational centerline, and may be coupled to a first transfer spindle; a second intermediate gear that engages the input pinion, turns about a quaternary rotational centerline, and may be coupled to a second transfer spindle; a third intermediate gear that turns about the tertiary rotational centerline and may be coupled to the first transfer spindle; and a fourth intermediate gear that turns about the quaternary rotational centerline and may be coupled to the second transfer spindle; and an output gear that meshes with the third intermediate gear and the fourth intermediate gear, turns about the secondary rotational centerline, and is drivingly linked to the hub assembly; a first engagement member that selectively joins either the first intermediate gear or the third intermediate gear to the first transfer spindle; and a second engagement member that selectively joins either the second intermediate gear or the fourth intermediate gear to the second transfer spindle.

A process for manufacturing a renewed tire, comprising applying a new tread layer onto a foundation tire having a lateral wall portion that incorporates, relative to one hundred parts by mass of an elastomeric component, at least twenty parts by mass of an elastomer possessing conjugated diene-derived repeating units and ethylene-derived repeating units.

An airless wheel construction comprising: an elastomeric member including at least one fabric reinforcement strand, the strand being formed from filaments, a substantial portion of which are bonded to one another within the strand; and wherein the filaments are selected from aramid, polyamide, polyester, polyethylene terephthalate, polyethylene naphthalate, glass fibre and carbon fibre filaments.

An airless wheel-tyre assembly comprising: an outer ring-shaped ground-engaging section; a ring-shaped load-bearing band situated beneath and holding up the ground-engaging section, the load-bearing band including a plurality of concentric plies, at least one of which is a elastomeric matrix strengthened by fabric filaments made of bundled strands that are partly melded into unitary cords, the strands being selected from one or more of aramid, polyamide, polyester, polyethylene terephthalate, polyethylene naphthalate, glass fibre and carbon fibre.

A tire lacking pressurized air, comprising: a ring-shaped tread section; a ring-shaped load-bearing band beneath and holding up the tread section, the band having a plurality of stacked ring-shaped strata, at least one of which includes an elastomeric matrix strengthened by fabric cords formed from filaments partly bonded into unitary cords, the filaments being selected from polyester, polyethylene terephthalate, and polyethylene naphthalate, the cords further containing a diisocyanate, and most of the filaments being joined together through the diisocyanate.

A pneumatic tyre having a crown portion with an outer contact face, the crown portion being formed as a two-ply structure consisting of an upper stratum containing a initial rubber blend exhibiting a first loss compliance value LC and a lower stratum containing a subsequent rubber blend exhibiting a second loss compliance value LC, wherein both LC and LC are measured with a dynamic mechanical spectrometer at 10 Hz, under a 10% static pre-deformation and a 2.5% oscillating deformation while temperature is swept between 0 and 130° C.; wherein, at a crown temperature falling between 5 and 50° C., LC exceeds LC; and wherein the proportional volume of the subsequent rubber blend to the initial rubber blend within the crown portion lies between 0.5:1 and 10:1.

A pneumatic tyre having a tread provided with a road-contacting face, the tread being a two-stratum structure composed of an outer stratum containing a first rubber mixture exhibiting a first storage-independent dissipative modulus E″ and an inner stratum containing a second rubber mixture exhibiting a second dissipative modulus E″, each of E″ and E″ being measured by a dynamic mechanical spectrometer operated at 10 Hz, with a 10% static pre-deformation and a 2.5% oscillatory deformation, while the temperature is swept from 0 to 130° C.; wherein, at a tread temperature between 0 and 20° C., E″ is greater than E″; and wherein a volumetric proportion of the second rubber mixture to the first rubber mixture within the tread lies between 0.5:1 and 10:1.

A pneumatic tyre comprising: a tread face bearing at least three rib-like channels running along the circumference of the tyre; the channels being dimensioned in width so that, while the tyre bears a load on the road, opposing sidewalls do not come into abutment; wherein at least one of a pair of outboard channels situated at the two lateral extremities of the tread is shaped such that a flank of the channel on the shoulder side forms an included angle exceeding 90 degrees with the tread face; and wherein at least one of the remaining channels, other than said pair of outboard channels, has a location of greatest width along its depth that lies nearer the channel floor than the plane of the tread face.

A computer-executed process for estimating the rate at which a tread depletes on a motor vehicle's tyre, the process comprising: retrieving specification data for at least one tyre fitted to a motor vehicle; retrieving specification data for the motor vehicle; receiving operational telemetry data from the motor vehicle; and estimating a tread depletion rate using, at least in part, the retrieved tyre specification data, the retrieved vehicle specification data, and the received telemetry data, in accordance with a data-derived mathematical model of tyre wear.

A computer-executed process for determining a rate at which a vehicle's tires degrade, the process comprising: sending tire specification data for at least one tire mounted on a vehicle; conveying vehicle specification data; communicating vehicle telemetry readings; and receiving a computed degradation rate derived at least partly from the sent tire specification data, the sent vehicle specification data, and the communicated telemetry readings, wherein the computed degradation rate is produced by a data-driven mathematical model of tire wear.

A computer-based arrangement for tracking the degradation speed of a vehicle's tread, the arrangement including one or more processors arranged to: acquire specification details of at least one wheel covering mounted on a conveyance; acquire specification details of the conveyance; acquire operational data transmitted from the conveyance; and determine a degradation speed of the wheel covering using, at least in part, the acquired wheel covering specification details, the acquired conveyance specification details and the acquired conveyance operational data, in accordance with a data-derived mathematical degradation model.

A tire without inflation gas, the tire including: a ring-shaped running surface member; a first flank member and a second flank member, the first flank member incorporating a first textile reinforcement layer and the second flank member incorporating a second textile reinforcement layer; wherein the first reinforcement layer occupies solely a first axial side of the tire and the second reinforcement layer occupies solely a second axial side of the tire, the second axial side lying opposite the first axial side; wherein each of the first and second reinforcement layers possesses a peripheral terminal section fastened to the running surface member, a peripheral seating section located radially inward, and a peripheral connecting section spanning from the terminal section to the corresponding seating section crosswise relative to a radially inward face of the running surface member; wherein the terminal section of the first reinforcement layer is secured to the running surface member parallel thereto and extends toward a first substantially outboard axial direction, and wherein the terminal section of the second reinforcement layer is secured to the running surface member parallel thereto and extends toward a second substantially outboard axial direction oriented opposite the first outboard axial direction.

A airless wheel covering, comprising: a ring-shaped ground-contacting strip; a first plies-of-fabric layer confined to a first axial face of the covering; a second plies-of-fabric layer confined to a second axial face of the covering; wherein each layer possesses a pair of radially innermost seating segments, a radially outermost crown segment secured to the strip, and a pair of intermediate spans each running crosswise to the strip from the crown segment down to a respective seating segment.

A raising apparatus adapted to be coupled with a tyre mounting device possessing a revolvable wheel support and a lever, the lever carrying a tool at a free extremity, the raising apparatus comprising: a pair of independently telescopic drivers positionable beneath the revolvable wheel support of the tyre mounting device; a governing unit linked in signal communication with the drivers; wherein, when the raising apparatus is coupled to the tyre mounting device having a rim secured to the revolvable wheel support and a tyre fitted around the rim, the governing unit is arranged to: extend a first of the drivers so that at least a segment of the tyre is elevated relative to the rim and the tool of the tyre mounting device is able to selectively contact at least a segment of the tyre.

A process for repositioning a tire with respect to a rim, the rim being secured to a revolving rim support of a tire mounting apparatus, the apparatus having a boom carrying a tool at its free end, the process comprising: furnishing a raising assembly couplable to the mounting apparatus, the raising assembly incorporating first and second telescoping drivers and a control unit signally connected to the first and second drivers, the first and second drivers positioned beneath the revolving rim support; telescopically advancing the first driver so that a segment of the tire is elevated away from the rim and the tool of the mounting apparatus is able to selectively contact a segment of the tire.

A cycle wheel hub-to-rim linkage assembly comprising: a rotatable axle carried by a central spindle, the axle adapted to mount a wheel for turning movement; a set of radially projecting collars extending outward from the spindle, each collar defining a ring of circumferentially spaced openings; a set of wire-like tension members each having a terminal end, a distal end and an intermediate length extending between them, the terminal end of each member seated in one of the spaced openings, the distal end of each member joined to a peripheral hoop configured to carry a tread-bearing covering; wherein the terminal end of each member couples to one of the spaced openings of the collars so as to establish three zones of engagement between the terminal end and the associated collar, the three zones provided to reinforce a bent transition region of the member and mitigate member breakage and lateral wobble; wherein a first zone of engagement is defined by a enlarged cap of each member resting within one of the spaced openings, a second zone of engagement is defined by an inner curved section of each member bearing against a boundary wall bounding the one of the openings and a third zone of engagement is defined by each member bearing against a perimeter edge of the collar; and wherein the number of tension members is selected from six, eight, nine, ten, twelve, fifteen, sixteen or eighteen.

A wheel guard assembly releasably mountable on an aircraft wheel, the aircraft wheel including a tire-bearing rim and a central hub defining a bore extending axially through the hub inside the rim, comprising: at least two guard shells; a first guard shell of the at least two guard shells positioned adjacent a first lateral face of said wheel; a second guard shell of the at least two guard shells positioned adjacent an opposite lateral face of the wheel relative to the first; a locating projection formed integrally with each of the at least two guard shells, the locating projection of the first guard shell bearing against a radially intermediate flange of the hub projecting inwardly from the rim and carrying at least one raceway channel on the first lateral face, and passing beyond the flange into the bore from the first lateral face; and at least one bearing raceway received within the raceway channel of the flange, wherein the locating projections contact one another over at least part of their respective extents such that the locating projections detachably join the first guard shell to the second guard shell, thereby holding the at least one bearing raceway against the flange and shielding an inner wall of the bore; and

query_text: A removable guard assembly for mounting on a wheel of an airplane, the wheel comprising a peripheral flange, a central boss projecting inwardly from the flange at its midsection and carrying at least one bearing seat recess with a bearing ring seated therein, and a central bore extending through the boss; the guard assembly comprising: at least two shell parts; a first shell part of the at least two shell parts positioned on one face of the wheel; a second shell part of the at least two shell parts positioned on an opposite face of the wheel relative to the first; at least one unitary retaining projection extending from the first shell part of the at least two shell parts, the at least one unitary retaining projection contacting the central boss on at least one face of the wheel and passing through the central bore from the one face to the opposite face, wherein the at least one unitary retaining projection extending from the first shell part holds the bearing ring within the bearing seat recess and mates with the second shell part such that the at least one unitary retaining projection detachably joins the first shell part to the opposed second shell part and thereby detachably secures the guard assembly to the wheel; and

query_text: A procedure for deploying a wheel guard on an aircraft wheel so that a projecting guard element holds at least one bearing cup within a central bearing seat of the wheel, comprising: positioning a first of at least two guard halves, the first guard half bearing at least one projecting guard element, the projecting guard element being lined up with a hub opening; inserting the projecting guard element through the hub opening of the aircraft wheel, the aircraft wheel including a rim and a hub having a bearing seat that projects radially inward from the rim at a mid-radial region of the rim and carrying at least one bearing cup channel, the projecting guard element thus being engaged with the aircraft wheel so that it reaches and mates with a second guard half of the at least two guard halves through the hub opening; mating at least one attachment feature of the projecting guard element to detachably fasten the first guard half to the second guard half; and maintaining the at least one bearing cup against the bearing seat of the wheel while the wheel guard remains detachably fastened.

A roller support unit comprising: a shaft component permitting angular displacement around an upright pivot line; a rolling element whose transverse rotation axis is displaced sideways in a first lateral sense from the upright pivot line; and a foot component including a main frame and forming a cavity positioned beneath the shaft component that accommodates a segment of the rolling element, wherein at least part of the foot component is displaced sideways from the upright pivot line in a second lateral sense opposite the first lateral sense; and wherein, while the rolling element turns, a lower face of the foot component sits raised above the lowest point of the rolling element.

A technique for guiding an autonomous ground vehicle through a non-standardized household setting, the technique comprising: determining a plurality of target stops within the household setting; establishing routes linking at least certain of the target stops; detecting one or more hazardous segments along the routes where traversal by the vehicle at a baseline velocity would present an excessive likelihood of jostling or dislodging a payload carried by the vehicle; recording geographic positions of the one or more hazardous segments; and, upon sensing that the vehicle is situated within or adjacent to a recorded position of the one or more hazardous segments, lowering the velocity of the vehicle to at least one limit value beneath the baseline velocity so as to diminish the chance of jostling or dislodging the payload.

A computer-implemented process for enabling self-directed movement of an automated carrier through a non-standardized household setting, the process comprising: determining a collection of intended stopping points within the household setting; determining route segments linking at least some of the intended stopping points; detecting one or more zones along the route segments where a person pushing the carrier would have to exert a force surpassing a predefined magnitude; recording positions of the one or more zones; and excluding the automated carrier from traversing any route segment containing the one or more zones unless a person manually overrides such exclusion.

A wheel-rolling assembly lacking inflation, comprising: a ring-shaped contact band; a load-bearing framework including an annular central mounting member and a multitude of struts disposed radially between the contact band and the central mounting member, each strut extending outward from the central mounting member to hold up the contact band; wherein at least one of the struts includes: a) an inner section formed of a first rubber-like material exhibiting a first rigidity, and b) an outer section, situated radially outward of the inner section, formed of a second rubber-like material exhibiting a second rigidity that differs from the first rigidity.

An airless wheel-tyre apparatus, comprising: a peripheral running layer; a load-bearing framework having a central annular core member, an outer annular band carrying the running layer, and a set of struts disposed between the band and the core to sustain the band on the core; wherein at least one of the struts incorporates a first rubbery material exhibiting a first rigidity; and wherein at least one of the core member and the band incorporates a further rubbery material, distinct from the first rubbery material, exhibiting a further rigidity exceeding the first rigidity by no less than five percent.

An airless wheel-support assembly comprising: a ground-engaging outer band; a load-bearing framework including a central inner collar, a peripheral annular rim carrying the outer band, and a series of struts disposed between the rim and the collar to hold the rim on the collar, wherein at least one of the struts exhibits a substantially X-like profile and includes a pair of inboard limbs and a pair of outboard limbs joined together at an intersecting junction of the at least one strut, wherein the pair of outboard limbs includes a base segment abutting the peripheral rim, and wherein the pair of inboard limbs includes a cap segment abutting the central collar, wherein at least one of the base segment and the cap segment is formed of a first elastomeric material having a first rigidity; and wherein the at least one strut includes a second elastomeric material located between the base segment and the intersecting junction, the second elastomeric material having a second rigidity that is at least 5% less than the first rigidity.

A airless wheel tyre, comprising: a central boss defining a rotational axis extending along an axial orientation; a load-bearing framework positioned radially beyond the boss; a reinforcing belt disposed radially beyond the framework, the reinforcing belt including a base body and a set of mass-lightening inserts embedded within the base body and oriented along the axial orientation, each insert bounding a cavity and formed from a substance differing in makeup from the base body, wherein at least certain of the inserts constitute at least one row in which all inserts of the row sit at an identical radial spacing from the rotational axis and abut consecutive inserts of the row; and a ground-contacting cover disposed radially beyond the reinforcing belt and adapted to contact a paved surface; wherein certain of the inserts belong to a first row forming an innermost radial row of the inserts, and certain other inserts belong to a second row forming an outermost radial row of the inserts, the second row lying at a greater radial distance from the rotational axis than the first row.

A two-wheeler pneumatic covering, comprising: a radially layered casing framework and a running surface strip disposed externally in the radial direction relative to the casing framework; wherein the casing framework includes an inner fabric layer carrying a first set of fibrous strengthening filaments and an outer fabric layer carrying a second set of fibrous strengthening filaments, the outer fabric layer being stacked radially over the inner fabric layer; wherein the filaments of the first set run in mutual parallel alignment and are angled at a predetermined tilt relative to a mid-plane (X-X) of the covering at a central region of the running surface strip, and the filaments of the second set run in mutual parallel alignment and are angled at the same predetermined tilt in the opposite sense relative to the mid-plane (X-X); wherein the filaments of both sets exhibit a specific strength between 0.35 cN/Tex and 1.2 cN/Tex at 2% extension and between 0.5 cN/Tex and 3 cN/Tex at 5% extension; and wherein at least one central circumferential band of the running surface strip straddling the mid-plane (X-X) is formed of a cured elastomer having a static modulus Ca3 at 70° C. between 9.0 and 14.0, a loss tangent at 70° C. and 10 Hz between 0.120 and 0.160, and a storage modulus E′ at 70° C. and 10 Hz between 3.7 and 4.1.

A pneumatic covering for a heavy earthmoving machine, the covering comprising: a belt assembly positioned radially inward of a tread band and radially outward of a ply structure, the belt assembly including wire filaments enveloped in elastomeric skim stock, the belt assembly being substantially mirror-symmetric about a mid-circumferential plane that is orthogonal to the rotational axis of the covering and bisects the tread band, the belt assembly including at least five belt plies carrying wire filaments enveloped in elastomeric skim stock, the radially outermost belt ply constituting a restraining ply whose wire filaments are resilient and exhibit a tensile modulus of no more than 110 GPa, the belt assembly including at least one working ply whose filaments are inclined at an angle of at least 15 degrees relative to the mid-circumferential plane on each side of the equatorial plane, a shoulder fill compound disposed between the axially outermost end of the axially widest working ply and the ply structure, formed of at least one elastomeric material, on each side of the equatorial plane, decoupling compounds disposed about the axial terminations of the belt plies and interposed between those terminations and the adjacent belt ply, the decoupling compounds having a radial thickness of at least 0.5 mm, wherein the elongation at rupture of the decoupling compounds at 100 degrees Celsius, measured per standard NF T 46-002, is at least 500 percent, and the maximum loss tangent tan delta of the decoupling compounds, measured per standard ASTM D 5992-96 at 100 degrees Celsius and 10 Hz, is no greater than 0.06.

A tyre, comprising: a crown section extending circumferentially and shaped as a ring; a set of sidewall sections positioned at opposite lateral edges of the crown section; a pair of bead regions each located radially inward of the sidewall sections; a single casing ply extending between the bead regions; several breaker plies arranged radially outward of the casing ply within the crown section; a belt reinforcement ply arranged radially outward of the breaker plies; the crown section being formed of two strata, namely an inner base strata disposed radially outward of the belt reinforcement ply and an outer cap strata disposed radially outward of the base strata and defining a road-engaging surface of the crown section, a base strata rubber mixture having a Shore hardness at 20° C. between 60 and 65, a 100% modulus at 100° C. between 2.0 MPa and 4.0 MPa, and a product of tensile strength at 100° C. (in MPa) and elongation at rupture at 100° C. (in %) of at least 2000, and a casing cord forming the casing ply being an organic fiber cord exhibiting an elongation under a 1.5 cN/dtex load on the radially inner side of the breaker plies between 5.5% and 8.5% and an elongation at break between 20% and 30%, and a product A=D×Ec of a linear density based on corrected mass D per casing cord (dtex/cord) and a cord insertion count Ec (cords per 50 mm) measured orthogonally to the cord extension direction lying between 1.8×10^5 dtex/50 mm and 3.0×10^5 dtex/50 mm.

A tyre comprising: a tread section running around the circumference of the tyre and shaped as a ring; a pair of flank sections positioned on opposite sides of the tread section; a pair of bead sections each located radially inward of a respective flank section, with a single carcass ply extending between the bead sections; several crown plies arranged radially outward of the carcass ply within the tread section; and a reinforcing band arranged radially outward of the crown plies; the tread section consisting of two strata, namely an inner sub-tread stratum positioned radially outward of the reinforcing band and an outer cap stratum positioned radially outward of the sub-tread stratum and forming the ground-engaging face of the tread section; a binder cord forming the reinforcing band being a polyethylene terephthalate filament cord whose elongation under a 2.0 cN/dtex load at 100° C. lies between 2.0% and 4.0%, a sub-tread rubber compound forming the sub-tread stratum having a Shore hardness at 20° C. between 60 and 65, a tensile modulus at 100% extension at 100° C. between 2.0 MPa and 4.0 MPa, and a product of tensile strength at 100° C. in MPa and elongation at rupture at 100° C. in percent of at least 2000; and the sub-tread rubber compound incorporating, per 100 parts by mass of elastomer, 35 to 60 parts by mass of carbon black having a CTAB specific surface area below 70 m2/g and 3 to 30 parts by mass of silica having a CTAB specific surface area below 180 m2/g.

A pneumatic vehicle wheel covering comprising: a tread section including at least one of a land strip or a land block; a slit formed within the land strip or the land block, the slit having: an upper zone facing outwardly in a radial direction; a meshing zone situated radially beneath and joined immediately to the upper zone; and a foundation zone situated radially beneath and joined immediately to the meshing zone, wherein the foundation zone narrows radially inwardly from a first breadth BW 1 to a second breadth BW 2, and wherein the meshing zone comprises a plurality of protruding meshing segments and recessed meshing segments defining a sinusoidal undulation within a plane defined by a circumferential axis C of the covering and an axial axis A of the covering.

A pneumatic vehicle covering, the covering having a tread section that includes at least one of a tread ridge or a tread knob; a lamella formed within the tread ridge or the tread knob, the lamella comprising: an upper outer section located at the top, a meshing section situated radially beneath and directly joined to the upper outer section, and a foundation section situated radially beneath and directly joined to the meshing section, wherein the meshing section features a series of protruding meshing segments and receding meshing segments arranged to define a zigzag contour within a plane defined by a peripheral direction of the covering and a radial direction of the covering.

An automotive road-engaging assembly comprising: an interior hub member configured for attachment to a motor vehicle; an exterior annular member encircling the interior hub member; and a set of pneumatic dampers linked between the interior hub member and the exterior annular member so as to permit relative displacement therebetween, each of the pneumatic dampers including a pressure vessel housing and a plunger assembly having a tubular rod and a broadened plunger head affixed thereto, the broadened plunger head being slidably displaceable within the pressure vessel housing and delimiting a first pressurized compartment and a second pressurized compartment on respectively opposite faces of the broadened plunger head, the broadened plunger head defining a passage extending therethrough that enables gas communication between the first pressurized compartment and an interior of the tubular rod.

A vehicle wheel arrangement comprising: a hub ring configured for attachment to the vehicle; a tire-supporting ring encircling the hub ring; a set of pneumatic dampers linked between the hub ring and the tire-supporting ring to permit relative displacement therebetween, each of the pneumatic dampers including a cylindrical housing, and a plunger having a tubular rod and a broadened flange affixed thereto, the broadened flange being slidably displaceable within the cylindrical housing and partitioning it into first and second chambers on opposite faces of the broadened flange, the broadened flange defining a passage therethrough enabling fluid communication between the first chamber and an interior of the tubular rod; a check element mounted on the tubular rod to throttle fluid flow through the passage; and a retaining collar secured to the tire-supporting ring and projecting radially inward to form a positive travel limit with adjacent regions of the hub ring.

A process for fabricating multiple pneumatic dampers intended for installation between an interior hub ring and an exterior hub ring of a wheel arrangement, the process comprising: attaching a widened plunger cap of a pressurized plunger to a tubular plunger rod of the pressurized plunger; disposing the pressurized plunger so as to slide within a pressure barrel body such that the widened plunger cap divides the interior of the pressure barrel body into a first pressure chamber and a second pressure chamber on opposite faces of the widened plunger cap; and machining an aperture through the widened plunger cap that allows pneumatic fluid to pass between the first pressure chamber and the tubular plunger rod.

A braking rotor arrangement comprising: a carrier secured to a shaft of a motorized land craft, and a rotor positioned on an interior side, relative to a central axis of the shaft, of the carrier and removably coupled to the carrier; wherein the rotor defines an aperture through which the shaft is intended to pass; the carrier includes outwardly extending lugs along a perimeter of the carrier and inwardly extending notches along the perimeter; the rotor includes inwardly extending tabs within the aperture and outwardly extending recesses within the aperture; when the rotor occupies a predetermined first angular orientation about the central axis relative to the carrier, the lugs and the tabs are joined while overlapping one another; and when the rotor occupies a second angular orientation about the central axis differing from the first angular orientation, the lugs are received within the recesses and the tabs are received within the notches as seen along the central axis, and the rotor is free of overlap with the carrier along the central axis.

A braking rotor arrangement comprising: a carrier secured to a shaft of a motor vehicle; and a rotor positioned radially inward, relative to an axis of the shaft, of the carrier and removably coupled to the carrier, wherein the rotor defines a polygonal aperture through which the shaft passes, the carrier exhibits a polygonal perimeter, when the rotor is oriented about the axis at a designated first angular orientation with respect to the carrier, the rotor and the carrier are joined in mutually overlapping relation, and when the rotor is oriented about the axis at a second angular orientation differing from the first angular orientation, the perimeter of the carrier lies within the aperture as seen along the axis such that the rotor does not overlap the carrier along the axis.

A bearing mounting assembly for coupling a wheel bearing arrangement to a trailer spindle, comprising: a primary collar portion configured to be affixed to the spindle; a secondary collar portion secured to the primary collar portion and configured to receive the wheel bearing arrangement; wherein the primary collar portion is fastened to the spindle and the wheel bearing arrangement is mounted onto the secondary collar portion, the wheel bearing arrangement being readily fitted to or detached from the bearing mounting assembly; and further wherein the assembly is supplied fitted to the spindle as a one-piece unit secured during fabrication, the assembly shielding the spindle from harm by interposing between the bearing and spindle, and further wherein a selection of assemblies is available to match differing spindles.

A bearing mounting assembly for attaching a wheel bearing unit to a trailer axle, the assembly comprising: a primary hub section adapted to be secured to the axle; a secondary hub section coupled to the primary hub section and configured to receive the wheel bearing unit; wherein the primary hub section is fixed to the axle, the wheel bearing unit is mountable onto the secondary hub section, and the wheel bearing unit can be readily fitted to or detached from the assembly.

A mounting arrangement for a vehicle live axle, comprising: a differential casing having a bore formed at a terminal region of the casing configured to accept an end portion of a tubular spindle housing; and a two-part annular flange of the casing, the flange bounding the bore and possessing a radially interior annulus and a radially exterior annulus; wherein the interior annulus is configured to grip the tubular spindle housing by a press-fit engagement; and wherein the two-part flange distributes loading to yield lower strain within the casing than a flange having one annulus.

A vehicle axle arrangement, comprising: a differential casing presenting a seating aperture at a terminal end thereof; a tubular axle sleeve possessing an inward end seated within the seating aperture; and a twin-annulus casing portion of the differential casing, the twin-annulus casing portion delimiting the seating aperture and possessing a radially interior annulus and a radially exterior annulus; wherein the tubular axle sleeve is lodged and retained within the radially interior annulus by a press-type friction engagement; and wherein the twin-annulus casing portion imparts diminished strain upon the differential casing in comparison with a single-annulus configuration.

A tireless vacuum-type wheel covering, comprising: a outer wear band disposed atop a ply-cord casing and positioned at a central peripheral region, with a channel recess cut into an exposed face of the wear band; a gas-impermeable barrier sheet secured between the wear band and the ply-cord casing or secured beneath the ply-cord casing, the barrier sheet including at least one textile fabric ply whose warp and weft yarns each consist of between five and thirty monofilaments, the fabric ply being rendered into the barrier sheet by rubber saturation and rubber surface coating; and the barrier sheet extending across at least a bead seat region to a shoulder region, with a terminal edge of the barrier sheet running to the bead seat region and folded back to form an upturned flap.

A vehicle pneumatic covering comprising: a crown portion spanning a mid-plane (X-X) and two lateral portions, the crown portion being bordered from a first lateral portion by a first peripheral channel and from a second lateral portion by a second peripheral channel; the crown portion exhibiting an axial extent of at least 35% of an operative breadth of the crown; the crown portion incorporating a plurality of raised strips containing respective sets of transverse channels and incisions; wherein the raised strips include at least one primary strip carrying a plurality of primary transverse channels; the primary transverse channels traversing at least 90% of the breadth of the primary strip; each primary transverse channel including a substantially rectilinear leading section tilted with respect to a direction parallel to the mid-plane (X-X) by an angle no greater than 70°, a substantially rectilinear trailing section oriented oppositely to the leading section, and an arcuate joining section extending between the leading section and the trailing section; and the crown portion further including a set of incisions comprising a plurality of primary incisions situated within the primary strip between the primary transverse channels; wherein: the primary incisions extend across at least 60% of the breadth of the primary strip; the primary incisions follow a substantially straight path forming with the mid-plane (X-X) an angle θ′ corresponding to the angle θ; and the primary incisions never cross one another.

A pneumatic tyre whose tread face is designed to engage the road surface, the tread including protruding blocks arranged into at least a first and a second pattern unit, these units being partly delimited from each other by channels and rising outward from a floor to the running face across a radial depth D of no less than 6 mm and no more than the overall tread thickness Hsre; each pattern unit (MA, MB) having a first segment situated on one side of a mid-circumferential plane (C) through the tread centre, said first segment merging without interruption into a second segment situated on the opposite side of that plane; the tread being formed by repeating, around one wheel revolution, the first pattern unit MA composed of segments MA1 and MA2 at a spacing PA, and the second pattern unit MB composed of segments MB1 and MB2 at a spacing PB, where PA is less than or equal to PB; each segment (MA1, MB1; MA2, MB2) being a solid body whose leading surfaces, meaning those whose outer corner edge meets the contact patch first as the tyre rolls over the ground, form an angle PS12 with the axial direction defined by the tyre rotation axis, PS12 lying within 0° to 60°; each segment of each pattern unit containing at least one principal slit that follows the curvature of that segment and runs roughly parallel to its boundaries, said principal slit extending uninterrupted from a first axial margin on one side of the plane (C) to a junction located within a principal cavity on the other side of the plane (C), the principal cavity reaching a second margin of the tread, and the axial breadth of the principal slit amounting to 52% to 63% of the axial breadth of the tread; wherein the junction lies at a perpendicular distance from the plane (C) between 0 and 25 mm, and wherein the angle PS12 of each leading surface of a tread segment lies within 25° to 60° at the axially inner end of the principal cavity.

A tyre tread for a commercial vehicle tyre, comprising: a peripheral orientation encircling a rotational axis, an axial orientation running in parallel with the rotational axis, and a radial orientation normal to the rotational axis; a lateral block possessing an outer crest face; a auxiliary block possessing an auxiliary crest face, wherein the auxiliary block is positioned farther from the equatorial plane than the lateral block along the axial orientation and abuts the lateral block such that a contact boundary exists where the auxiliary block and the lateral block meet, wherein the auxiliary crest face is disposed nearer to the rotational axis along the radial orientation than the outer crest face is disposed to the rotational axis along the radial orientation; and a plurality of relief slits within the lateral block that cross the contact boundary and extend into the auxiliary block, wherein the relief slits are separated from one another along the peripheral orientation such that consecutive ones of the relief slits do not meet at the contact boundary, wherein the auxiliary block adjoins the lateral block across the contact boundary between consecutive ones of the relief slits, and wherein no separation channel is formed between the lateral block and the auxiliary block.

An apparatus for controlling air pressure within a wheel of a motor vehicle, the apparatus comprising: a storage vessel holding gas at a second pressure exceeding the gas pressure inside the wheel; a pump arranged to draw gas from the wheel and deliver it into the storage vessel; and control logic arranged to obtain a requested alteration to a state of the gas within the wheel; and when the requested alteration is a rise in gas pressure within the wheel, direct gas from the storage vessel into the wheel; when the requested alteration is a drop in gas pressure within the wheel, route gas from the wheel into the storage vessel through the pump; and when the requested alteration is a lowering of gas temperature within the wheel, both feed gas from the storage vessel into the wheel and route gas from the wheel into the storage vessel.

A computer-executed procedure for adjusting the air pressure within at least one wheel of a motor vehicle, the procedure comprising, through control logic of a computing apparatus: obtaining a target alteration to at least one state of the gas held inside the wheel; and where the target alteration calls for raising the gas pressure inside the wheel, directing gas held in a storage vessel at a second pressure exceeding the wheel's gas pressure into the wheel; or where the target alteration calls for lowering the gas pressure inside the wheel, directing gas from the wheel into the storage vessel through a pump; and where the target alteration calls for lowering the gas temperature inside the wheel, directing gas from the storage vessel into the wheel and directing gas from the wheel into the storage vessel.

A process for regulating air pressure within one or more wheel-mounted tyres of a motor vehicle, the process comprising: establishing, via a controller, a pressure metric derived from one or more sensed inflation levels; and directing, by the controller and in response to the pressure metric, at least one regulating valve into an unobstructed state to draw gas from a pressurized reservoir and fill the one or more tyres.

An apparatus for regulating inflation of one or more wheel tires mounted to an automobile, comprising: a distribution block forming a passageway and structured to route pressurized gas originating from a supply reservoir; a transducer structured to detect an instantaneous gas pressure; at least one flow regulator structured to selectively govern gas delivery from the supply reservoir toward the one or more wheel tires; and a controller coupled in signal communication with the flow regulator and the transducer, the controller being structured to: derive a pressure-related metric from the instantaneous gas pressure, and direct, responsive to the pressure-related metric, the flow regulator into an unobstructed state to convey gas from the supply reservoir and thereby pressurize the one or more wheel tires.

A technique for regulating air inflation in tyres mounted to an automobile, comprising: sensing, via a transducer, an air pressure within the tyres; establishing, by a controller, that the air pressure is lower than a minimum acceptable threshold; and directing, by the controller and responsive to establishing that the air pressure is lower than the minimum acceptable threshold, a regulating valve into an unobstructed state to route gas from a compressed supply into a shared manifold and to fill the tyres.

A tamper-resistant wheel retention device comprising: a head piece presenting a conventional wrench-engaging face and a lower capture section; a shank assembly including: a helical segment for anchoring the device to a matching internally threaded seat on an automobile; a tapered post situated opposite the helical segment and terminating in a free tip, wherein the head piece hides the tapered post; a recessed channel established beneath the tapered post and possessing a diameter smaller than a foot of the tapered post, wherein the lower capture section of the head piece is plastically displaced radially inward into the recessed channel through a cold-forming operation to hold the head piece on the shank assembly; and a keyed anti-theft drive profile situated between the helical segment and the tapered post and left uncovered by the head piece for mating with a matching proprietary removal implement, wherein turning the head piece leaves the helical segment stationary, and wherein the shank assembly can be unscrewed from the matching internally threaded seat using the keyed anti-theft drive profile.

A tamper-resistant wheel retention device comprising: a head piece presenting an ornamental contact face and a lower engagement section; a shank member including: an externally screwed section for affixing the device to a matching screw-threaded seat on a motor vehicle; a neck positioned opposite the screwed section for accepting the head piece, the neck bearing a locking projection terminating in a free tip, a recess located adjacent the neck for mating with the lower engagement section of the head piece, wherein the lower engagement section is held within the recess to keep the head piece on the shank member; and a coded anti-theft actuation feature situated between the screwed section and the neck, wherein the shank member is detachable by way of the coded anti-theft actuation feature, and wherein turning the head piece while pressing on its ornamental contact face does not turn the screwed section of the shank member.

A process for manufacturing a securing device comprising: furnishing a shank member possessing a threaded section and a projecting pin extending to a terminal end away from the threaded section, wherein a recess is machined beneath the projecting pin, and wherein a tamper-resistant recessed actuation geometry is situated between the threaded section and the pin for mating with a matching protected driver implement; supplying a covering element possessing a conventional wrench-engaging face and a lower anchoring region; positioning the covering element over the shank member so as to enclose the projecting pin; and plastically deforming the covering element through cold forming so that the lower anchoring region is pressed into the recess, thereby holding the covering element on the shank member.

A technique for maneuvering a conveyance within an article handling installation, the conveyance having at least one rolling member, the technique comprising: driving the at least one rolling member along a first heading so that the conveyance advances; the at least one rolling member incorporating a central core, a peripheral band, and a flexible coupling layer situated between the central core and the peripheral band; and allowing the flexible coupling layer of the at least one rolling member to alter its configuration during rotation of the at least one rolling member, the flexible coupling layer comprising neighboring compliant members that bound an oval-shaped gap therebetween, the oval-shaped gap possessing a long dimension inclined relative to a substantially outward direction of the neighboring compliant members, and wherein each crest of curved sections of the neighboring compliant members shifts between lying nearer the peripheral band than the central core and lying nearer the central core than the peripheral band, such that torque is conveyed from the central core to the peripheral band more rapidly when the rotation of the central core follows the direction of the long dimension than when that rotation runs counter to it.

A technique for controlling a conveyance unit within an article handling installation, the conveyance unit comprising at least one roller, said technique comprising: turning the at least one roller in a forward sense so that the conveyance unit advances; the at least one roller having a core, a periphery, and a flexible linkage positioned between the core and the periphery; and damping a pressing load through the flexible linkage of the at least one roller during its rotation, the flexible linkage containing neighboring flexible members that jointly bound oval-shaped gaps, each oval-shaped gap possessing a long axis skewed relative to a substantially radial orientation of the neighboring flexible members, and wherein each crest of curved sections of the neighboring flexible members shifts between a position nearer the periphery than the core and a position nearer the core than the periphery, such that torque is conveyed from the core to the periphery more rapidly when the rotational sense of the core aligns with the long axis than when the rotational sense of the core is opposed to the long axis; and
